issues.title: [release/2.11][inductor] huggingface amp_fp16 and float16 training XLNetLMHeadModel perf regression
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug




Issue:
Perf Regression for XLNetLMHeadModel training inductor:
|  |  Pt2.10  |  Pt2.11 |Pt2.11 vs Pt 2.10|
|---|---|---|---|
|float16| 0.883  |  0.791 | 0.89 |
|amp-float16|  1.294 | 0.953  |  0.73 |

Reproducer
```
docker run -it --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --privileged --shm-size=8g intelgpu/ubuntu-24.04-lts2:2523.40 bash
curl -LsSf [地址已移除] | env UV_INSTALL_DIR="/usr/local/bin" sh

uv venv torch-2.10 --python 3.10 --clear
source torch-2.10/bin/activate
uv pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url [地址已移除]
uv pip install pip numpy pandas psutil scipy requests setuptools==79.0.0
uv pip install transformers==4.55.2
uv pip install timm==1.0.19

pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"

deactivate
uv venv torch-2.11 --python 3.10 --clear
source torch-2.11/bin/activate
uv pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url [地址已移除]
uv pip install pip numpy pandas psutil scipy requests setuptools==79.0.0
uv pip install transformers==4.55.2
uv pip install timm==1.0.19

git clone [地址已移除]
cd pytorch
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

git clone [地址已移除]
rsync -avz ./torch-xpu-ops/.ci/benchmarks/ ./benchmarks/dynamo/

python huggingface.py --training --amp --amp-dtype float16 -d xpu -n10 --performance --disable-cudagraphs --only XLNetLMHeadModel --cold-start-latency --backend=inductor
```

issues.title: SYCL compilation flag -fsycl-id-queries-fit-in-int does not work as expected for TriuTril kernel.
issues.body:
This issue is created to track unexpected behavior observed when launching sycl kernels on XPU.

## Problem description

During SYCL code build the flag `-fsycl-id-queries-fit-in-int` is the default one: [DOCUMENTATION]([地址已移除])
In the main PyTorch build system there is no such flag, so the default one is used.
It assumes that the ranges passed when launching sycl kernel fit into `uint32` limits. That supposedly allows some optimizations by not using double precision for indexing.

I created simple cpp sycl kernel to test it.
The attempt to launch sycl kernel with range exceeding max `uint32` ends up in thrown Exception.
```cpp
size_t large_range = 5000000000UL;  // > uint32 max
q.submit([&](sycl::handler& h) {
    h.parallel_for(sycl::range<1>(large_range), [=](sycl::id<1> idx) {
        auto global_id = idx[0];  // Throws exception with default flag
        // kernel work...
    });
});
```

Exception:
```text
Provided range and/or offset does not fit in int. Pass '-fno-sycl-id-queries-fit-in-int' to remove this limit.
```
On the other hand, when launching the TriuTril kernel in PyTorch ([MENTIONED KERNEL]([地址已移除])), there is no Exception, but the results are wrong.

So in normal, simple case, there is Exception thrown when range exceeds the max `uint32`. We need to disable the default flag to make it work by adding `-fno-sycl-id-queries-fit-in-int` to build.

In PyTorch Triangular kernels for XPU, there is no Exception thrown. Kernel executes, but results are wrong. The experiments showed that the wrong results are caused by `get_global_id()` function that returns the ids truncated to `uint32`.
```cpp
IndexType linear_idx = item.get_global_id(0) * elements_per_thread;
// The linear_idx is effectively:
// linear_idx = real_id % MAX_UINT32
```

## Considerations

I believe it would be good to investigate this mismatch in behavior and find the root cause. It is much better to have the Exception rather than silently truncating `uint64` values to `uint32`.
On the other hand, maybe the flag `-fno-sycl-id-queries-fit-in-int` may be added to build system to avoid the truncation in the kernel and allow ranges bigger than max `uint32`. But due to  [DOCUMENTATION]([地址已移除]) it may introduce performance issues.

The main goal of this issue is to first find why the TriangularOpsKernels doesn't throw Exceptions when range is bigger than max `uint32` value.

## Additional links

There is the discussion about it in one of the PRs: #2864

nodes.bodyText: Hi @daisyden: test cases passed in main branch, please verify.

The @skipIfXpu(msg="AssertionError: torch-xpu-ops: 2958") decorator on test_dtensor_basic_export has been removed on branch daisyden/missing_test (commit 728a822917d), based on pytorch:viable/strict.
Verification

Standalone: python test/distributed/tensor/test_dtensor_compile.py TestDTensorCompile.test_dtensor_basic_export → PASS on XPU.
Companion test test_dtensor_basic_compile (also covered by this issue's title) already had no skip and passes on XPU.

Caveat
When test_dtensor_basic_export runs after test_dtensor_basic_compile in the same process (e.g. pytest -k, or python test_dtensor_compile.py TestDTensorCompile.test_dtensor_basic_compile TestDTensorCompile.test_dtensor_basic_export), it fails an assertExpectedInline mismatch:
- L_self_buffers_buffer_ , L_self_buffers_buffer_device_mesh , L_x_ , = self._dynamo_bytecode_flatten(*_fn_args)
+ L_self_buffers_buffer_ , L_x_ , L_mesh_ , = self._dynamo_bytecode_flatten(*_fn_args)
- from_local = ... from_local(l_x_, l_self_buffers_buffer_device_mesh, [...])
+ from_local = ... from_local(l_x_, l_mesh_, [...])

This is a test-ordering/dynamo-cache pollution that is not XPU-specific — it appears to be a regression from pytorch/pytorch#178115 ([coor] fully flatten DTensorSpec in __tensor_flatten__, 2026-03-27). Should be filed as a separate upstream issue.

issues.title: [distributed] all_to_all_single Compatibility Issue on B60/XCCL
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Problem Description

On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` produces
data corruption, while `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
(ft_c version) works correctly.

## Symptoms

- sglang-diffusion in Ulysses attention mode produces completely wrong attention outputs
- Ulysses attention redistributes data between sequence and head dimensions via all_to_all
- `dist.all_to_all_single` corrupts the redistributed data, causing incorrect attention output
- End result: severely degraded or completely black generated images/videos

## Root Cause

`torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` has a bug on the XCCL backend causing incorrect
data exchange. Using `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
(PyTorch functional collectives API) bypasses this issue.

## Current walk around

Override `all_to_all_4D` in `XpuCommunicator` to use ft_c instead of dist:

```python
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c

# Original code (broken on XPU)
output = torch.empty_like(input_)
dist.all_to_all_single(output, input_, group=group)

# Fixed (ft_c workaround)
output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
    input_.flatten(),
    output_split_sizes=None,
    input_split_sizes=None,
    group=group,
)
output = output.reshape(input_shape)
```

## Affected Locations in Codebase

| File | Function | Purpose | Status |
|------|----------|---------|--------|
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py` | `AllToAll4D.forward()` | Default all_to_all_4D implementation | Uses `dist.all_to_all_single` |
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/device_communicators/xpu_communicator.py` | `all_to_all_4D()` | XPU-specific override | **Fixed** (uses ft_c) |

## Reproduction Test

```bash
# Run on XPU (4 GPUs)
export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1,2,3
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py

# Test different dtypes
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
```

Expected results (PyTorch 2.9.0+xpu, 4 GPUs):
- Test 1 (dist.all_to_all_single simple): **FAIL** (small tensor corrupted on 4 GPUs)
- Test 2 (ft_c.all_to_all_single simple): PASS
- Test 3 (dist.all_to_all_single large): PASS (large tensor works)
- Test 4 (ft_c.all_to_all_single large): PASS
- Test 5 (4D Ulysses pattern dist vs ft_c): PASS (large tensor)
- Test 6 (Sequential ft_c stability): PASS

## Reproduction Script

```python
"""
Minimal reproduction script for all_to_all_single issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` produces
corrupted data, while `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
works correctly.

This bug affects Ulysses attention in sglang-diffusion, where all_to_all_4D is used
to redistribute attention heads and sequence dimensions across devices.

Usage:
    export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1,2,3
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    if torch.xpu.is_available():
        torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank)
    else:
        torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    dist.init_process_group(
        backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size,
        device_id=torch.device(device),
    )
    return rank, world_size, device


def test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single with small verifiable data.
    Each rank sends rank*10+i to rank i.
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # Verify: output[i] should be i*10 + rank
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 2: Same test using ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround).
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single with large tensor (attention-sized).
    Each rank fills its chunk with rank+1 values, then verifies after exchange.
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64  # seq_chunk * head_dim
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    # Each rank creates [world_size] chunks, chunk[i] filled with rank+1
    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(total, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # After all_to_all, chunk[i] in output should come from rank i, so value = i+1
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single with large tensor (workaround).
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 5: Simulate the all_to_all_4D pattern from Ulysses attention.
    scatter_dim=2 (heads), gather_dim=1 (sequence).
    [B, shard_S, H, D] -> all_to_all -> [B, S, shard_H, D]

    Tests both dist.all_to_all_single and ft_c.all_to_all_single, then compares.
    """
    batch = 1
    shard_seqlen = 64
    num_heads = 8  # must be divisible by world_size
    head_dim = 64

    assert num_heads % world_size == 0, f"num_heads={num_heads} must be divisible by world_size={world_size}"
    shard_hn = num_heads // world_size

    # Create deterministic input (same seed on all ranks, but use rank-specific data)
    torch.manual_seed(42 + rank)
    input_4d = torch.randn(batch, shard_seqlen, num_heads, head_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    # ---- dist.all_to_all_single path ----
    input_t = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [H, shard_S, B, D]
    output_dist = torch.empty_like(input_t)
    dist.all_to_all_single(output_dist, input_t)
    output_dist = torch.cat(output_dist.split(shard_hn), dim=1)  # [shard_H, S, B, D]
    output_dist = output_dist.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [B, S, shard_H, D]

    # ---- ft_c.all_to_all_single path (workaround) ----
    input_t2 = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()
    input_shape = input_t2.shape
    output_ftc = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_t2.flatten(),
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )
    output_ftc = output_ftc.reshape(input_shape)
    output_ftc = torch.cat(output_ftc.split(shard_hn), dim=1)
    output_ftc = output_ftc.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()

    # Compare
    has_nan_dist = torch.isnan(output_dist).any().item()
    has_nan_ftc = torch.isnan(output_ftc).any().item()
    max_diff = (output_dist.float() - output_ftc.float()).abs().max().item()
    match = max_diff < 1e-3

    expected_shape = (batch, shard_seqlen * world_size, shard_hn, head_dim)
    shape_ok = output_dist.shape == expected_shape and output_ftc.shape == expected_shape

    return match and shape_ok and not has_nan_dist and not has_nan_ftc, {
        "output_shape": output_dist.shape,
        "expected_shape": expected_shape,
        "max_diff": max_diff,
        "has_nan_dist": has_nan_dist,
        "has_nan_ftc": has_nan_ftc,
        "match": match,
    }


def test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype, rounds=5):
    """
    Test 6: Multiple sequential all_to_all calls to check for intermittent failures.
    """
    chunk_size = 256 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size
    all_passed = True

    for i in range(rounds):
        input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

        output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
            input_tensor,
            output_split_sizes=None,
            input_split_sizes=None,
            group=dist.group.WORLD,
        )

        for j in range(world_size):
            chunk = output[j * chunk_size : (j + 1) * chunk_size]
            expected = float(j + 1)
            if abs(chunk.float().mean().item() - expected) > 1e-2:
                all_passed = False

    return all_passed


def _gather_pass_count(passed, world_size):
    """Gather pass/fail from all ranks via all_gather_object (CPU-side)."""
    result_list = [None] * world_size
    dist.all_gather_object(result_list, 1 if passed else 0)
    return sum(result_list)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test all_to_all_single on XPU/XCCL")
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    dtype_map = {"float32": torch.float32, "float16": torch.float16, "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16}
    dtype = dtype_map[args.dtype]

    rank, world_size, device = init_distributed()

    if rank == 0:
        backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
        print(f"=== all_to_all_single compatibility test ===")
        print(f"Backend: {backend}, World size: {world_size}, Dtype: {args.dtype}")
        print(f"Device: {device}")
        print()

    dist.barrier()

    results = {}

    # --- Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single ---
    p1, inp1, out1, err1 = test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc1 = _gather_pass_count(p1, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc1 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 1] dist.all_to_all_single (simple):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc1}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p1:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp1}, output={out1}, errors={err1}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_simple"] = pc1 == world_size

    # --- Test 2: ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround) ---
    p2, inp2, out2, err2 = test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc2 = _gather_pass_count(p2, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc2 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 2] ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc2}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p2:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp2}, output={out2}, errors={err2}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_simple"] = pc2 == world_size

    # --- Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single large ---
    p3, err3 = test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc3 = _gather_pass_count(p3, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc3 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 3] dist.all_to_all_single (large tensor):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc3}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p3:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err3}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_large"] = pc3 == world_size

    # --- Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single large (workaround) ---
    p4, err4 = test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc4 = _gather_pass_count(p4, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc4 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 4] ft_c.all_to_all_single (large tensor, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc4}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p4:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err4}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_large"] = pc4 == world_size

    # --- Test 5: 4D attention pattern (dist vs ft_c) ---
    p5, info5 = test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc5 = _gather_pass_count(p5, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc5 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 5] all_to_all_4D Ulysses pattern (dist vs ft_c):")
        print(f"  Output shape: {info5['output_shape']}, expected: {info5['expected_shape']}")
        print(f"  Max diff: {info5['max_diff']}, NaN(dist)={info5['has_nan_dist']}, NaN(ftc)={info5['has_nan_ftc']}")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc5}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["4d_pattern"] = pc5 == world_size

    # --- Test 6: Sequential stability ---
    p6 = test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc6 = _gather_pass_count(p6, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc6 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 6] Sequential ft_c.all_to_all_single (5 rounds):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc6}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["sequential"] = pc6 == world_size

    # --- Summary ---
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("=== Summary ===")
        labels = [
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (simple)", "dist_simple"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, WA)", "ftc_simple"),
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (large)", "dist_large"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (large, WA)", "ftc_large"),
            ("all_to_all_4D Ulysses (dist vs ft_c)", "4d_pattern"),
            ("Sequential ft_c stability", "sequential"),
        ]
        for name, key in labels:
            ok = results[key]
            print(f"  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}")

        dist_broken = not results["dist_simple"] or not results["dist_large"]
        ftc_ok = results["ftc_simple"] and results["ftc_large"] and results["sequential"]

        if dist_broken and ftc_ok:
            print("\n** dist.all_to_all_single is BROKEN on current XCCL backend. **")
            print("** Use torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single as workaround. **")
        elif not dist_broken:
            print("\nAll tests passed. dist.all_to_all_single works on this backend.")
        else:
            print("\nBoth paths have issues. Check environment.")

    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

🐛 Describe the bug
Problem Description
On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, torch.distributed.all_to_all_single produces
data corruption, while torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single
(ft_c version) works correctly.
Symptoms

sglang-diffusion in Ulysses attention mode produces completely wrong attention outputs
Ulysses attention redistributes data between sequence and head dimensions via all_to_all
dist.all_to_all_single corrupts the redistributed data, causing incorrect attention output
End result: severely degraded or completely black generated images/videos

Root Cause
torch.distributed.all_to_all_single has a bug on the XCCL backend causing incorrect
data exchange. Using torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single
(PyTorch functional collectives API) bypasses this issue.
Current walk around
Override all_to_all_4D in XpuCommunicator to use ft_c instead of dist:
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c

# Original code (broken on XPU)
output = torch.empty_like(input_)
dist.all_to_all_single(output, input_, group=group)

# Fixed (ft_c workaround)
output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
    input_.flatten(),
    output_split_sizes=None,
    input_split_sizes=None,
    group=group,
)
output = output.reshape(input_shape)
Affected Locations in Codebase



File
Function
Purpose
Status




python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py
AllToAll4D.forward()
Default all_to_all_4D implementation
Uses dist.all_to_all_single


python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/device_communicators/xpu_communicator.py
all_to_all_4D()
XPU-specific override
Fixed (uses ft_c)



Reproduction Test
# Run on XPU (4 GPUs)
export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1,2,3
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py

# Test different dtypes
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
Expected results (PyTorch 2.9.0+xpu, 4 GPUs):

Test 1 (dist.all_to_all_single simple): FAIL (small tensor corrupted on 4 GPUs)
Test 2 (ft_c.all_to_all_single simple): PASS
Test 3 (dist.all_to_all_single large): PASS (large tensor works)
Test 4 (ft_c.all_to_all_single large): PASS
Test 5 (4D Ulysses pattern dist vs ft_c): PASS (large tensor)
Test 6 (Sequential ft_c stability): PASS

Reproduction Script
"""
Minimal reproduction script for all_to_all_single issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` produces
corrupted data, while `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
works correctly.

This bug affects Ulysses attention in sglang-diffusion, where all_to_all_4D is used
to redistribute attention heads and sequence dimensions across devices.

Usage:
    export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1,2,3
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    if torch.xpu.is_available():
        torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank)
    else:
        torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    dist.init_process_group(
        backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size,
        device_id=torch.device(device),
    )
    return rank, world_size, device


def test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single with small verifiable data.
    Each rank sends rank*10+i to rank i.
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # Verify: output[i] should be i*10 + rank
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 2: Same test using ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround).
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single with large tensor (attention-sized).
    Each rank fills its chunk with rank+1 values, then verifies after exchange.
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64  # seq_chunk * head_dim
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    # Each rank creates [world_size] chunks, chunk[i] filled with rank+1
    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(total, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # After all_to_all, chunk[i] in output should come from rank i, so value = i+1
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single with large tensor (workaround).
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 5: Simulate the all_to_all_4D pattern from Ulysses attention.
    scatter_dim=2 (heads), gather_dim=1 (sequence).
    [B, shard_S, H, D] -> all_to_all -> [B, S, shard_H, D]

    Tests both dist.all_to_all_single and ft_c.all_to_all_single, then compares.
    """
    batch = 1
    shard_seqlen = 64
    num_heads = 8  # must be divisible by world_size
    head_dim = 64

    assert num_heads % world_size == 0, f"num_heads={num_heads} must be divisible by world_size={world_size}"
    shard_hn = num_heads // world_size

    # Create deterministic input (same seed on all ranks, but use rank-specific data)
    torch.manual_seed(42 + rank)
    input_4d = torch.randn(batch, shard_seqlen, num_heads, head_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    # ---- dist.all_to_all_single path ----
    input_t = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [H, shard_S, B, D]
    output_dist = torch.empty_like(input_t)
    dist.all_to_all_single(output_dist, input_t)
    output_dist = torch.cat(output_dist.split(shard_hn), dim=1)  # [shard_H, S, B, D]
    output_dist = output_dist.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [B, S, shard_H, D]

    # ---- ft_c.all_to_all_single path (workaround) ----
    input_t2 = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()
    input_shape = input_t2.shape
    output_ftc = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_t2.flatten(),
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )
    output_ftc = output_ftc.reshape(input_shape)
    output_ftc = torch.cat(output_ftc.split(shard_hn), dim=1)
    output_ftc = output_ftc.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()

    # Compare
    has_nan_dist = torch.isnan(output_dist).any().item()
    has_nan_ftc = torch.isnan(output_ftc).any().item()
    max_diff = (output_dist.float() - output_ftc.float()).abs().max().item()
    match = max_diff < 1e-3

    expected_shape = (batch, shard_seqlen * world_size, shard_hn, head_dim)
    shape_ok = output_dist.shape == expected_shape and output_ftc.shape == expected_shape

    return match and shape_ok and not has_nan_dist and not has_nan_ftc, {
        "output_shape": output_dist.shape,
        "expected_shape": expected_shape,
        "max_diff": max_diff,
        "has_nan_dist": has_nan_dist,
        "has_nan_ftc": has_nan_ftc,
        "match": match,
    }


def test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype, rounds=5):
    """
    Test 6: Multiple sequential all_to_all calls to check for intermittent failures.
    """
    chunk_size = 256 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size
    all_passed = True

    for i in range(rounds):
        input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

        output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
            input_tensor,
            output_split_sizes=None,
            input_split_sizes=None,
            group=dist.group.WORLD,
        )

        for j in range(world_size):
            chunk = output[j * chunk_size : (j + 1) * chunk_size]
            expected = float(j + 1)
            if abs(chunk.float().mean().item() - expected) > 1e-2:
                all_passed = False

    return all_passed


def _gather_pass_count(passed, world_size):
    """Gather pass/fail from all ranks via all_gather_object (CPU-side)."""
    result_list = [None] * world_size
    dist.all_gather_object(result_list, 1 if passed else 0)
    return sum(result_list)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test all_to_all_single on XPU/XCCL")
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    dtype_map = {"float32": torch.float32, "float16": torch.float16, "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16}
    dtype = dtype_map[args.dtype]

    rank, world_size, device = init_distributed()

    if rank == 0:
        backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
        print(f"=== all_to_all_single compatibility test ===")
        print(f"Backend: {backend}, World size: {world_size}, Dtype: {args.dtype}")
        print(f"Device: {device}")
        print()

    dist.barrier()

    results = {}

    # --- Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single ---
    p1, inp1, out1, err1 = test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc1 = _gather_pass_count(p1, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc1 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 1] dist.all_to_all_single (simple):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc1}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p1:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp1}, output={out1}, errors={err1}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_simple"] = pc1 == world_size

    # --- Test 2: ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround) ---
    p2, inp2, out2, err2 = test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc2 = _gather_pass_count(p2, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc2 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 2] ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc2}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p2:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp2}, output={out2}, errors={err2}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_simple"] = pc2 == world_size

    # --- Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single large ---
    p3, err3 = test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc3 = _gather_pass_count(p3, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc3 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 3] dist.all_to_all_single (large tensor):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc3}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p3:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err3}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_large"] = pc3 == world_size

    # --- Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single large (workaround) ---
    p4, err4 = test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc4 = _gather_pass_count(p4, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc4 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 4] ft_c.all_to_all_single (large tensor, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc4}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p4:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err4}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_large"] = pc4 == world_size

    # --- Test 5: 4D attention pattern (dist vs ft_c) ---
    p5, info5 = test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc5 = _gather_pass_count(p5, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc5 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 5] all_to_all_4D Ulysses pattern (dist vs ft_c):")
        print(f"  Output shape: {info5['output_shape']}, expected: {info5['expected_shape']}")
        print(f"  Max diff: {info5['max_diff']}, NaN(dist)={info5['has_nan_dist']}, NaN(ftc)={info5['has_nan_ftc']}")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc5}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["4d_pattern"] = pc5 == world_size

    # --- Test 6: Sequential stability ---
    p6 = test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc6 = _gather_pass_count(p6, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc6 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 6] Sequential ft_c.all_to_all_single (5 rounds):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc6}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["sequential"] = pc6 == world_size

    # --- Summary ---
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("=== Summary ===")
        labels = [
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (simple)", "dist_simple"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, WA)", "ftc_simple"),
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (large)", "dist_large"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (large, WA)", "ftc_large"),
            ("all_to_all_4D Ulysses (dist vs ft_c)", "4d_pattern"),
            ("Sequential ft_c stability", "sequential"),
        ]
        for name, key in labels:
            ok = results[key]
            print(f"  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}")

        dist_broken = not results["dist_simple"] or not results["dist_large"]
        ftc_ok = results["ftc_simple"] and results["ftc_large"] and results["sequential"]

        if dist_broken and ftc_ok:
            print("\n** dist.all_to_all_single is BROKEN on current XCCL backend. **")
            print("** Use torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single as workaround. **")
        elif not dist_broken:
            print("\nAll tests passed. dist.all_to_all_single works on this backend.")
        else:
            print("\nBoth paths have issues. Check environment.")

    dist.destroy_process_group()

issues.title: [distributed] batch_isend_irecv Compatibility Issue on B60/XCCL
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Problem Description

On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))`
causes silent data corruption on the receive side (all-zeros or garbage data), while
individual `dist.irecv` / `dist.isend` calls work correctly.

## Symptoms

- sglang-diffusion in USP mode (tp=1, ulysses=4) generates completely black videos
- TP mode (tp=4, ulysses=1) works normally
- Denoising stage latent data is correct; the issue appears in VAE parallel decoding
- VAE parallel decoding uses height-dimension sharding + halo exchange; halo exchange is called in every convolution layer
- `batch_isend_irecv` causes halo data transfer failure, convolution output errors, and ultimately all-black VAE output

## Root Cause

The `halo_exchange` function was changed from individual `irecv/isend` to
`batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))` after commit `574aa8c1f`. This API does not work
correctly on the XCCL backend.

## Current walk around

In `wan_dist_utils.py`'s `halo_exchange`, check the platform via `current_platform.is_xpu()`:
use individual `irecv/isend` on XPU, and `batch_isend_irecv` on other platforms.

## Affected Locations in Codebase

| File | Function | Purpose | Status |
|------|----------|---------|--------|
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vaes/parallel/wan_dist_utils.py` | `halo_exchange()` | Wan VAE parallel decoding halo exchange | **Fixed** |
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/group_coordinator.py` | `PipelineGroupCoordinator._communicate_shapes()` | Pipeline Parallel inter-stage shape communication | To be fixed (triggered when pp>1) |
| `python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_updater.py` | expert rebalance P2P | LLM-side MoE expert load balancing | Non-diffusion path |

## Reproduction Test

```bash
# Run on XPU (4 GPUs)
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py

# Or use mpirun
mpirun -np 4 python test_batch_isend_irecv.py

# Test different dtypes
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py --dtype bfloat16
```

Expected results:
- Test 1 (individual basic): PASS
- Test 2 (batch basic): FAIL (on XPU/XCCL)
- Test 3 (halo individual): PASS
- Test 4 (halo batch): FAIL (on XPU/XCCL)

## Environment

- Container image: intel/llm-scaler-omni:0.1.0-b6
- PyTorch: 2.9.0+xpu
- oneAPI: 2025.1
- oneCCL: 2021.15.6
- Platform: Intel Arc Pro B60 × 4
- Distributed backend: XCCL (PyTorch XPU distributed)
- CCL environment variables:
  - `CCL_SYCL_ALLTOALL_ARC_LL=1`
  - `CCL_SYCL_CCL_BARRIER=1`
- Model: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers (reproduced in USP mode)
- sglang-diffusion branch: xpu_0122

## Reproduce Script
```python
"""
Minimal reproduction script for batch_isend_irecv compatibility issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))` silently
produces corrupted data (zeros or garbage), while individual `dist.irecv/dist.isend`
calls work correctly.

Usage:
    mpirun -np 4 python test_batch_isend_irecv.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py
"""

import os
import argparse

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        # torchrun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        # mpirun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    dist.init_process_group(backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size)
    torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank) if torch.xpu.is_available() else torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    return rank, world_size, device


def test_individual_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using individual dist.irecv / dist.isend calls."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    reqs = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=prev_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=next_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=next_rank))

    for req in reqs:
        req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify: rank 0 should receive from rank 1, middle ranks from both neighbors, last rank from prev
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)  # value from next rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)  # value from prev rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_batch_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    p2p_ops = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, prev_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, next_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, next_rank))

    if p2p_ops:
        reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_halo_exchange_pattern(rank, world_size, device, use_batch, dtype=torch.float32):
    """
    Simulate the halo exchange pattern used in WanVAE parallel decode.
    Each rank owns a local slice of a height-sharded tensor and exchanges
    top/bottom halo rows with neighbors.
    """
    local_h, w = 8, 16
    # Fill with rank-specific values so correctness is verifiable
    x = torch.full((1, 4, local_h, w), float(rank + 1) * 10, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    # Make top/bottom rows distinctive
    x[..., 0, :] = float(rank + 1) * 100  # top row
    x[..., -1, :] = float(rank + 1) * 200  # bottom row

    halo_size = 1
    top_row = x[..., :halo_size, :].contiguous()
    bottom_row = x[..., -halo_size:, :].contiguous()
    recv_top = torch.zeros_like(top_row)
    recv_bottom = torch.zeros_like(bottom_row)

    if use_batch:
        p2p_ops = []
        if rank > 0:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_top, rank - 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, top_row, rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, bottom_row, rank + 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_bottom, rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        if p2p_ops:
            reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
            for req in reqs:
                req.wait()
    else:
        reqs = []
        if rank > 0:
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_top, src=rank - 1))
            reqs.append(dist.isend(top_row, dst=rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            reqs.append(dist.isend(bottom_row, dst=rank + 1))
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_bottom, src=rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify recv_top: should be bottom_row of (rank-1), i.e. rank * 200
    # Verify recv_bottom: should be top_row of (rank+1), i.e. (rank+2) * 100
    passed = True
    details = []

    if rank > 0:
        expected_top = float(rank) * 200  # bottom_row value of prev rank
        actual_top = recv_top.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_top - expected_top) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_top: expected={expected_top}, actual={actual_top}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_top: zeroed (rank 0)")

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_bottom = float(rank + 2) * 100  # top_row value of next rank
        actual_bottom = recv_bottom.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_bottom - expected_bottom) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_bottom: expected={expected_bottom}, actual={actual_bottom}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_bottom: zeroed (last rank)")

    return passed, details


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test batch_isend_irecv on XPU/XCCL")
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
    args = parser.parse_args()
```

🐛 Describe the bug
Problem Description
On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, torch.distributed.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))
causes silent data corruption on the receive side (all-zeros or garbage data), while
individual dist.irecv / dist.isend calls work correctly.
Symptoms

sglang-diffusion in USP mode (tp=1, ulysses=4) generates completely black videos
TP mode (tp=4, ulysses=1) works normally
Denoising stage latent data is correct; the issue appears in VAE parallel decoding
VAE parallel decoding uses height-dimension sharding + halo exchange; halo exchange is called in every convolution layer
batch_isend_irecv causes halo data transfer failure, convolution output errors, and ultimately all-black VAE output

Root Cause
The halo_exchange function was changed from individual irecv/isend to
batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...)) after commit 574aa8c1f. This API does not work
correctly on the XCCL backend.
Current walk around
In wan_dist_utils.py's halo_exchange, check the platform via current_platform.is_xpu():
use individual irecv/isend on XPU, and batch_isend_irecv on other platforms.

halo_exchange()
Wan VAE parallel decoding halo exchange

Reproduce Script
"""
Minimal reproduction script for batch_isend_irecv compatibility issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))` silently
produces corrupted data (zeros or garbage), while individual `dist.irecv/dist.isend`
calls work correctly.

Usage:
    mpirun -np 4 python test_batch_isend_irecv.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py
"""

import os
import argparse

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        # torchrun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        # mpirun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    dist.init_process_group(backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size)
    torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank) if torch.xpu.is_available() else torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    return rank, world_size, device


def test_individual_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using individual dist.irecv / dist.isend calls."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    reqs = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=prev_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=next_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=next_rank))

    for req in reqs:
        req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify: rank 0 should receive from rank 1, middle ranks from both neighbors, last rank from prev
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)  # value from next rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)  # value from prev rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_batch_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    p2p_ops = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, prev_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, next_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, next_rank))

    if p2p_ops:
        reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_halo_exchange_pattern(rank, world_size, device, use_batch, dtype=torch.float32):
    """
    Simulate the halo exchange pattern used in WanVAE parallel decode.
    Each rank owns a local slice of a height-sharded tensor and exchanges
    top/bottom halo rows with neighbors.
    """
    local_h, w = 8, 16
    # Fill with rank-specific values so correctness is verifiable
    x = torch.full((1, 4, local_h, w), float(rank + 1) * 10, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    # Make top/bottom rows distinctive
    x[..., 0, :] = float(rank + 1) * 100  # top row
    x[..., -1, :] = float(rank + 1) * 200  # bottom row

    halo_size = 1
    top_row = x[..., :halo_size, :].contiguous()
    bottom_row = x[..., -halo_size:, :].contiguous()
    recv_top = torch.zeros_like(top_row)
    recv_bottom = torch.zeros_like(bottom_row)

    if use_batch:
        p2p_ops = []
        if rank > 0:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_top, rank - 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, top_row, rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, bottom_row, rank + 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_bottom, rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        if p2p_ops:
            reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
            for req in reqs:
                req.wait()
    else:
        reqs = []
        if rank > 0:
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_top, src=rank - 1))
            reqs.append(dist.isend(top_row, dst=rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            reqs.append(dist.isend(bottom_row, dst=rank + 1))
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_bottom, src=rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify recv_top: should be bottom_row of (rank-1), i.e. rank * 200
    # Verify recv_bottom: should be top_row of (rank+1), i.e. (rank+2) * 100
    passed = True
    details = []

    if rank > 0:
        expected_top = float(rank) * 200  # bottom_row value of prev rank
        actual_top = recv_top.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_top - expected_top) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_top: expected={expected_top}, actual={actual_top}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_top: zeroed (rank 0)")

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_bottom = float(rank + 2) * 100  # top_row value of next rank
        actual_bottom = recv_bottom.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_bottom - expected_bottom) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_bottom: expected={expected_bottom}, actual={actual_bottom}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_bottom: zeroed (last rank)")

    return passed, details


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test batch_isend_irecv on XPU/XCCL")
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    dtype_map = {"float32": torch.float32, "float16": torch.float16, "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16}
    dtype = dtype_map[args.dtype]

    rank, world_size, device = init_distributed()

    if rank == 0:
        backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
        print(f"=== batch_isend_irecv compatibility test ===")
        print(f"Backend: {backend}, World size: {world_size}, Dtype: {args.dtype}")
        print(f"Device: {device}")
        print()

    dist.barrier()

nodes.bodyText:
This is not a functionality issue of distributed because the failure is cause by different default behavior of xpu test suite. The TestCase class will initialize cuda context with a default device 0 before test runs. However, in xpu's case, device is not set until later in the test being initialized based on rank, so for these ForwardInputs tests the expected device is different.
I noticed in the TestCase class there are lots of cuda specifc code which might cause such tiny differences. Are there any ongoing efforts checking or adapting this class?
No, we do not have ongoing efforts in TestCase for distributed. How about change this line [地址已移除] to device = torch.device(device_type.type, torch.accelerator.current_device_index()) ?
Proposed pytorch/pytorch#181307 with some minimal change to the test (initializes device at the start). This also fixes the failure.

Triton failes when bsr_softmax is processing sparse matrices with rows longer than 131,072 elements, the operation crashes at runtime with ZE_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_KERNEL_NAME.
When n <= 131072, TILE == MAX_ROW_NNZ so range(TILE, MAX_ROW_NNZ, TILE) is always empty.
When n > 131072 (= 2**17), TILE = 131072 < MAX_ROW_NNZ, the loops have ≥1 iterations, and the XPU Triton backend fails

I’ve seen this fail as:

ZE_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_KERNEL_NAME
Module doesn't contain any kernels
ZE_RESULT_ERROR_MODULE_BUILD_FAILURE

The failure is tied to long-row XPU case when max_row_nnz > 2**17. Besides the final long-row UT case is effectively batched. In test_triton_bsr_softmax from the previous loop, so the failing shape is (2, 2, 1, 150000) (not only (1, 150000)).
I will add this information to the open issue in Triton intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#6872.

Hi @CuiYifeng
Summary of the issue:
_bsr_softmax_kernel's TILE is hardcoded to 2**17, which works on CUDA but overflows XPU's HW PTSS limit via register spilling (confirmed by Intel's Triton team intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#6872). The kernel's existing tiling loop already handles TILE < MAX_ROW_NNZ correctly, so a smaller XPU tile is a safe fix, but we want to align on the right shape for it before submitting.
Three design questions:

Should max_tile become an explicit per-backend constant, rather than a single hardcoded 2**17?
Is a fixed 2**14 the right XPU value, or should we tune TILE and num_warps together?
Per dev-tomek's analysis, increasing num_warps also reduces per-thread register pressure.
Should the misleading "Triton's max numel is bounded by 2 ** 17" comments (in the kernel and in the corresponding torch-xpu-ops test) be corrected to say "CUDA" explicitly?
We already found this phrasing caused us to assume 2**17 was a backend-independent Triton constant, when it's actually a CUDA-tuned value.

Since the fix lives in pytorch/pytorch rather than torch-xpu-ops repo, we'd like your input on the design before we submit a PR.

@jafraustro For the three design questions:

"Should max_tile become an explicit per-backend constant, rather than a single hardcoded 2**17" [Yes, that's a good idea.]
"Is a fixed 2**14 the right XPU value, or should we tune TILE and num_warps together?" [Could you explain the reason for using 2**14 on XPU? Personally, since the current issue is functionality, I recommend a simple value with a reasonable explanation.]
"Should the misleading "Triton's max numel is bounded by 2 ** 17" comments (in the kernel and in the corresponding torch-xpu-ops test) be corrected to say "CUDA" explicitly?" [Yes, agree.]

issues.title: [Win][Build] There is Cyclic dependencies error when build with BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS=true
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When build PyTorch on windows, there two modes: BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS or not.
In release build case, BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS is false. It's passed in building on windows.
But when set BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS=true or CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE is "Debug", the build mode BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS will lead to error:
```
CMake Error: The inter-target dependency graph contains the following strongly connected component (cycle):
    "torch_xpu" of type SHARED_LIBRARY
      depends on "torch_xpu_ops" (weak)
    "torch_xpu_ops" of type STATIC_LIBRARY
      depends on "torch_xpu" (weak)
  At least one of these targets is not a STATIC_LIBRARY.  Cyclic dependencies are allowed only among static libraries.
  CMake Generate step failed.  Build files cannot be regenerated correctly.
```

Reproduce:
Apply following diff in torch_xpu_ops, and build again.
```
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index 8f6fa8d6..033a47d5 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -96,6 +96,7 @@ endif()

 # Only for debugging. Save building time by shrinking translation unit scope.
 set(BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS $ENV{BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS})
+set(BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS TRUE)
 if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE MATCHES "(Debug|RelWithDebInfo)")
   set(BUILD_SEPARATE_OPS TRUE)
 endif()
```

issues.title: torch xpu event has ~0.1ms latency, which is too large
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`use_profiler = True` on b580 get 0.0009ms, `use_profiler = False` on b580 get 0.13ms, xpu overhead is ~120us
`use_profiler = True` on 4080s get 0.0013ms, `use_profiler = False` on b580 get 0.007ms,  cuda overhead is ~6us
```python
import torch
import time
import os
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load

my_neg = torch.neg_

tensor_shape_to_flush_cache = (64, 1024, 1024)
device = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator().type

activities = []
use_profiler = False
if torch.xpu.is_available():
    activities.append(ProfilerActivity.XPU)
else:
    activities.append(ProfilerActivity.CUDA)

def warm_up_l2_cache(x, flag = False):
    if not flag:
        return
    for _ in range(10):
        x.add_(1.)
        x.add_(-1.)
    x.sum()

def generate_shapes():
    shapes = []
    for mb in range(1, 200):
        shapes.append([mb * 1024 * 256])
        return shapes


def collect_perf(byte_size, cold_boot):
    warm_up_l2_cache_flag = not cold_boot
    wall_time_sum = 0

    getattr(torch, device).empty_cache()

    x = torch.randn(byte_size, dtype=torch.float16, device=device)
    for i in range(10):
        warm_up_l2_cache(x, warm_up_l2_cache_flag)
        my_neg(x)
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()

    if use_profiler:
        with profile(activities=activities) as prof:
            for i in range(100):
                warm_up_l2_cache(x, warm_up_l2_cache_flag)
                my_neg(x)
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
        kernel_filter = filter(lambda x: "Neg" in x.name or "neg" in x.name, prof.events())
        kernels = list(kernel_filter)
        assert len(kernels) == 100
        for i in range(100):
            assert kernels[i].count == 1
            wall_time_sum += kernels[i].device_time # in us
        return wall_time_sum / 1000


    start = [getattr(torch, device).Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(100)]
    end = [getattr(torch, device).Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(100)]

    for i in range(100):
        warm_up_l2_cache(x, warm_up_l2_cache_flag)
        start[i].record()

        my_neg(x)
        end[i].record()
    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
    #time.sleep(10)
    for i in range(100):
        wall_time_sum += start[i].elapsed_time(end[i])
    return wall_time_sum


for shape in generate_shapes():
    sum_time_reuse_cache = collect_perf(shape, False)
    size = shape[0] * 2 * 2 / 1024/ 1024
    print((sum_time_reuse_cache/100), "ms")
```

### Versions

main

nodes.bodyText: Should be oneAPI related. JIRA at CMPLRLLVM-76467

Impact:
PyTorch team: For PyTorch itself, this only affects torch.Event, so no big impact for PyTorch side.
Customers: for vLLM team, because they rely on torch.Event, so this has more impact for them.
Update:
oneAPI team is WIP on this. Please see the JIRA for update (CMPLRLLVM-76467). No target for oneAPI JIRA for now, so we label it to pytorch 2.15 as pytorch-side track

Update:
The compiler will refine this in 2026.2

The fix is in intel/llvm#22810
For the oneAPI perspective, starting from internal build 20260806_160000 , and will be public available in 2026.2 , thus we mark the PyTorch 2.15 target still reasonable. So leave this open until from the pytorch side, we upgrade the oneAPI and solve it.

nodes.bodyText: I'll look into it.

After analyzing the issue and adding an initial implementation in XPU and PyTorch, it turned out that fixing this autograd test requires adding a sleep method in XPU and some adjustments in the stream scheduling/synchronization logic. Since the first of these already has its own task assigned (#1986), we need to hold off on fixing this test util the mentioned task is completed.

Sleep dependency (#1986) is resolved.
torch.xpu._sleep is implemented end-to-end (at::xpu::sleep → torch._C._xpu_sleep → torch.xpu._sleep) and verified working on Arc B580 with the current oneAPI 2026.x driver (the required ext_oneapi_clock_sub_group aspect and compiler version are both available). So the sleep primitive is no longer a blocker.
PyTorch-side change: pytorch/pytorch#193379 (should be merged first)
The autograd test helper _sleep_if_cuda was CUDA-only (a no-op on XPU), so the stream-sync tests never actually induced the race on XPU. I generalized it to _sleep_if_supported (dispatches to torch.get_device_module(acc)._sleep when available) and un-gated the test from @onlyCUDA. With this, the correctness stream-sync tests now genuinely exercise the sleep and pass on XPU (..._case_2_correctness_xpu, test_warn_on_accumulate_grad_stream_mismatch_flag_xpu); the case_3/case_4 tests are skipped for lack of a 2nd GPU.
Why test_side_stream_backward_overlap still fails / must be skipped: #4955 (should be merged after PyTorch PR above)
This test detects overlap by recording torch.Event(enable_timing=True) events inside both backward branches.
I confirmed with a set of minimal experiments that:

independent XPU streams do run kernels concurrently (two parallel sleeps ≈ 1× wall time), and
the autograd engine correctly places the two backward nodes on distinct streams,

but XPU enable_timing events are implemented via sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::submit_profiling_tag(), which acts as a device-wide serialization point across queues. Measured directly: the same two-stream sleep workload runs concurrently with no events or with non-timing events (~704 ms), but serializes (~1405 ms) as soon as enable_timing events are recorded.
In other words, the act of measuring the overlap destroys it on XPU. This is an oneAPI runtime limitation (consistent with the dependency component: oneAPI label), not a PyTorch autograd bug. It is tracked in #4951, which should unskip this test and confirm it passes once the runtime side is fixed.

issues.title: [RFC] Migrate XPU kernel math functions from std::/:: to sycl::/sycl::native:: namespace
issues.body:
## Summary

XPU SYCL kernels in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/` currently use `std::`, `::`, or bare C math functions (e.g. `std::exp`, `::expf`, `sqrtf`) instead of the SYCL-native `sycl::` or `sycl::native::` namespace equivalents. This should be unified to use `sycl::` namespace functions for correctness, portability, and potential performance benefits on Intel GPU hardware.

### Mapping convention (mirroring CUDA → SYCL)

| Current (std/bare) | SYCL replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `std::exp`, `::expf`, `expf` | `sycl::exp` | |
| `std::log`, `::logf`, `logf` | `sycl::log` | |
| `std::sqrt`, `sqrtf` | `sycl::sqrt` | |
| `std::abs`, `std::fabs`, `::abs` | `sycl::fabs` (float/double), `sycl::abs` (int) | complex → keep `std::abs` |
| `std::pow` | `sycl::pow` | |
| `std::ceil`, `ceilf` | `sycl::ceil` | |
| `std::floor`, `floorf` | `sycl::floor` | |
| `std::tanh`, `::tanhf` | `sycl::tanh` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::fmod` | `sycl::fmod` | |
| `std::lgamma` | `sycl::lgamma` | |
| `std::log10` | `sycl::log10` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::log1p`, `::log1p` | `sycl::log1p` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::log2` | `sycl::log2` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::isinf` | `sycl::isinf` | device code only |
| `std::isnan` | `sycl::isnan` | device code only |
| `std::isfinite` | `sycl::isfinite` | device code only |
| `std::copysign` | `sycl::copysign` | |
| `std::erf` | `sycl::erf` | |
| `std::erfc` | `sycl::erfc` | |
| `std::exp2` | `sycl::exp2` | |
| `std::expm1` | `sycl::expm1` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::frexp` | `sycl::frexp` | |
| `std::sin` | `sycl::sin` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::cos` | `sycl::cos` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::tan` | `sycl::tan` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::asin` | `sycl::asin` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::acos` | `sycl::acos` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::atan` | `sycl::atan` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::sinh` | `sycl::sinh` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::cosh` | `sycl::cosh` | complex → keep `std::` |
| `std::asinh` | `sycl::asinh` | |
| `std::acosh` | `sycl::acosh` | |
| `std::atanh` | `sycl::atanh` | |
| `std::trunc`, `std::truncf` | `sycl::trunc` | complex component calls → keep `std::` |
| `std::nearbyintf` | `sycl::rint` (closest SYCL equivalent) | needs accuracy verification |
| `std::rsqrt` | `sycl::rsqrt` | |

### Important notes

- **Complex types:** `sycl::` math functions do NOT support `c10::complex`/`std::complex` types. When an operator is dispatched for both real and complex types, the `std::` call must be preserved for complex and only changed to `sycl::` for real types.
- **Host code:** `std::` calls in host code (outside kernels/functors) should remain as-is.
- **`STD_FUNCTOR` macro:** `ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp` defines a `STD_FUNCTOR` macro (line 181) that generates `std::OP_NAME(t)` inside device functors. Many functions are affected by this single macro. Migrating these requires either specializing the macro or replacing it with explicit functor definitions that dispatch between `sycl::` and `std::` based on type.

### SYCL math function reference
[地址已移除]

---

## Task List

Each task = one function → one PR with code change + accuracy test + performance test.
PR must be merged before checking the box.

### Infrastructure

- [x] **0. `XPUMathCompat.h` internal updates**
  - Migrate: `::expf` → `sycl::exp`, `::tanhf` → `sycl::tanh`, etc.
  - Add missing compat functions to match `CUDAMathCompat.h`: abs, ceil, copysign, floor, log, log1p, max, min, pow, sincos, sqrt, tan, normcdf

- [ ] **0b. `NumericUtils.h` — add XPU fast math branches (PyTorch main repo)**
  - `aten/src/ATen/NumericUtils.h` defines `at::exp`, `at::log`, `at::log1p`, `at::tan` template functions
  - On CUDA/HIP these use fast math intrinsics (`__expf`, `__logf`, `__log1pf`, `__tanf`)
  - On XPU (non-CUDA/HIP), they currently fall back to `::exp`, `::log`, etc. (C libm)
  - Should add `#elif defined(__SYCL_DEVICE_ONLY__)` branches using `sycl::native::exp`, `sycl::native::log`, etc. to match CUDA behavior
  - Note: XPU kernels currently do NOT call `at::exp` etc. (0 occurrences in torch-xpu-ops/src/), but aligning for correctness and future use
  - ⚠️ This is a PyTorch main repo change — needs separate PR to pytorch/pytorch

### Math functions (alphabetical)

- [x] **1. `abs` / `fabs`** — `std::abs`, `std::fabs`, `::abs` → `sycl::fabs` (float/double), `sycl::abs` (int)
  - ~65 occurrences across 17+ files
  - Files: ActivationLogSigmoidKernels.cpp, BinaryMiscOpsKernels.cpp, DeformConv2dKernels.cpp, DistanceKernels.cpp, Embedding.cpp, ForeachReduceKernels.cpp, GcdLcmKernels.cpp, LaguerrePolynomialLKernel.cpp, LegendrePolynomialPKernel.cpp, LogAddExpKernels.cpp, ReflectionPadKernels.cpp, UpSampleBilinear2dKernels.cpp, MathExtensions.h
  - ⚠️ Keep `std::abs` for complex types in: AbsKernel.cpp, ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp, UnarySignKernels.cpp, SharedReduceOps.h

- [x] **2. `acos`** — `std::acos` → `sycl::acos`
  - UnaryGeometricAcosKernel.cpp (1 call)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:246 via STD_FUNCTOR macro
  - ⚠️ ForeachUnaryKernels also dispatched for complex types → keep `std::` for complex

- [x] **3. `acosh`** — `std::acosh` → `sycl::acosh`
  - UnaryGeometricAcoshKernel.cpp (1 call)

- [x] **4. `asin`** — `std::asin` → `sycl::asin`
  - UnaryGeometricAsinKernel.cpp (2 calls: AsinComplexFunctor, AsinFunctor)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:247 via STD_FUNCTOR macro
  - ⚠️ ForeachUnaryKernels also dispatched for complex types → keep `std::` for complex

- [x] **5. `asinh`** — `std::asinh` → `sycl::asinh`
  - UnaryGeometricAsinhKernel.cpp (2 calls: AsinhComplexFunctor, AsinhFunctor)

- [x] **6. `atan`** — `std::atan` → `sycl::atan`
  - UnaryGeometricAtanKernel.cpp (2 calls: AtanComplexFunctor, AtanFunctor)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:248 via STD_FUNCTOR macro
  - ⚠️ ForeachUnaryKernels also dispatched for complex types → keep `std::` for complex

- [x] **7. `atanh`** — `std::atanh` → `sycl::atanh`
  - UnaryGeometricAtanhKernel.cpp (2 calls: AtanhComplexFunctor, AtanhFunctor)

- [x] **8. `ceil`** — `std::ceil`, bare `ceilf` → `sycl::ceil`
  - UpSampleBilinear2dKernels.cpp: 8 occurrences (4 device + 4 host)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:195 via STD_FUNCTOR macro
  - ⚠️ Keep host-code `ceilf` as-is

- [x] **9. `copysign`** — `std::copysign` → `sycl::copysign`
  - CopysignKernel.cpp

- [x] **10. `cos`** — `std::cos` → `sycl::cos`
  - UnaryGeometricCosKernel.cpp (1 call)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:252 via STD_FUNCTOR macro
  - Also used in Expm1Functor<c10::complex> in UnaryKernels.cpp
  - ⚠️ ForeachUnaryKernels also dispatched for complex types → keep `std::` for complex

- [x] **11. `cosh`** — `std::cosh` → `sycl::cosh`
  - UnaryGeometricCoshKernel.cpp (2 calls: CoshComplexFunctor, CoshFunctor)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:249 via STD_FUNCTOR macro
  - ⚠️ ForeachUnaryKernels also dispatched for complex types → keep `std::` for complex

- [x] **12. `erf`** — `std::erf` → `sycl::erf`
  - UnarySpecialOpsKernels.cpp (2 calls: ErfFunctor for float + double)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:189 via STD_FUNCTOR macro (float types only)

  - UnarySpecialOpsKernels.cpp (2 calls: ErfcFunctor for float + double)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:190 via STD_FUNCTOR macro (float types only)

- [x] **14. `exp`** — `std::exp`, `::expf`, bare `expf` → `sycl::exp`
  - UnaryKernels.cpp (ExpFunctor), UnarySpecialOpsKernels.cpp (SigmoidFunctor, Exp2Functor<complex>, Logit*, EntrFunctor)
  - ActivationEluKernels.cpp, ActivationGeluKernel.cpp, ActivationMishKernels.cpp, ActivationSiluKernels.cpp, ActivationSoftplusKernels.cpp, ActivationLogSigmoidKernels.cpp
  - BatchNormKernels.cpp, DistributionTemplates.h, FusedAdamUtils.h, LossCTCKernels.cpp, LossKernels.cpp, SoftMaxKernels.cpp, RNNKernels.cpp
  - Philox4x32.h (bare `expf`, 4 occurrences)
  - ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp:319 via STD_FUNCTOR macro

Complex types: sycl:: math functions do NOT support c10::complex/std::complex types. When an operator is dispatched for both real and complex types, the std:: call must be preserved for complex and only changed to sycl:: for real types.
Host code: std:: calls in host code (outside kernels/functors) should remain as-is.
STD_FUNCTOR macro: ForeachUnaryKernels.cpp defines a STD_FUNCTOR macro (line 181) that generates std::OP_NAME(t) inside device functors. Many functions are affected by this single macro. Migrating these requires either specializing the macro or replacing it with explicit functor definitions that dispatch between sycl:: and std:: based on type.

SYCL math function reference

aten/src/ATen/NumericUtils.h defines at::exp, at::log, at::log1p, at::tan template functions
On CUDA/HIP these use fast math intrinsics (__expf, __logf, __log1pf, __tanf)
On XPU (non-CUDA/HIP), they currently fall back to ::exp, ::log, etc. (C libm)
Should add #elif defined(__SYCL_DEVICE_ONLY__) branches using sycl::native::exp, sycl::native::log, etc. to match CUDA behavior
Note: XPU kernels currently do NOT call at::exp etc. (0 occurrences in torch-xpu-ops/src/), but aligning for correctness and future use
⚠️ This is a PyTorch main repo change — needs separate PR to pytorch/pytorch

[地址已移除]

[地址已移除]
Newest CI that has this error:
[地址已移除]
To locally reproduce error I run test in loop:
for i in {0..20}; do python -m pytest test_ops_gradients_xpu.py -k test_fn_gradgrad_grid_sampler_2d_xpu_float64; done
After few iterations I got the same error that is reported and randomly occur on CI.

Hi @jmamzax,
I had similar problem and issue regarding not reentrant backward. In my case the operator was not-deterministic because it was using atomic operations, so due to floating point operations being not associative, every run the result can be slightly different. It just looks like on XPU the differences are a little bigger then already set 1e-15.
Here is my PR that fixed similar problem: pytorch/pytorch#178589
Maybe you already found the solution, but if not feel free to contact me if you want to discuss this issue 😄

Prepared tolerance change commit: BBBela/pytorch@9302d50
The operator grid_sampler_2d is marked as not deterministic on XPU device:

  
    
      torch-xpu-ops/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/GridSampler.cpp
    
    
         Line 808
      in
      745e2d3
    
  
  
    

        
          
           globalContext().alertNotDeterministic("grid_sampler_2d_backward_xpu"); 
        
    
  


It uses internally atomic operations which can cause small results' differences between runs even for identical inputs. That is caused by floating point operations being not associative, so different order of accumulating the same values can give slightly different results.
That is why this PR increases gradcheck_nondet_tol for grid_sampler_2d from 1e-15 to 1e-14, which is still a very strict tolerance, but allows small drifts related to not deterministic accumulation order.
Many operators marked as not deterministic already sets the gradcheck_nondet_tol to GRADCHECK_NONDET_TOL which is equal to 1e-12.
Adding wait_upstream label to create batched PR to PyTorch when several similar changes are needed.
CC: @Silv3S
This issue would be fixed by pytorch/pytorch#186089
