Longer term: since #189653 will surface many more _xpu-suffixed test names that were never exercised by CPU-only skip-list generation, re-running scripts/compile_tests/update_failures.py on an XPU-enabled worker (or auditing test/compiled_autograd_skips/ for missing device-suffixed siblings of already-skipped tests) would help catch the rest of this class of gap before it lands.

Branch: agent/fix-issue-4381 (ded2195678..afdd51dc93) in agent_space_xpu/pytorch.
What the bug was
Compiled autograd captures the backward graph against allocate_dummy() placeholders (torch.zeros([0, 123456789])), which are always defined. So the C++ accumulation loop evaluates call_accumulate's undefined-tensor guards against dummies at capture time, and any InputBuffer slot fed by ≥2 edges gets an unconditional raw torch.add(old, new) baked into the FX graph. At runtime a node can legitimately return an undefined gradient on such an edge — ConvolutionBackwardBackward0 does, for both grad-wrt-input and grad-wrt-weight, when the batch dim is zero — which arrives as None, and torch.add(None, tensor) raises. Eager never hits this: InputBuffer::add skips undefined incoming vars and moves rather than adds into an undefined slot.
The fix (3 files, target repo is pytorch, not torch-xpu-ops)
New call_accumulate in torch/_dynamo/external_utils.py mirroring InputBuffer::add, and AutogradCompilerInstance.accumulate proxies it instead of torch.add. Fixing at capture time is impossible — definedness isn't knowable until the graph runs. I did not take the issue's own suggested route of adding a test/compiled_autograd_skips/ marker; that hides the defect. A fresh-context skip-guard review of the staged diff returned APPROVE.
Verification
Pure-Python change, so no rebuild — and the wheel's copies of both edited files were byte-identical to the base commit, so patching them in place was faithful.

issues.title: [XPU] Expose occupancy properties required by Inductor dynamic RBLOCK scaling
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Summary

Inductor’s dynamic RBLOCK scaling relies on device occupancy properties to decide whether to generate reduced `R_BLOCK` candidates for reduction kernels.

The relevant implementation is in torch/_inductor/runtime/hints.py, where `DeviceProperties.create()` copies properties from the backend device interface into the backend-independent `DeviceProperties` tuple.

The affected heuristic is `_could_rblock_scale` in triton_heuristics.py.

On XPU, `_could_rblock_scale` currently evaluates to `False`, so `_dynamic_scale_rblock()` is skipped.

The affected tests are:

- `ComboKernelTests.test_combo_kernel_dynamic_scale_rblock`
- `ComboKernelTestsPerSubkernelBlocks.test_combo_kernel_dynamic_scale_rblock`

The test explicitly requires `_could_rblock_scale` to be `True` at test_combo_kernels.py.

## Current `DeviceProperties` fields

`DeviceProperties` currently contains:

```python
class DeviceProperties(typing.NamedTuple):
    type: str
    index: int
    multi_processor_count: int
    cc: int
    major: int | None = None
    regs_per_multiprocessor: int | None = None
    max_threads_per_multi_processor: int | None = None
    max_threads_per_block: int | None = None
    warp_size: int | None = None
```

The values are populated in `DeviceProperties.create()` using:

```python
props = device_interface.get_device_properties(device)

return cls(
    type=device_type,
    index=device.index,
    multi_processor_count=multi_processor_count,
    cc=device_interface.get_compute_capability(device),
    major=getattr(props, "major", None),
    regs_per_multiprocessor=getattr(props, "regs_per_multiprocessor", None),
    max_threads_per_multi_processor=getattr(
        props, "max_threads_per_multi_processor", None
    ),
    max_threads_per_block=getattr(props, "max_threads_per_block", 1024),
    warp_size=getattr(props, "warp_size", None),
)
```

## Properties required by dynamic RBLOCK scaling

### `compiled_binary.n_regs`

This is a compiled Triton kernel property, not a device property.

It is read from:

```python
nreg = getattr(compiled_binary, "n_regs", None)
```

The Intel Triton backend now provides this value after PR #7416. This value does not need to be added to `DeviceProperties`.

### `multi_processor_count`

This property is already available for XPU.

The current XPU fallback is:

```python
multi_processor_count = props.gpu_subslice_count
```

For the current design, one XPU subslice/Xe-core is treated as one occupancy unit, analogous to one CUDA SM.

The current PVC device reports:

```text
gpu_subslice_count = 64
```

The units of all other occupancy properties must be consistent with this choice.

### `regs_per_multiprocessor`

This property is currently missing on XPU.

It is used by both `_could_rblock_scale` and `_iter_rblock_scale_candidates()`:

```python
nreg <= (
    regs_per_multiprocessor
    // max_threads_per_multi_processor
)
```

and:

```python
max_blocks_per_sm = max(
    regs_per_multiprocessor // nreg_per_block,
    1,
)
```

With subslice/Xe-core as the occupancy unit, this value must represent:

```text
The total register/GRF capacity of one subslice/Xe-core.
```

It must not be confused with:

- the register capacity of one EU;
- the total register capacity of the entire device;
- `compiled_binary.n_regs`;
- the Triton default `n_regs = 128`.

This value must come from a real Intel XPU hardware or runtime source. It should not be guessed from the currently exposed EU-count fields.

### `max_threads_per_multi_processor`

This property is currently missing on XPU.

It represents the maximum number of resident threads per occupancy unit. It is not the same as the maximum work-group size.

The current XPU device reports:

```text
max_work_group_size = 1024
```

This can be used for:

```python
max_threads_per_block
```

but it must not be used as:

```python
max_threads_per_multi_processor
```

If the occupancy unit is confirmed to be one subslice/Xe-core, this value may potentially be derived from:

```text
subgroup_width
* gpu_eu_count_per_subslice
* gpu_hw_threads_per_eu
```

For example:

```text
32 * 8 * 8 = 2048
```

However, this formula needs to be validated against Intel XPU occupancy semantics before being exposed as a public property.

### `warp_size`

This property is currently missing from the raw XPU properties exposed to PyTorch.

It is required by `_iter_rblock_scale_candidates()` and is used in:

```python
nreg_per_warp = nreg * warp_size
nreg_per_block = nreg_per_warp * triton_config.num_warps
```

The Intel Triton backend currently uses a subgroup width of 32, so the expected initial value is likely:

```text
warp_size = 32
```

This value must match the subgroup/warp width used by the Intel Triton backend.

Although `DeviceProperties.warp_size_or_default` returns 32 for non-CUDA/HIP devices, that fallback does not satisfy the current heuristic because `_could_rblock_scale` checks the raw field:

```python
device_prop.warp_size is not None
```

Therefore, XPU must either expose `warp_size` through the native device properties or populate it explicitly in `DeviceProperties.create()`.

## Current XPU status

| Property | XPU status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | Available | `"xpu"` |
| `index` | Available | Taken from `torch.device` |
| `multi_processor_count` | Available | Derived from `gpu_subslice_count` |
| `cc` | Available | Backend compute capability value |
| `major` | Not available | XPU has no CUDA compute capability |
| `regs_per_multiprocessor` | Missing | Must be the real capacity of one subslice/Xe-core |
| `max_threads_per_multi_processor` | Missing | Must describe resident threads per subslice/Xe-core |
| `max_threads_per_block` | Available/defaulted | `max_work_group_size`, currently 1024 |
| `warp_size` | Missing | Expected to match the Triton subgroup width, currently likely 32 |

## `major` should not be fabricated for XPU

The current CUDA/HIP-only gate is:

```python
and device_prop.type in ["cuda", "hip"]
and bool(device_prop.major)
and (device_prop.major >= 8 or torch.version.hip)
```

This gate is appropriate for CUDA/HIP, where `major` represents CUDA compute capability. XPU does not have an equivalent CUDA `major` field, so assigning an artificial value such as `major = 8` would be incorrect.

Instead, `_could_rblock_scale` should use backend-specific capability checks:

```python
is_xpu = device_prop.type == "xpu"
is_cuda_or_hip = device_prop.type in ("cuda", "hip")

and (is_xpu or is_cuda_or_hip)
and (
    is_xpu
    or (
        bool(device_prop.major)
        and (device_prop.major >= 8 or torch.version.hip)
    )
)
```

The XPU path should only be enabled once the required occupancy properties are correctly populated.

## Required changes

### PyTorch/XPU backend

Expose the following properties through `_XpuDeviceProperties`:

```python
regs_per_multiprocessor
max_threads_per_multi_processor
warp_size
```

The values should flow through the following layers:

```text
Intel XPU runtime / Level Zero / compute-runtime
    -> c10::xpu::DeviceProp
    -> torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp
    -> torch.xpu.get_device_properties()
    -> DeviceProperties.create()
```

### Inductor

Update `_could_rblock_scale` so that:

- CUDA/HIP continue to use the existing `major` check.
- XPU uses XPU-specific capability and occupancy properties.
- XPU is not required to provide a fabricated CUDA `major`.

### Tests

After the properties and gate are implemented:

1. Remove the XPU skip, if any, from the dynamic RBLOCK tests.
2. Verify that `_could_rblock_scale` is `True` for a combo reduction.
3. Verify that `_dynamic_scale_rblock()` generates scaled candidates.
4. Verify that combo candidates contain suffixed keys such as:
   ```text
   R0_BLOCK_0
   R0_BLOCK_1
   ```
5. Add coverage for the XPU values returned by `DeviceProperties.create()`.

## Acceptance criteria

For an XPU combo reduction with dynamic RBLOCK scaling enabled:

```python
device_props.type == "xpu"
device_props.multi_processor_count is not None
device_props.regs_per_multiprocessor is not None
device_props.max_threads_per_multi_processor is not None
device_props.warp_size is not None
compiled_binary.n_regs is not None
```

and:

```python
CachingAutotuner._could_rblock_scale is True
```

The implementation must use real XPU occupancy properties and must not depend on a fabricated CUDA `major` value.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

With subslice/Xe-core as the occupancy unit, this value must represent:
The total register/GRF capacity of one subslice/Xe-core.

It must not be confused with:

the register capacity of one EU;
the total register capacity of the entire device;
compiled_binary.n_regs;
the Triton default n_regs = 128.

This value must come from a real Intel XPU hardware or runtime source. It should not be guessed from the currently exposed EU-count fields.
max_threads_per_multi_processor
This property is currently missing on XPU.
It represents the maximum number of resident threads per occupancy unit. It is not the same as the maximum work-group size.
The current XPU device reports:
max_work_group_size = 1024

This can be used for:
max_threads_per_block
but it must not be used as:
max_threads_per_multi_processor
If the occupancy unit is confirmed to be one subslice/Xe-core, this value may potentially be derived from:
subgroup_width
* gpu_eu_count_per_subslice
* gpu_hw_threads_per_eu

For example:
32 * 8 * 8 = 2048

However, this formula needs to be validated against Intel XPU occupancy semantics before being exposed as a public property.
warp_size
This property is currently missing from the raw XPU properties exposed to PyTorch.
It is required by _iter_rblock_scale_candidates() and is used in:
nreg_per_warp = nreg * warp_size
nreg_per_block = nreg_per_warp * triton_config.num_warps
The Intel Triton backend currently uses a subgroup width of 32, so the expected initial value is likely:
warp_size = 32

This value must match the subgroup/warp width used by the Intel Triton backend.
Although DeviceProperties.warp_size_or_default returns 32 for non-CUDA/HIP devices, that fallback does not satisfy the current heuristic because _could_rblock_scale checks the raw field:
device_prop.warp_size is not None
Therefore, XPU must either expose warp_size through the native device properties or populate it explicitly in DeviceProperties.create().
Current XPU status



Property
XPU status
Notes




type
Available
"xpu"


index
Available
Taken from torch.device


multi_processor_count
Available
Derived from gpu_subslice_count


cc
Available
Backend compute capability value


major
Not available
XPU has no CUDA compute capability


regs_per_multiprocessor
Missing
Must be the real capacity of one subslice/Xe-core


max_threads_per_multi_processor
Missing
Must describe resident threads per subslice/Xe-core


max_threads_per_block
Available/defaulted
max_work_group_size, currently 1024


warp_size
Missing
Expected to match the Triton subgroup width, currently likely 32



major should not be fabricated for XPU
The current CUDA/HIP-only gate is:
and device_prop.type in ["cuda", "hip"]
and bool(device_prop.major)
and (device_prop.major >= 8 or torch.version.hip)
This gate is appropriate for CUDA/HIP, where major represents CUDA compute capability. XPU does not have an equivalent CUDA major field, so assigning an artificial value such as major = 8 would be incorrect.
Instead, _could_rblock_scale should use backend-specific capability checks:
is_xpu = device_prop.type == "xpu"
is_cuda_or_hip = device_prop.type in ("cuda", "hip")

and (is_xpu or is_cuda_or_hip)
and (
    is_xpu
    or (
        bool(device_prop.major)
        and (device_prop.major >= 8 or torch.version.hip)
    )
)
The XPU path should only be enabled once the required occupancy properties are correctly populated.
Required changes
PyTorch/XPU backend
Expose the following properties through _XpuDeviceProperties:
regs_per_multiprocessor
max_threads_per_multi_processor
warp_size
The values should flow through the following layers:
Intel XPU runtime / Level Zero / compute-runtime
    -> c10::xpu::DeviceProp
    -> torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp
    -> torch.xpu.get_device_properties()
    -> DeviceProperties.create()

Inductor
Update _could_rblock_scale so that:

CUDA/HIP continue to use the existing major check.
XPU uses XPU-specific capability and occupancy properties.
XPU is not required to provide a fabricated CUDA major.

Tests
After the properties and gate are implemented:

Remove the XPU skip, if any, from the dynamic RBLOCK tests.
Verify that _could_rblock_scale is True for a combo reduction.
Verify that _dynamic_scale_rblock() generates scaled candidates.
Verify that combo candidates contain suffixed keys such as:
R0_BLOCK_0
R0_BLOCK_1


Add coverage for the XPU values returned by DeviceProperties.create().

Acceptance criteria
For an XPU combo reduction with dynamic RBLOCK scaling enabled:
device_props.type == "xpu"
device_props.multi_processor_count is not None
device_props.regs_per_multiprocessor is not None
device_props.max_threads_per_multi_processor is not None
device_props.warp_size is not None
compiled_binary.n_regs is not None
and:
CachingAutotuner._could_rblock_scale is True
The implementation must use real XPU occupancy properties and must not depend on a fabricated CUDA major value.
Alternatives
No response
Additional context
No response

nodes.bodyText: max_threads_per_multi_processor can be evaluated by "max work items per sub slice". Only regs_per_multiprocessor is lacking.
I think we don't need regs_per_multiprocessor because Intel GPU share grf resource per hardware thread instead of SM. So we have no concept can map this property.

issues.body:
## Description

`test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu` (`TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU`, `test/test_transformers.py`) fails on XPU with a large accuracy mismatch when running the FLASH_ATTENTION fused kernel (`fused_kernel0` == `SDPBackend.FLASH_ATTENTION`) against the MATH reference backend, for the `dense` (non-nested) input case.

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!

Mismatched elements: 32655 / 32768 (99.7%)
Greatest absolute difference: 2.993957042694092 at index (12, 1, 0, 15) (up to 0.007 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 1.0007356405258179 at index (5, 1, 1, 4) (up to 0.007 allowed)
```

## Root cause / context

This test cell is running on XPU **for the first time** as of pytorch/pytorch#185115 ("[Test] Enable `TestSDPAGpuOnly` on XPU and skip cases unsupported by torch-xpu-ops"), which renamed `TestSDPACudaOnly` -> `TestSDPAGpuOnly` and instantiated it on XPU via `instantiate_device_type_tests`.

That PR already narrowed the `type` parametrize to `["dense"]` only on XPU (skipping `nested`, tracked at #3132), but it did **not** add a skip for the `dense` + `FLASH_ATTENTION` combination, so this cell now runs unguarded and fails with a near-100% element mismatch — i.e. XPU's flash attention fused kernel is producing numerically incorrect output for this dense packed-QKV case, not just failing tolerance by a small margin.

PR #185115's own DrCI AI verdict on the XPU CI failure confirms this analysis:

> "This causes `test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy` with `type="dense"` and `fused_kernel=FLASH_ATTENTION` to run on XPU for the first time. The test fails because XPU's flash attention kernel produces inaccurate results for this case, which was not skipped by the PR."

No existing tracking issue was found in `intel/torch-xpu-ops` for this specific dense+FLASH_ATTENTION accuracy cell (related but distinct issues: #3132 nested-type skip, #3133 nested-contiguity RuntimeError).

## Failing test

```
Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_transformers_xpu.TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU,test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu
```

## Reproduction

```
python test/test_transformers.py TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU.test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu
```

## CI reference

- PR: [地址已移除]
- Failing job: [地址已移除]
- Related: #3132, #3133

## Action items

- [ ] Confirm root cause (XPU flash attention kernel numerical bug vs. missing skip)
- [ ] Add `@skipIfXpu` / in-body skip for `type="dense"` + `fused_kernel=FLASH_ATTENTION` in `test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy` in `pytorch/pytorch` `test/test_transformers.py`, referencing this issue
- [ ] Mirror the skip in `third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/skip_list_common.py`
- [ ] Investigate/fix the underlying XPU flash attention kernel accuracy issue for dense packed QKV inputs

Automated fix session for #4401 — workflow run.

Issue Triage

Value

no


Scope
torch-xpu-ops


Dependencies
(none named in body)


Handling
agent-fixable



Carried context: a maintainer comment on this issue attributes the failure to
the CI machine's PVC LTS2 driver shipping an older IGC with a known accuracy
issue. That is a hypothesis about the environment, not the body-declared
scope, so this run does not stop on it — instead Stage 2 reproduces the case on
the current nightly wheel + this runner's driver, which is the empirical test of
that claim.
Automated by issue-triage.

Reproduce (stage: nightly)
Verdict: CANNOT_VERIFY — blocker: the reported failure is PVC-specific and
this fix runner has no PVC device.









Wheel
torch 2.15.0.dev20260905+xpu (nightly XPU index)


Fix runner GPU
8x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics (BMG, 0xE211), driver 26.22.38646.7


Failing CI runner
dut7900_pvc_card_3, labels linux.idc.xpu (PVC)


Command run
pytest -sv --timeout 600 test_transformers_xpu.py::TestSDPACudaOnlyXPU::test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu


Result
PASSED in 10.7s



The exact node id in the issue (TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU) exists only on the
unmerged pytorch PR, so the equivalent cell was run from torch-xpu-ops' own
vendored copy of the file, which carries the identical test body and is not
covered by skip_list_common.py for type=dense (only the two nested cells
are skipped there).
Checks run beyond the single cell, all on BMG:

The FLASH_ATTENTION backend is genuinely selected (_fused_sdp_choice returns
1 under sdpa_kernel([FLASH_ATTENTION])), so the pass is not a silent
fallback to MATH.
40 random seeds of the exact test shape (B=16, S=8, H=4, D=64, fp16, packed
QKV, strides (6144, 64, 768, 1)): 0 failures, worst absolute deviation
0.0074 — i.e. fp16 rounding scale, nothing like the reported 2.99 /
99.7% mismatch.
A 144-config sweep over head dims 32/64/96/128/192/256, packed vs unpacked,
contiguous vs strided, causal vs not: 0 failures in all 72 fp16 configs.
(The bf16 half of the sweep exceeds a 7e-3 tolerance, which is expected for
bf16 against an fp32 MATH reference and is not what this test measures --
the test only uses fp16.)


Root cause analysis
Not a torch-xpu-ops source-level defect that this run can locate or fix, on
three independent pieces of evidence:

No functional change since the failure. git log over
src/ATen/native/transformers/xpu/flash_attn/ shows the last change after
2026-07-21 to be clang-tidy / modernization work (#4372, #4373, #4827).
Nothing landed that could have fixed a genuine numerical bug, so the pass on
BMG today is not "already fixed upstream" -- it is the same kernel source
behaving correctly.
No PVC-specific code path exists. The SYCL-TLA FMHA forward kernel is
architecture-agnostic in source: kSubgroupSize is a fixed 16, the QK/PV
tile shapes are compile-time constants selected per head dim, and the device
architecture is consulted only for an allowlist check in
sycltla/mha_fwd.cpp (intel_gpu_pvc, intel_gpu_pvc_vg,
intel_gpu_bmg_g21, intel_gpu_bmg_g31). There is no device-property-driven
tiling or accumulation-order choice that could diverge between PVC and BMG.
This is consistent with the maintainer comment already on this issue
attributing the failure to the PVC LTS2 driver's older IGC. A near-total
(99.7% of elements) mismatch with relative error ~1.0 is the signature of a
miscompiled kernel, not of a tolerance being slightly too tight.

Taken together: the failure most plausibly lives in the IGC/driver stack on the
pytorch-CI PVC machines, and confirming or refuting that requires running on
PVC. That hardware is not present on this runner, which is why the verdict is
CANNOT_VERIFY rather than "no longer reproduces" -- declaring the issue stale
from a BMG-only pass would not be supportable.
Suggested next steps for a human

Re-run the cell on a PVC machine with a current driver/IGC. If it passes,
the issue is an environment pin on the pytorch IDC PVC runners, and the fix
belongs there rather than in kernel code.
If it still fails on PVC with a current stack, capture the generated kernel
ASM on PVC (the extract-asm-syclkernel-aot /
extract-xpu-kernel-asm skills exist for this) and compare against BMG to
localize the miscompile before touching the kernel source.
Note that pytorch/pytorch#185115 is still open and was reworked
(TestSDPAGpuOnly -> TestSDPAAccelerator); its current head still runs
type="dense" + FLASH_ATTENTION on XPU unguarded, so this cell will
surface again on PVC when that PR next runs CI.


Summary









Issue
#4401 -- test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu accuracy failure

single-bug

NEEDS_HUMAN (reason=cannot_verify)

Fix branch
none -- no fix was implemented, so there is no patch artifact

kernel change it cannot verify. The analysis above is the deliverable; the PVC
re-run in "next steps" is the one action that would unblock it.

```python
 def test_cuda_memory_leak_detection(self):
        l = []

        @self.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check
        def no_leak():
            pass

        @self.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check
        def leak_gpu0():
            # increasing to 8MB to force acquiring a new block and overcome blocksize differences across platforms
            l.append(torch.randn(1024 * 1024 * 8, device=torch.device(f"{GPU_TYPE}:0")))

        no_leak()
        regex = r"CUDA driver API confirmed .+ on device 0.+"
        if IS_JETSON:
```

```python

class CudaMemoryLeakCheck:
    def __init__(self, testcase, name=None):
        self.name = testcase.id() if name is None else name
        self.testcase = testcase

        # initialize context & RNG to prevent false positive detections
        # when the test is the first to initialize those
        from torch.testing._internal.common_cuda import initialize_cuda_context_rng
        initialize_cuda_context_rng()

    # Stores CUDA memory data provided by PyTorch's caching allocator and
    #   the CUDA driver.
    #
    # NOTE: The undocumented torch.cuda.mem_get_info() returns
    #   (#free bytes, #total bytes available) on the GPU
    def __enter__(self):
        self.caching_allocator_befores = []
        self.driver_befores = []

        # Performs a gc if required (required if any CUDA memory is held)
        num_devices = torch.cuda.device_count()
        for i in range(num_devices):
            caching_allocator_mem_allocated = torch.cuda.memory_allocated(i)
            # NOTE: gc is based exclusively on caching allocator memory
            #   because the driver will always have some bytes in use (context size?)
            if caching_allocator_mem_allocated > 0:
                gc.collect()
                torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces()
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
                break
...
```

issues.title: [Inductor] Optimize scaled_mm Triton Template
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Summary

This issue tracks ongoing optimizations to the Triton template implementation of `scaled_mm` in PyTorch Inductor.

The current Triton template leaves room for performance improvements on XPU. This tracking issue serves as a central place to organize optimization efforts and link the corresponding PRs.

## Goals
- [x]  Validate Triton kernel correctness
- [ ]  Improve `scaled_mm` kernel performance
    - [x]  Use 2D block prefetch and load for matrix B
    - [x]  Enable SIMD32 code generation. Triton currently generates SIMD16 instructions by default, which limits performance on some workload.
    - [ ] Investigate unexpected MOV instructions between 2D Block Load and DPAS
    - [ ] Investigate unexpected initialization instructions before 2D Block Load

## Planned Optimizations
### Use 2D block prefetch and load for matrix B
1. Created a Triton issue([地址已移除]) to track the performance issue.
2. Optimized the FP8 tensor-wise scaled_mm Triton template by leveraging tl.make_tensor_descriptor for matrix loading, enabling 2D Block Load and prefetch. The optimization improved the kernel performance for (M=512, N=512, K=256, no bias), reducing execution latency from 70 μs to 30 μs (~57% reduction).

### Enable SIMD32 code generation. Triton currently generates SIMD16 instructions by default, which limits performance on some workload.
Triton currently generates SIMD16 instructions by default. Performance analysis shows that, for the `(M=512, N=512, K=256, no bias)` workload, using TRITON_INTEL_ENABLE_DPAS_FOR_WARP_SIZE_32=1 to generate SIMD32 instructions can improve kernel performance by approximately 20%.

### Investigate unexpected MOV instructions between 2D Block Load and DPAS
1. Created a Triton issue([地址已移除]) to track the performance issue.

### Investigate unexpected initialization instructions before 2D Block Load
1. Created a Triton issue([地址已移除]) to track the performance issue.

issues.title: [DLE 2026.1 / XPU] `expandable_segments:True` regresses on BMG — `DEVICE_LOST` in xccl collectives (and a matching FSDP2 hang); clean on DLE 2025.3
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Hi,

We hit a reproducible regression on Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG, 2-GPU, PCIe) that
appears when the PyTorch XPU caching allocator runs in **`expandable_segments`**
mode. It is **new in the DLE 2026.1 runtime** — the identical repro passes on
DLE 2025.3. There are two surface symptoms that we've traced to the same trigger.


Setting `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` (the shared alloc-conf; the
CUDA-named `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` alias also reaches the XPU allocator) makes
the allocator hand out virtual-memory (VMM/USM) blocks. On DLE 2026.1, downstream
use of those blocks fails:

1. **Collective path → crash.** A 256 MiB `all_reduce` (the log prints `268MB`
   decimal) on such a buffer dies at the next `torch.xpu.synchronize()` with
   `RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)`.
   Minimal (~40-line repro, no model/FSDP).
2. **Local FSDP2 path → hang.** A real 2-GPU FSDP2 step-1 forward hangs (no
   collective involved) at a single-scalar device→host copy
   (`_can_skip_causal_mask_xpu` → `.item()` → `appendUSMMemcpy`, L0-v2 adapter).
   Both ranks ~97% CPU, no error.

Same trigger, same fix (don't set `expandable_segments` on XPU). Flipping only that
one env var flips each case between pass and fail.

Same box, same GPU kernel driver (26.22.38646) throughout; only the DLE runtime set
differs. Full `collect_env` for both stacks is in the repo.

| torch | oneCCL | DLE | `expandable_segments:True` + 256 MiB `all_reduce` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.13.0+xpu (stable) | 2022.0 | 2026.1 | ❌ DEVICE_LOST |
| 2.14 nightly | 2022.0 | 2026.1 | ❌ DEVICE_LOST |
| **2.13 nightly** | **2021.17** | **2025.3** | ✅ SURVIVED  ← torch held at 2.13, only runtime changed |
| 2.12.0+xpu | 2021.17 | 2025.3 | ✅ SURVIVED |

## Ask

On DLE 2026.1, could you look at how the oneCCL / L0-v2 collective path handles
buffers from the `expandable_segments` (VMM/USM) allocator? Specifically:
- the collective that crashes at `torch.xpu.synchronize()` with `DEVICE_LOST`, and
- the immediate-in-order-queue `appendUSMMemcpy` that hangs when FSDP2 work is
  pending (details + gdb/py-spy stacks in the scalar-copy-hang folder).

[repro.py]([地址已移除])

### log
for the detail log, can pm me. Because put in internal repository. But sent to panas for the log

## extra information on non docker image or proper setup steps.
--
the current native machine.

Both installed as plain pip wheels into isolated venvs. Both pull the same runtime on their own: oneCCL 2022.0 + intel-sycl-rt 2026 (libsycl.so.9), xpu_build=20260000. No DLE image anywhere.

Stack (native pip, no DLE)	EXPANDABLE=1	EXPANDABLE=0

torch 2.13.0+xpu (stable)	❌ DEVICE_LOST at synchronize() (catchable RuntimeError)	✅ SURVIVED (val=2.0)

torch 2.14.0.dev20260722+xpu (nightly)	❌ SIGABRT — oneCCL send_entry.hpp:109 SEND failed / OFI Bad address(14)	✅ SURVIVED (val=2.0)

Both flip deterministically on the one env var. So yes — the bug reproduces natively, with the public wheel, on both torch versions. No DLE required.

--

nodes.bodyText:
I met this issue in BMG B580 Windows Weekly on
quantization\core\test_quantized_op_xpu.py
quantization\core\test_quantized_tensor_xpu.py
quantization\core\test_workflow_module_xpu.py
export\test_export_training_ir_to_run_decomp_xpu.py

I had this issue in BMG B580 Windows Weekly while running separately each by each on example tests:
export\test_export_xpu.py::TestDynamismExpression::test_no_grad_param_inplace
export\test_export_xpu.py::TestOneOffModelExportResult::test_hf_logging_logger

Adding fresh repro data from PyTorch 2.14 XPU nightly. These tests passed with PyTorch 2.13, but crash during collection with 2.14 before any test body runs.
Environment

Container: intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18
Python: 3.10.20
PyTorch target: torch==2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu
torchvision target: torchvision==0.29.0.dev20260806+xpu
torchaudio target: torchaudio==2.11.0.dev20260806+xpu
Triton XPU target: triton-xpu==3.8.0+git1e2d42a0
Baseline: PyTorch 2.13 XPU, same tests passed

Additional affected tests observed
pytest -v test/xpu/export/test_export_training_ir_to_run_decomp_xpu.py
pytest test/xpu/quantization/core/test_workflow_module_xpu.py
pytest test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_op_xpu.py
pytest test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_tensor_xpu.py

All four fail during collection with:
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'

Representative stacks:
test/xpu/export/test_export_training_ir_to_run_decomp_xpu.py:30: in <module>
    from export import test_export, testing
../../test/export/test_export.py:31: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental.control_flow import cond, map
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'

test/xpu/quantization/core/test_workflow_module_xpu.py:28: in <module>
    from test_workflow_module import (
../../test/quantization/core/test_workflow_module.py:48: in <module>
    from torch.testing._internal.common_quantization import (
.../site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_quantization.py:14: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental import control_flow
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'

test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_op_xpu.py:28: in <module>
    from test_quantized_op import TestQuantizedOps
../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py:39: in <module>
    from torch.testing._internal.common_quantization import (
.../site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_quantization.py:14: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental import control_flow
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'

test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_tensor_xpu.py:33: in <module>
    from test_quantized_tensor import TestQuantizedTensor
../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_tensor.py:17: in <module>
    from torch.testing._internal.common_quantization import get_supported_device_types
.../site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_quantization.py:14: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental import control_flow
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'

Light analysis
This looks like an API/package compatibility regression between the 2.14 wheel and tests/helpers being imported:

The XPU wrapper tests import upstream PyTorch test modules, for example test/export/test_export.py and test/quantization/core/test_*.py.
Those upstream modules or packaged internal helpers still import functorch.experimental, especially functorch.experimental.control_flow.
In the observed PyTorch 2.14 XPU environment, the functorch.experimental namespace is not available, so pytest fails during collection.
The quantization failures route through torch.testing._internal.common_quantization from the installed PyTorch package, so this is not only a torch-xpu-ops wrapper issue. The installed 2.14 package itself still contains an internal helper that imports the missing namespace.
A nearby unrelated XPU op test still passes, which points to an import/API compatibility issue rather than a general XPU runtime failure.

Possible fix direction: restore/ship the functorch.experimental compatibility namespace in the 2.14 XPU package, or update the affected upstream test/helper imports to the current replacement API and sync the XPU wrapper tests.

Automated fix session for this issue. Stage reports are appended below as the pipeline advances.

Issue Triage



Field

Automated by issue-triage.

Root-cause Analysis

Issue type: core framework bug (pytorch test infra)
Fix repo: pytorch
Analyzed at: pytorch@ded21956
Root cause: TestFX.setUp in pytorch's test/test_fx.py flips the
process-global torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations to True
(test/test_fx.py:271-276) and restores it only in tearDown
(test/test_fx.py:282-286); it then calls
torch.ops.load_library(find_library_location("libtorchbind_test.so"))
(test/test_fx.py:278-280), which raises OSError in XPU CI because the
installed wheel does not ship that test-only library
(find_library_location falls back to a non-existent
torch/build/lib/libtorchbind_test.so). unittest does not run tearDown
when setUp raised, so the flag stays True for the remainder of that
xdist worker process. The next TestCommonPass mutation case in the same
module (test/xpu/test_fx_xpu.py:164 tracing
test/fx/test_common_passes.py:51-54, y.add_(1)) then hits the guard at
torch/fx/proxy.py:232 and fails with
RuntimeError: Tried to trace mutable operation aten::add_.Tensor.
Nothing device-specific is involved: in the referenced nightly run all 422
TestFX cases fail with the libtorchbind_test.so OSError, and all ten
TestCommonPass mutation cases fail — including the _cpu variants
(test_correctness_CSEPass_Mutation_cpu,
test_correctness_factory_CSEPass_MutationFactory_cpu, ...), which rules out
any XPU kernel or functionalization gap.
Fix strategy: In pytorch test/test_fx.py, move the
libtorchbind_test.so load in TestFX.setUp ahead of the
check_mutable_operations save/flip so no statement that can raise executes
while the global flag is flipped. This matches the ordering the sibling
classes in the same file already use (TestOperatorSignatures:5188,
TestFXAPIBackwardCompatibility:5231, TestFunctionalTracing:5593,
TestVisionTracing:5872 all set the flag as the last statement of setUp).
Verdict: IMPLEMENTING — non-exception-safe global-state flip in a
device-agnostic pytorch test file; one-file, test-only fix.

Automated by fix-root-cause.

Implementation

Target repo: pytorch (test/test_fx.py)
Changed files: test/test_fx.py (1 file, +8 / -5)
Skip-guard review: APPROVE (no skip / xfail / tolerance-loosening / assertion-deletion constructs added)

+++ b/test/test_fx.py
@@ -268,17 +268,20 @@ def _parse_profiler_trace_lines(traces: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
 class TestFX(JitTestCase):
     def setUp(self):
         super().setUp()
+        if not (IS_FBCODE or IS_WINDOWS or IS_MACOS):
+            lib_file_path = find_library_location("libtorchbind_test.so")

-        # Enable it in testing but not by default

+        # process-global and is only restored in tearDown, which unittest skips
+        # when setUp raises -- so this must stay the last statement of setUp, or
+        # a failure above would leak it into every later test in the process.

The load_library call is the only statement in setUp that can raise, so
moving it above the flag flip means a missing libtorchbind_test.so can no
longer leave check_mutable_operations = True behind for the rest of the
worker process. No behavioural change for the TestFX cases themselves.

TestFX.setUp flipped the process-global
torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations to True before doing the
one thing in setUp that can fail (loading the test-only
libtorchbind_test.so, which the XPU wheel does not ship). Because unittest
skips tearDown when setUp raises, the flag stayed True for the rest of the
xdist worker, and the next TestCommonPass mutation test to trace an in-place
op failed. Moving the library load above the flag flip means the flip is the
last statement in setUp, so nothing can leak it. The reported failure was
never device-specific; the _cpu variants failed the same way.
Follow-up, not fixed here: the ~422 TestFX setUp errors from the wheel
not shipping libtorchbind_test.so remain. This change only stops them from
taking the 10 mutation tests down with them. Making TestFX itself pass on a
wheel install needs a separate decision (ship the library, or skip those cases
when it is absent) and belongs in its own issue.

why: root-cause
Strongly accept.
Root cause dates back to #64467 (2021): that PR added the mutable-op tracing flag to TestFX, but inserted the process-global flag flip before the only statement in setUp that can throw (loading libtorchbind_test.so), with the restore left in tearDown. unittest does not run tearDown when setUp raises, so the flag stays flipped for the rest of the process.
What exposed it: our wheel is built with the upstream release config (INSTALL_TEST=0), so it does not ship that .so and setUp always throws; and test_fx_xpu.py puts TestFX and TestCommonPass in the same module. Those two together surface a hazard that has been there since 2021, showing up as TestCommonPass's add_ being rejected. Nothing XPU-specific — the _cpu variants fail the same way.
Patch looks good. Two follow-ups:

 Land the fix upstream. Opened as pytorch/pytorch#196569. Next: add it to the apply_torch_pr.py pr-list so CI picks it up without waiting for the pin to move. Keep this issue open until the fix actually reaches the pytorch used by CI — the case is currently exempted via this issue's skipped label feeding Known_issue.log, and closing the issue removes that exemption.
 Make TestFX skip instead of error when the library is missing. The missing .so still takes down all 422 TestFX cases at setUp, including the three SYCL profiler tests we added in test_fx_xpu.py, which have therefore never run. Upstream already landed pytorch/pytorch#193122, which makes load_torchbind_test_lib() raise SkipTest rather than OSError, but test_fx.py still calls find_library_location + load_library directly. Switching it over would turn those 422 errors into honest skips. Two things to settle first: it changes Windows behaviour (TestFX currently skips the load entirely on Windows, the helper loads torchbind_test.dll), and it would leave our three profiler tests permanently skipped unless we also make the library available in the test job. Worth a separate issue.

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

I just found some of our loop kernel still uses total elements as global range,  means the for loop does nothing. In all loop kernels, global range should be std::min(total_elements, syclGpuEuCount() * syclGpuHWThreadsPerEU() * 32)
i.e. 
[avg pool]([地址已移除]) AvgPool2dKernelFunctor  and AvgPool2dChannelsLastKernelFunctor  uses XPU_KERNEL_LOOP, but global range is still total elements. I get 10% improvement on channels last, 1024,768,17,17, kernel size=3, stride=1, pad=1 on 1550 by simply set global range = subgroup size * vector engine per core * hardward thread per vector engine * xe core number

[地址已移除] ConvDepthwise3dXpuFunctor and ConvDepthwise3dXpuBackwardInputFunctor, global range is hard code by min(num_output, 65536)

issues.title: [xpu-aglinment] Fix NLLLoss2d backward 32-bit offset overflow
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

<!-- agent:status:IN_REVIEW -->

`F.nll_loss(...).backward()` produces a silently wrong gradient on XPU when the
flattened offset reaches 2^31. The XPU SYCL backward kernel still uses 32-bit
`sample`, `toffset`, and `ioffset` values, so the offset wraps around instead of
addressing the full tensor.

This was found during XPU alignment for upstream PyTorch issue
[地址已移除] The upstream CUDA path was
already fixed by selecting a 64-bit index type when 32-bit indexing is unsafe;
the analogous XPU kernel was never updated, so XPU still exhibits the original
overflow.

### Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

print("torch", torch.__version__)
print("xpu available", torch.xpu.is_available())

x = torch.zeros((2**16 + 1, 2**15, 1, 1), device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16, requires_grad=True)
target = torch.zeros((2**16 + 1, 1, 1), device="xpu", dtype=torch.long)

F.nll_loss(x, target, reduction="sum").backward()

assert x.grad[0, 0, 0, 0].item() == -1.0
assert x.grad[-1, 0, 0, 0].item() == -1.0
```

### Actual behavior

The first gradient is correct while the final sample gradient is zero, matching
32-bit offset wraparound at `sample * map_nelem * n_classes == 2**31`:

```text
x.grad[0,0,0,0]  = -1.0
x.grad[-1,0,0,0] = 0.0
RESULT: confirmed
```

### Expected behavior

Every valid target position receives its gradient regardless of tensor size,
matching CPU/CUDA eager semantics:

```text
x.grad[0,0,0,0]  = -1.0
x.grad[-1,0,0,0] = -1.0
```

### Alignment metadata

- Upstream source: [地址已移除]
- Source type: upstream issue (CUDA fixed; XPU unaligned)
- Local XPU result: confirmed
- Routed area: `intel/torch-xpu-ops`, XPU NLLLoss2d backward kernel offset typing
- Target repository: `intel-sandbox/torch-xpu-ops-exp`

### Notes

The upstream CUDA issue was closed after its kernel selected a 64-bit index type
when 32-bit indexing is unsafe. The XPU fix should independently align the SYCL
implementation with that guard (widen `sample`/`toffset`/`ioffset` to 64-bit when
the flattened extent exceeds `INT_MAX`) rather than modifying shared PyTorch code.

A regression test should be added under `test/repro/` and run with `pytest`.

### Versions

```text
PyTorch version: 2.14.0.dev20260713+xpu
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
Is XPU available: True
Intel GPU: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
Relevant path: src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/*Loss*.cpp (NLLLoss2d backward)
```

issues.title: [XPU] torchrun --numa-binding fails on XPU: _XpuDeviceProperties missing pci_domain_id/pci_bus_id/pci_device_id
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch/numa/binding.py` was made device-generic in #185266 (`torch.cuda` ->
`torch.accelerator`), but XPU doesn't satisfy the implicit backend contract, so
`--numa-binding` is unusable on Intel GPUs.

`_get_numa_node_index_for_device_index` (`torch/numa/binding.py:595-604`) reads
three PCI attributes to find the device's NUMA node via sysfs:

```python
domain = device_properties.pci_domain_id
bus    = device_properties.pci_bus_id
device = device_properties.pci_device_id
pci_addr = f"{domain:04x}:{bus:02x}:{device:02x}.0"
with open(f"/sys/bus/pci/devices/{pci_addr}/numa_node") as f: ...
```

CUDA binds them at `torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1201-1203`. XPU exposes no `pci_*`
attribute at all (full list: `torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp:326-360`), and
`grep -rn "pci" torch/csrc/xpu/ torch/xpu/ c10/xpu/` returns zero hits. The data is
missing one layer down too — `AT_FORALL_XPU_EXT_DEVICE_PROPERTIES`
(`c10/xpu/XPUDeviceProp.h:116-139`) never queries a PCI address — so *
need a change**, not just the pybind11 binding.

### Impact

`torchrun --numa-binding=<mode>` **fails to launch** with `AttributeError`:
`torch/distributed/run.py:957-960` doesn't set
`should_fall_back_if_binding_fails`, which defaults to `False`
(`binding.py:95`), so `_handle_exception` re-raises (`binding.py:266`)
fallback enabled it instead runs unbound and loses the locality win. The upstream
default (`numa_options=None`) is unaffected.

### Secondary issue: no test enforces the contract

`test/test_numa_binding.py` passes on XPU but gives no real XPU covera
`torch.get_device_module` to a `MagicMock` returning a hand-rolled
`MockDeviceProperties` that declares the three `pci_*` fields (lines 2
It would pass with no accelerator present. That mocking is right for its purpose
(fabricating 4-socket / 8-NUMA-node topologies no CI runner has), so t
missing test at a different layer. The contract exists only in #185266's
description:

> backends ... must expose `get_device_properties()` returning an obje
> `pci_domain_id`, `pci_bus_id`, and `pci_device_id`

`test/test_xpu.py:131` runs on real hardware but only checks self-consistency and a
few `> 0` assertions, so it misses this too.

### Suggested direction

1. Expose the PCI address on XPU. SYCL appears to offer it as one stri
   (`"0000:4d:00.0"`) not three ints — confirm against the installed
   `sycl/ext/intel/info/device.hpp`, including drivers lacking the ext
   Parsing to ints in the XPU layer keeps `binding.py` single-shaped.
2. Add a real-hardware contract test asserting those attributes exist
   `torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()`'s properties.
   `test/test_accelerator.py:277` is a good template.

HPU and PrivateUse1/OpenReg are likely affected the same way.

### Versions

`main` at f594cadbd10e.

issues.title: [xpu-aglinment] Fix GELU erf-tail catastrophic cancellation
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

<!-- agent:status:OPEN -->

Exact GELU on XPU loses the negative tail to catastrophic cancellation. The XPU
SYCL kernel computes the normal CDF term as `0.5 * (1 + erf(x * sqrt(1/2)))`.
For large negative values `erf` approaches `-1`, so `1 + erf(...)` cancels and
the remaining precision is lost.

This was found during XPU alignment for upstream PyTorch PR
[地址已移除] CPU/CUDA/MPS were covered by the
upstream fix, while XPU was explicitly excluded as an out-of-tree backend, so
XPU still exhibits the cancellation.

### Reproducer

```python
import math
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

x = torch.arange(-12.0, 12.0, 2**-6, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float32)
xref = x.cpu().double()
tail = xref.abs() >= 4.0
alpha = math.sqrt(0.5)

expected_fwd = 0.5 * xref * torch.erfc(-xref * alpha)
actual_fwd = F.gelu(x).cpu().double()
fwd_error = ((actual_fwd - expected_fwd)[tail] /
             expected_fwd[tail].abs().clamp(min=1e-30)).abs().max().item()

grad = torch.ones_like(x)
expected_bwd = (0.5 * torch.erfc(-xref * alpha) +
                xref * math.sqrt(2.0 / math.pi) * 0.5 *
                torch.exp(-0.5 * xref * xref))
actual_bwd = torch.ops.aten.gelu_backward(grad, x).cpu().double()
bwd_error = ((actual_bwd - expected_bwd)[tail] /
             expected_bwd[tail].abs().clamp(min=1e-30)).abs().max().item()

print(f"forward tail relative error: {fwd_error:.3e}")
print(f"backward tail relative error: {bwd_error:.3e}")
assert fwd_error < 1e-3
assert bwd_error < 1e-3
```

### Actual behavior

The exact-GELU forward tail is corrupted by cancellation instead of matching the
stable `erfc` reference:

```text
gelu forward tail relative error (|x|>=4): 1.000e+00
gelu_backward tail relative error (|x|>=4): 3.256e-02
XPU gelu forward: catastrophic cancellation detected (err=1.000e+00)
RESULT: confirmed
```

### Expected behavior

Forward and backward negative-tail relative error stay below `1e-3` for
`|x| >= 4`, matching a float64 `erfc` reference and CPU/CUDA eager semantics.

### Alignment metadata

- Upstream source: [地址已移除]
- Source type: upstream PR (CPU/CUDA/MPS fixed; XPU excluded)
- Local XPU result: confirmed
- Routed area: `intel/torch-xpu-ops`, `GeluErfFunctor` / `GeluErfBackwardFunctor` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ActivationGeluKernel.cpp`

### Notes

Use the stable expression `0.5 * erfc(-x * sqrt(1/2))` for the CDF term in both
exact-GELU forward and backward. Preserve the PDF term and the tanh-approximate
GELU path. The failure is specific to exact GELU, not the tanh approximation.

A regression test should be added under `test/regressions/` and run with
`pytest` after an editable XPU build; it must fail on the baseline and pass after
the fix.

### Versions

```text
PyTorch version: 2.14.0.dev20260713+xpu
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
Is XPU available: True
Intel GPU: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
Relevant path: src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ActivationGeluKernel.cpp
```

<!-- agent:triage-log -->

issues.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug

Exact GELU on XPU loses the negative tail to catastrophic cancellation. The XPU
SYCL kernel computes the normal CDF term as 0.5 * (1 + erf(x * sqrt(1/2))).
For large negative values erf approaches -1, so 1 + erf(...) cancels and
the remaining precision is lost.
This was found during XPU alignment for upstream PyTorch PR
pytorch/pytorch#189234. CPU/CUDA/MPS were covered by the
upstream fix, while XPU was explicitly excluded as an out-of-tree backend, so
XPU still exhibits the cancellation.
Reproducer
import math
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

x = torch.arange(-12.0, 12.0, 2**-6, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float32)
xref = x.cpu().double()
tail = xref.abs() >= 4.0
alpha = math.sqrt(0.5)

expected_fwd = 0.5 * xref * torch.erfc(-xref * alpha)
actual_fwd = F.gelu(x).cpu().double()
fwd_error = ((actual_fwd - expected_fwd)[tail] /
             expected_fwd[tail].abs().clamp(min=1e-30)).abs().max().item()

grad = torch.ones_like(x)
expected_bwd = (0.5 * torch.erfc(-xref * alpha) +
                xref * math.sqrt(2.0 / math.pi) * 0.5 *
                torch.exp(-0.5 * xref * xref))
actual_bwd = torch.ops.aten.gelu_backward(grad, x).cpu().double()
bwd_error = ((actual_bwd - expected_bwd)[tail] /
             expected_bwd[tail].abs().clamp(min=1e-30)).abs().max().item()

print(f"forward tail relative error: {fwd_error:.3e}")
print(f"backward tail relative error: {bwd_error:.3e}")
assert fwd_error < 1e-3
assert bwd_error < 1e-3
Actual behavior
The exact-GELU forward tail is corrupted by cancellation instead of matching the
stable erfc reference:
gelu forward tail relative error (|x|>=4): 1.000e+00
gelu_backward tail relative error (|x|>=4): 3.256e-02
XPU gelu forward: catastrophic cancellation detected (err=1.000e+00)
RESULT: confirmed

Expected behavior
Forward and backward negative-tail relative error stay below 1e-3 for
|x| >= 4, matching a float64 erfc reference and CPU/CUDA eager semantics.
Alignment metadata

Upstream source: pytorch/pytorch#189234
Source type: upstream PR (CPU/CUDA/MPS fixed; XPU excluded)
Local XPU result: confirmed
Routed area: intel/torch-xpu-ops, GeluErfFunctor / GeluErfBackwardFunctor in src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ActivationGeluKernel.cpp

Notes
Use the stable expression 0.5 * erfc(-x * sqrt(1/2)) for the CDF term in both
exact-GELU forward and backward. Preserve the PDF term and the tanh-approximate
GELU path. The failure is specific to exact GELU, not the tanh approximation.
A regression test should be added under test/regressions/ and run with
pytest after an editable XPU build; it must fail on the baseline and pass after
the fix.
Versions
PyTorch version: 2.14.0.dev20260713+xpu
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
Is XPU available: True
Intel GPU: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
Relevant path: src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ActivationGeluKernel.cpp

source.title: [XPU] Fix exact-GELU erf-tail catastrophic cancellation

2. test_correctness_CSEPass_Mutation_cpu — Fixed upstream in PyTorch. Root cause: TestFX.setUp was raising on a missing library, leaving torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations = True behind. Even though TestFX.tearDown tried to restore it, unittest skips tearDown when setUp raises. The flag stayed True for the rest of the process, breaking every later test that traces mutating code, including TestCommonPass.test_correctness_CSEPass_Mutation*.
Fix: switch the restore from tearDown (which may be skipped or interrupted) to addCleanup, which runs regardless. See PyTorch PR [link to be added].

Root-cause Analysis

Issue type: core framework bug (upstream test infra)
Fix repo: pytorch
Analyzed at: pytorch@ded21956
Root cause: Two independent defects in test/dynamo/test_modes.py.
(1) test_nested_compile_transformer_with_flex_attention_compiled_layers is
guarded by @unittest.skipUnless(IS_FLEX_ATTENTION_CUDA_PLATFORM_SUPPORTED and not torch.version.hip, ...) (test/dynamo/test_modes.py:1915-1918), so it never
runs on XPU. It was added CUDA-only (#174504 merged), and the XPU port
(#189358 merged, 8c0a67ce3b) extended only the sibling
test_2tier_blockmask_tensor_closure_nested_compile_aot_export
(test/dynamo/test_modes.py:2168-2172).
(2) The reported ValueError: trying to initialize the default process group twice! is not the primary failure. The test calls
dist.init_process_group("fake", ...) (test_modes.py:2074) and only tears it
down via a trailing dist.destroy_process_group() (test_modes.py:2167), which
is skipped whenever the body raises. PyTorch CI runs non-distributed tests with
-x --reruns=2 (test/run_test.py:1357, NUM_PYTEST_RERUNS at
test/run_test.py:115), so the in-process rerun re-enters init_process_group
against the leaked default PG. The rerun's ValueError becomes the final
reported failure and hides the real first-attempt error - which is exactly the
traceback pasted in this issue.
Fix strategy: test/dynamo/test_modes.py only. Extend the skipUnless on
test_nested_compile_transformer_with_flex_attention_compiled_layers with
or IS_FLEX_ATTENTION_XPU_PLATFORM_SUPPORTED, mirroring the sibling test's
already-merged guard; and replace the trailing dist.destroy_process_group()
with self.addCleanup(dist.destroy_process_group) registered right after
init_process_group, so the fake PG is destroyed even when the body raises.

issues.title: [B60][stock PyTorch][XPU] FlexAttention/PagedAttention accuracy regressions vs PVC
issues.body:
## Summary

B60 shows a broad XPU FlexAttention/PagedAttention accuracy regression in stock PyTorch tests. The same tests passed on PVC.

## Failure Category

Numerical accuracy mismatch between compiled output and eager/reference output.

Representative messages:

```text
Compiled FlexAttention is less accurate than eager in fp32
AssertionError: Out Compiled error ... is greater than ref error ... by more than 10.0X
AssertionError: Grad_Query Compiled error ... is greater than ref error ... by more than 10.0X
```

## Scope

- Test suite: stock PyTorch
- Platform comparison: B60 failed or skipped; PVC passed
- Affected rows observed: 119
- Main file: `test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py`

## Representative Failures

```text
test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestFlexAttentionXPU::test_builtin_score_mods_automatic_dynamic_score_mod7_xpu_float16
AssertionError: Compiled error 0.00022216421449210188 is greater than ref error 8.428077824380299e-05 by more than 1.1X

test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestPagedAttentionXPU::test_paged_builtin_score_mods_score_mod1_xpu_float32
AssertionError: False is not true : Out Compiled error 0.00012370378724345263 is greater than ref error 7.14636960574454e-08 by more than 10.0X

test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestFlexAttentionXPU::test_direct_backward_preserves_explicit_buffers_xpu
AssertionError: Grad_Query Compiled error 6.649729377544006e-05 is greater than ref error 3.495429805113324e-08 by more than 10.0X

test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestLearnableBiasesXPU::test_absolute_2d_bias_batch2_head4_seq_len256_headdim16_dtypefloat32_xpu
Skipped: Compiled FlexAttention is less accurate than eager in fp32
```

## Expected Behavior

Compiled XPU FlexAttention/PagedAttention should stay within the expected tolerance and match the PVC result.

## Notes

The failures cover many score modifiers, block sizes, head dimensions, and PagedAttention variants, so this looks like a shared FlexAttention numerical accuracy issue rather than isolated individual tests.

## Full Case List

Total cases: 119

<details>
<summary>Show all 119 cases</summary>

issues.bodyText:
Summary
B60 shows a broad XPU FlexAttention/PagedAttention accuracy regression in stock PyTorch tests. The same tests passed on PVC.
Failure Category
Numerical accuracy mismatch between compiled output and eager/reference output.
Representative messages:
Compiled FlexAttention is less accurate than eager in fp32
AssertionError: Out Compiled error ... is greater than ref error ... by more than 10.0X
AssertionError: Grad_Query Compiled error ... is greater than ref error ... by more than 10.0X

Scope

Test suite: stock PyTorch
Platform comparison: B60 failed or skipped; PVC passed
Affected rows observed: 119
Main file: test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py

Representative Failures
test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestFlexAttentionXPU::test_builtin_score_mods_automatic_dynamic_score_mod7_xpu_float16
AssertionError: Compiled error 0.00022216421449210188 is greater than ref error 8.428077824380299e-05 by more than 1.1X

test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestPagedAttentionXPU::test_paged_builtin_score_mods_score_mod1_xpu_float32
AssertionError: False is not true : Out Compiled error 0.00012370378724345263 is greater than ref error 7.14636960574454e-08 by more than 10.0X

test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestFlexAttentionXPU::test_direct_backward_preserves_explicit_buffers_xpu
AssertionError: Grad_Query Compiled error 6.649729377544006e-05 is greater than ref error 3.495429805113324e-08 by more than 10.0X

test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py::TestLearnableBiasesXPU::test_absolute_2d_bias_batch2_head4_seq_len256_headdim16_dtypefloat32_xpu
Skipped: Compiled FlexAttention is less accurate than eager in fp32

Expected Behavior
Compiled XPU FlexAttention/PagedAttention should stay within the expected tolerance and match the PVC result.
Notes
The failures cover many score modifiers, block sizes, head dimensions, and PagedAttention variants, so this looks like a shared FlexAttention numerical accuracy issue rather than isolated individual tests.

issues.body:
## Summary

B60 shows multiple stock PyTorch XPU Inductor tests where pytest workers crash during setup. The same tests passed on PVC.

## Failure Category

Worker process crash during test setup.

Representative message:

```text
failed on setup with "worker 'gwN' crashed while running ..."
```

## Scope

- Test suite: stock PyTorch
- Platform comparison: B60 error; PVC passed
- Affected rows observed: 9
- Affected areas:
  - `test/inductor/test_torchinductor_opinfo.py`
  - `test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py`
  - `test/inductor/test_torchinductor_strided_blocks.py`

## Representative Failures

```text
test/inductor/test_torchinductor_opinfo.py::TestInductorOpInfoXPU::test_comprehensive_nn_functional_max_pool3d_xpu_float64

failed on setup with "worker 'gw9' crashed while running ..."
```

The tests should complete normally or fail with a Python-level assertion/error. The pytest worker process should not crash.

```text
RuntimeError: tensor does not have a device
```

```text
UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST
```

issues.title: matmul hangs / falls into 50-80x slowdown on XPU once reduction dim k crosses 2**24 (oneDNN JIT GEMM 'Invalid immediate value')
issues.body:
Hi, I'm working on scikit-learn and on benchmarking scikit-learn and some implementation variants (scikit-learn intelex and array API backed scikit-learn). I found this bug during some benchmarks.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch.matmul`/`@` on XPU hangs (no error, no return) for a `(m, k) @ (k, 1)` matmul once `k` crosses `2**24` (16,777,216) for `float64` input - but only for some values of `m`. Verbose oneDNN logging shows the JIT GEMM kernel generator failing repeatedly with `Invalid immediate value` right before the hang, which looks like the actual cause: something derived from `k` (or a stride) doesn't fit in a 24-bit immediate field once `k > 2**24`, and instead of falling back to a different kernel it appears to retry the same failing one indefinitely.

```python
import torch

k = 16_777_217  # 2**24 + 1
m = 2
A = torch.randn(m, k, dtype=torch.float64, device="xpu")
B = torch.randn(k, 1, dtype=torch.float64, device="xpu")
C = A @ B  # hangs
torch.xpu.synchronize()
```

`k = 16,777,216` (`2**24`) completes in ~0.07s; `k = 16,777,217` hangs indefinitely (I killed it after several minutes while investigating).

Sweeping `m` at the same `k = 16,777,217`, the pattern is not monotonic:

| `m` | result |
|---|---|
| 2 | hangs |
| 3 | completes, ~3.57s (vs ~0.07s below the `k` threshold - ~50x slower, but returns) |
| 4 | completes, ~3.58s (consistent across repeats, scales to 5.31s at `k=25_000_000`) |
| 5 | completes, ~3.59s |
| 6 | hangs |
| 7 | hangs |
| 8 | hangs |

So `m=3,4,5` recover (slowly) while `m=2` and `m=6,7,8` hang outright - this looks like oneDNN is selecting different GEMM kernel/tiling implementations depending on `m`, and only some of those code paths hit the bad kernel-generation path.

`float32` does not reproduce at the analogous byte-size boundary: `k = 2**25` and `k = 2**25 + 1` (128 MiB and 128 MiB + 4 bytes, same as the float64 boundary in bytes) both complete in well under 0.1s. So whatever the actual overflowing value is, it isn't simply "total bytes moved" scaled the same way across dtypes.

Verbose log right before the hang (`m=2`, `k=16777217`, float64):

```
onednn_verbose,v1,info,oneDNN v3.12.0 (commit 80afa71049cd69a3df32adcccb623b12cd7baa22)
onednn_verbose,v1,info,gpu,runtime:SYCL
onednn_verbose,v1,info,gpu,engine,0,backend:Level Zero,name:Intel(R) Arc(TM) B390 GPU,driver_version:1.15.38646,binary_kernels:enabled
onednn_verbose,v1,primitive,error,gpu,jit::gemm,Invalid immediate value,src/gpu/intel/gemm/jit/gen_kernel.cpp:1035
onednn_verbose,v1,primitive,error,gpu,jit::gemm,Invalid immediate value,src/gpu/intel/gemm/jit/gen_kernel.cpp:1035
... (repeats, no forward progress)
```

**Nightly:** tried `torch==2.14.0.dev20260803+xpu` - it no longer hangs at any of the `m` values above (all of `m=2..8` now complete, consistently ~3.58-3.63s, vs ~0.04-0.07s below the `k` threshold). So the infinite-retry part seems to already be fixed there, but the underlying ~50-80x slowdown once `k` crosses `2**24` is still present across the board - looks like whatever changed stopped it from retrying forever, not the actual cost of whatever's failing/falling back once the immediate value doesn't fit.

**How I got here:** this showed up as a real hang in `sklearn.linear_model.Ridge` with `array_api_dispatch=True` (`device="xpu"`, torch backend, see array [API support doc]([地址已移除])) on `make_regression(n_samples=25_000_000, n_features=2)`. `Ridge`'s SVD solver computes `U.T @ y` after the SVD, where `U.T` ends up `(2, 25_000_000)`.
Since this was inside an unattended benchmark harness with a multi-minute timeout, letting it run long enough actually took down the GPU's compute engine, not just the one op:

```
kernel: xe 0000:00:02.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs, logical_mask: 0x1, guc_id=28, state=0x3
kernel: xe 0000:00:02.0: [drm] Tile0: GT0: Timedout job: seqno=..., lrc_seqno=..., guc_id=28, flags=0x20 in python [pid]
kernel: xe 0000:00:02.0: [drm] exec queue reset detected
```

### Versions

```
PyTorch version: 2.13.0+xpu
Is debug build: False
CUDA used to build PyTorch: None

OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64)
GCC version: (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0
Python version: 3.12.13 (64-bit runtime)
Python platform: Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
Is XPU available: True
XPU used to build PyTorch: 20260000
Intel GPU driver version:
* libze1: 1.28.6-1~24.04~ppa1
* intel-opencl-icd: 26.22.38646.6-1~24.04~ppa1
Intel GPU models detected:
* [0] _XpuDeviceProperties(name='Intel(R) Arc(TM) B390 GPU', platform_name='Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero V2', type='gpu', device_id=0xB080, driver_version='1.15.38646+6', total_memory=29304MB, is_integrated_gpu=1)

CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra X7 358H, 16 cores
```

(`is_integrated_gpu=1` above - this is a Panther Lake iGPU, `Arc B390` is just the device name string oneDNN/torch report for it, not a discrete card.)

So m=3,4,5 recover (slowly) while m=2 and m=6,7,8 hang outright - this looks like oneDNN is selecting different GEMM kernel/tiling implementations depending on m, and only some of those code paths hit the bad kernel-generation path.
float32 does not reproduce at the analogous byte-size boundary: k = 2**25 and k = 2**25 + 1 (128 MiB and 128 MiB + 4 bytes, same as the float64 boundary in bytes) both complete in well under 0.1s. So whatever the actual overflowing value is, it isn't simply "total bytes moved" scaled the same way across dtypes.
Verbose log right before the hang (m=2, k=16777217, float64):

So the infinite-retry part seems to already be fixed there, but the underlying ~50-80x slowdown once k crosses 2**24 is still present across the board - looks like whatever changed stopped it from retrying forever, not the actual cost of whatever's failing/falling back once the immediate value doesn't fit.

issues.title: SDPA XPU: scaled_dot_product_attention() fail with 'No available kernel'
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two related `TestSDPAAcceleratorXPU` test cases in `test/test_transformers.py` fail on XPU with `RuntimeError: No available kernel. Aborting execution.`. Both tests explicitly force `SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` via `sdpa_kernel(backends=[SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION])` while exercising Grouped Query Attention (GQA, `enable_gqa=True`) combined with either non-zero dropout or non-contiguous/broadcast tensor layouts. On XPU, the efficient-attention path currently rejects these input combinations (dropout, GQA head-count mismatch, and/or the specific memory layouts), so kernel dispatch has no viable backend and aborts.

One MQA related case also have the problem:
test/test_transformers.py::TestSDPAAcceleratorXPU::test_mqa_singleton_head_broadcast_native_cuda_fused_kernel0_xpu



Introduced/exercised via pytorch/pytorch#185115.

#### Case 1: `test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa_dropout_xpu`

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test/test_transformers.py", line 3308, in test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa_dropout
    actual = scaled_dot_product_attention(
RuntimeError: No available kernel. Aborting execution.

To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
    python test/test_transformers.py TestSDPAAcceleratorXPU.test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa_dropout_xpu
```

Captured warnings show every backend being rejected before falling through to `EFFICIENT_ATTENTION`, which itself has no available kernel for this input:

```
UserWarning: Flash attention kernel not used because: ...
UserWarning: Flash Attention does not support non-null attn_mask.
UserWarning: Overrideable attention kernel not used because: ...
UserWarning: Both fused kernels do not support non-zero dropout.
UserWarning: CuDNN attention kernel not used because: ...
UserWarning: XPU don't support SDPA cudnn attention backend.
UserWarning: Memory Efficient attention kernel not used because: ...
UserWarning: For dense input, both fused kernels require query, key and value to have the same num_heads.
  Query.sizes(): [2, 6, 17, 32], Key sizes(): [2, 2, 33, 32], Value sizes(): [2, 2, 33, 24]
```

Relevant test source (`test/test_transformers.py`):

```python
def test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa_dropout(self, device):
    """GQA should preserve query-head dropout and mask semantics."""
    batch, num_query_heads, num_kv_heads = 2, 6, 2
    ...
    with sdpa_kernel(backends=[SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION]):
        actual = scaled_dot_product_attention(
            query, key, value, attn_mask,
            dropout_p=0.2, scale=0.37, enable_gqa=True,
        )
        ...
```

#### Case 2: `test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa_*_num_query_heads_6_num_kv_heads_2_..._q_layout_sequence_sliced_k_layout_batch_expanded_v_layout_padded_xpu_float16`

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test/test_transformers.py", line 3249, in test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa
    actual = scaled_dot_product_attention(
RuntimeError: No available kernel. Aborting execution.

To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
    python test/test_transformers.py TestSDPAAcceleratorXPU.test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa_float16_num_query_heads_6_num_kv_heads_2_is_causal_False_use_attn_mask_False_q_layout_sequence_sliced_k_layout_batch_expanded_v_layout_padded_xpu_float16
```

on pytorch/pytorch#185115.

Relevant test source (`test/test_transformers.py`):

```python
@parametrize(
    "num_query_heads,num_kv_heads,is_causal,use_attn_mask,q_layout,k_layout,v_layout",
    [
        (8, 2, False, True, "padded", "sequence_sliced", "transposed"),
        (8, 4, True, False, "transposed", "offset", "head_sliced"),
        (6, 2, False, False, "sequence_sliced", "batch_expanded", "padded"),
    ],
)
def test_mem_efficient_attention_gqa(self, device, dtype, num_query_heads, num_kv_heads,
                                      is_causal, use_attn_mask, q_layout, k_layout, v_layout):
    query = make_strided_sdpa_input((2, num_query_heads, 16, 32), q_layout, device, dtype)
    key   = make_strided_sdpa_input((2, num_kv_heads, 32, 32), k_layout, device, dtype)
    value = make_strided_sdpa_input((2, num_kv_heads, 32, 16), v_layout, device, dtype)
    ...
    with sdpa_kernel(backends=[SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION]):
        actual = scaled_dot_product_attention(
            query, key, value, attn_mask=attn_mask, is_causal=is_causal, enable_gqa=True,
        )
```

Failing parametrization is the third case: `num_query_heads=6, num_kv_heads=2, is_causal=False, use_attn_mask=False, q_layout="sequence_sliced", k_layout="batch_expanded", v_layout="padded"`, where `make_strided_sdpa_input` produces non-contiguous/broadcast (expanded) strided tensors (see helper in the same file).

### Analysis

Both tests explicitly restrict SDPA to `SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` (no fallback allowed), so any gap in XPU's memory-efficient attention kernel support for GQA + dropout, or for GQA + broadcast/strided (non-contiguous) K/V layouts, surfaces as `No available kernel`. This appears related to known gaps tracked in:
- [地址已移除] (XPU has no `EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` backend / no current plan to add)
- [地址已移除] (memory-efficient attention unsupported on XPU, falls back to math)
- [地址已移除] / PR [地址已移除] (FlashAttention + dropout support)

Filing this separately since these specific parametrized GQA cases (dropout, and strided/broadcast K/V layouts) are not yet explicitly tracked.

issues.title: torch.topk on XPU returns invalid (-1) indices with NaN input at batch size >= ~512
issues.body:
## Summary

`torch.topk` on XPU returns out-of-range indices (`-1`) when the input contains a NaN row and the batch dimension is >= ~512. CPU on the identical seed/input returns valid indices. This is not an alternate/valid NaN-ordering convention — `-1` is never a valid `topk` index, and downstream `gather()` on that index aborts the process via a device-side bounds assert rather than raising a catchable exception.

Likely related to intel/torch-xpu-ops#3777 ("[Triton] torch.topk returns wrong values on XPU", closed without a linked fix) — same op, overlapping version window — but that repro is `[8,8]` float32 with no NaN, so we haven't confirmed it's the identical underlying defect.

## Repro

```python
import torch

torch.manual_seed(0)
go_cpu = torch.randn(512, 32, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
go_cpu[0] = float("nan")

values_cpu, ids_cpu = torch.topk(go_cpu, k=4, dim=-1, sorted=False)
print("CPU row0 ids:   ", ids_cpu[0].tolist())

go_xpu = go_cpu.to("xpu")
values_xpu, ids_xpu = torch.topk(go_xpu, k=4, dim=-1, sorted=False)
print("XPU row0 ids:   ", ids_xpu[0].tolist())

bad = (ids_xpu < 0) | (ids_xpu >= 32)
print("XPU bad_count:  ", bad.sum().item())

try:
    go_cpu.gather(1, ids_xpu.cpu())
    print("CPU gather with XPU's ids: succeeded (unexpected)")
except (IndexError, RuntimeError) as e:
    print("CPU gather with XPU's ids: raised", type(e).__name__, "->", e)

# On XPU, the same gather aborts the process with a device_assert
# (SIGABRT) instead of raising a catchable exception.
go_xpu.gather(1, ids_xpu)
```

## Observed output

```
CPU row0 ids:    [22, 21, 20, 23]
XPU row0 ids:    [0, -1, -1, -1]
XPU bad_count:   3
CPU gather with XPU's ids: raised RuntimeError -> index -1 is out of bounds for dimension 1 with size 32
AssertHandler::printMessage
.../torch-xpu-ops/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ScatterGatherKernels.cpp:233: operator(): global id: [1,0,0], local id: [1,0,0] Assertion `idx_dim >= 0 && idx_dim < index_size_ && "scatter gather kernel index out of bounds"` failed.
```
Process exits with SIGABRT (134).

## Trigger conditions (from further isolation, happy to share the sweep script)

- Requires a NaN row in the input — fully finite inputs (including degenerate all-zero/all-equal ties, and +-Inf) never reproduce, at any batch size tested.
- Requires batch size >= ~512 — fails at 512/1024/2048/4096/8192, passes at 16/64/128/256.
- Reproduces with `sorted=False`; not yet swept for `sorted=True`.

## Environment

- `torch==2.13.0+xpu`
- `triton-xpu==3.7.2`
- Intel Arc Pro B70 (30.3GiB), driver `intel-opencl-icd 26.18.38308.1`
- Does **not** reproduce on `torch==2.12.0+xpu` (older stack, otherwise same environment) — bisected by dependency bump alone, no application-level code changed across the bisect.

## Downstream impact

This corrupts MoE expert routing in vLLM (`grouped_topk()`, used by DeepSeek-V2/V3-style and LiquidAI LFM2 gates) when the router's gating output happens to contain a NaN — the corrupted index is then consumed by a fused Triton kernel doing `gather`, which asserts one step later than the plain-`gather` repro above shows, but from the same root cause. We understand from internal driver-team follow-up that a fix (a loop-strength-reduction wrap-around bug in IGC's shader codegen) has landed internally but is not yet in a public/GA driver release. We have not been able to test our exact repro (bf16, NaN-triggered) against the fixed driver build to confirm it resolves this trigger.

cc @astachowiczhabana
