nodes.bodyText: Internal follow-up on our end: driver/VAL team traced this to a loop-strength-reduction wrap-around bug in IGC codegen, hit by SegmentedGroupRadixSelectPairsFunctor/SegmentedGroupRadixSortPairsFunctor. Fix has landed internally (Intel GSD-12849, status: Implemented) but is not yet in a public/GA driver release as of this writing. We have not been able to test our exact repro (bf16, NaN-triggered) against the fixed driver build to confirm it resolves this specific trigger.

Root cause
Short version: the kernel that computes topk keeps some "empty" slots in a scratch buffer and marks them with the value -infinity and the index -1. It then decides which entries to keep by comparing only the values. Both NaN and a real -infinity input fail that comparison, so the empty slots are never replaced, and the placeholder index -1 gets written out as a real result.
Some background first
torch.topk(x, k) returns the k largest values in each row, and the position (index) of each one. Those indices are the part that matters here, because whatever consumes them will use them to look values up -- for example x.gather(1, indices) in the report.
XPU has three different implementations of topk and picks one at runtime depending on the shape (see TensorTopKKernel.cpp and TensorTopKSbtopkKernel.cpp). The one in this bug is the fastest and most specialised: the "sub-group" kernel, chosen only when k <= 8 and there are many rows. It is in TensorTopKSbtopkKernelImpl.h.
It works like this. A "sub-group" is a batch of 32 work items (lanes) that run in lockstep on the GPU. One sub-group handles one row of your tensor:
The row is split across the 32 lanes. Each lane walks its own chunk and keeps a small sorted list of the best K values it has seen, together with their indices.
The lanes then combine their lists in pairs -- lane 0 with lane 1, then 0 with 2, and so on -- until lane 0 holds the best K for the whole row. That merging step is bitonic_merge().
Lane 0 writes the K values and their indices out.
Where it goes wrong
At the start, every lane's list of K entries is filled with a placeholder, because nothing has been seen yet:
value = -infinity   (or the smallest possible integer, for integer types)
index = -1
The idea is that any real input beats a placeholder and pushes it out. The merge step decides that with a plain comparison on the value alone -- roughly if (their_value > my_value) take theirs.
That is the bug, and it fails in two separate ways:
NaN. By definition, every comparison involving NaN is false. NaN > x is false, NaN < x is false, even NaN == NaN is false. So NaN > -infinity is false, and a NaN never displaces a placeholder.
A real -infinity (or INT_MIN). The placeholder value is not a magic value -- it is a perfectly legal input value. And -infinity > -infinity is also false, because the comparison is strict. So a genuine -infinity in your data cannot displace a placeholder either. No NaN is needed to trigger this bug at all.
When a placeholder survives to the end, lane 0 writes out its index, -1. Now torch.topk has returned -1 as a position in your row. The gather() that follows reads out of bounds, and because a GPU cannot raise a Python exception from inside a kernel, you get the device-side assert / abort in the report instead of a normal error.
Whether you see it depends on how many placeholders are left over, which is why narrow rows fail and wide rows appear fine. Each lane loads several elements at a time (1, 2, 4 or 8, chosen from the dtype and row width), so with a 32-element row and k=4 each lane only ever sees one element and 3 of its 4 slots stay empty. That matches the reported output exactly: indices [0, -1, -1, -1] at 32 columns, and [0, 1, -1, -1] at 64 columns.
The telling detail
The other function in the same file, insert(), already knew about this. It tracked how many slots were filled in a count variable and used it to guard the comparison, and its comment even spells out the all--infinity case:
// ... an input value equal to the sentinel (e.g. all -inf for
// largest=true) would always stop at position K-1 ...
bitonic_merge() never tracked a count and had no equivalent guard. So the buffer was protected while a single lane was filling it, and unprotected the moment two lanes merged. That asymmetry is the whole bug.
The fix is to compare (value, index) pairs rather than values alone: an entry whose index is negative is empty and must lose to everything, and NaN has to be ordered explicitly (PyTorch treats NaN as larger than every real number, so it comes first for largest=True and is excluded for largest=False). Then the same comparison can be used by both insert() and bitonic_merge(), so they cannot disagree again.
The impact is wider than the report
Invalid -1 indices, then an abort. The reported symptom.
Silently wrong values, with no crash. When a NaN fails to displace anything, it is dropped from the result and a smaller real value is promoted in its place. This affects every shape that reaches this kernel, including the wide rows where all the indices look valid. No crash, no warning, just a wrong answer -- arguably worse than the abort.
No NaN required. A row of all -infinity (largest=True), all +infinity (largest=False), or all INT_MIN (int32) reproduces the -1 indices.
Two details in the report worth correcting
This is not an IGC codegen bug. It reproduces on a newer driver (26.22.38646.6) and is fully explained by the SYCL source.
"batch >= 512" is not portable. The real trigger is the threshold that selects this kernel: nsegments >= EU_count * HW_threads_per_EU / 4 in TensorTopKSbtopkKernel.cpp. That is 320 rows on the GPU I tested (160 EUs) and 512 on the reporter's, which is why 512 looked like the magic number. sorted=False and bfloat16 are also incidental -- sorted=True and fp16/fp32/fp64 fail identically.
How it got here (commit history)
8eaa591  2026-04-29  Add subgroup topk kernel for XPU (part1 of #3369) (#3371)
5872efe  2026-05-19  Revert "Add subgroup topk kernel ... (#3371)" (#3707)
9054dac  2026-05-25  Split subgroup topk kernel per-K for parallel AOT compilation (#3683)
6336b4f  2026-05-26  Add single workgroup topk kernel for XPU (part 2 of #3369) (#3372)
d27392a  2026-06-15  Use C++20 bit_ceil/bit_floor instead of hand-rolled helpers (#3950)
ffdf468  2026-08-12  Fix TopK AOT (#4907)
The bug arrived with the kernel itself in #3371 and has never been touched since. Reading the list in order:
#3371 introduced the sub-group kernel, including the value-only comparison in bitonic_merge(). This is the commit that introduced the bug.
#3707 reverted #3371 -- but for an unrelated reason (a build timeout in stock CD), not for this bug.
#3683 re-landed it. The comparison logic is byte-for-byte the same; the only change was splitting the code into per-K files so AOT compilation could run in parallel. So the revert-and-reland did not touch the defect.
#3372 is the interesting one. It added the other new topk kernel (the single-workgroup radix one) and, in passing, "fixes NaN handling in SortingRadixSelect.h TopKTypeConfig::convert" -- mapping NaN to the maximum radix value so it sorts correctly there. So NaN in topk was a known concern one day after #3683 re-landed the sub-group kernel, but only the radix path was fixed and the sub-group kernel was never revisited.
#3950 and #4907 are unrelated cleanups (a C++20 helper swap, and moving kernel properties onto the functor to avoid a JIT recompile).
Since these are all recent, this affects only builds that include #3371 / #3683; anything older routes through the fallback path and is unaffected.
Note on cost
Making the comparison correct is not free -- it adds an index check, and a NaN check for floating-point types, to the innermost loop. Measured on one device across 25 shapes that use this kernel, it costs roughly 11% more time per call (geomean; a few shapes get slightly faster, the worst is about 30% slower). That is still well ahead of the fallback path this kernel replaced, so fixing looks clearly better than reverting, but it is worth knowing before review.

issues.title: [Bug] fp8 scaled_mm_v2 TMA template: NoValidChoicesError on XPU (tensorwise/rowwise scaling)
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`torch.nn.functional.scaled_mm` (fp8 `aten._scaled_mm_v2`) lowering fails to
compile via `torch.compile`/Inductor's max-autotune GEMM path on XPU for both
tensorwise and rowwise scaling with TMA templates. Inductor's autotuner finds
"No choices exist for backend" for `aten._scaled_mm_v2.default` on XPU,
because XPU has no TMA-based (or ATEN fallback) scaled_mm choice registered
for the `max_autotune_gemm_backends` selection, causing a hard
`NoValidChoicesError` instead of falling back to an ATEN implementation.

## Affected Tests

Cases:
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_bfloat16_shape_1024,1024,512_use_fast_accum_False_xpu_bfloat16
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_bfloat16_shape_1024,1024,512_use_fast_accum_True_xpu_bfloat16
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_bfloat16_shape_16,32,32_use_fast_accum_False_xpu_bfloat16
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_bfloat16_shape_16,32,32_use_fast_accum_True_xpu_bfloat16
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_float32_shape_1024,1024,512_use_fast_accum_False_xpu_float32
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_float32_shape_1024,1024,512_use_fast_accum_True_xpu_float32
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_float32_shape_16,32,32_use_fast_accum_False_xpu_float32
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template_float32_shape_16,32,32_use_fast_accum_True_xpu_float32
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_rowwise_scaling_tma_template_shape_1024,1024,512_use_fast_accum_False_xpu
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_rowwise_scaling_tma_template_shape_1024,1024,512_use_fast_accum_True_xpu
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_rowwise_scaling_tma_template_shape_16,32,32_use_fast_accum_False_xpu
op_ut,test/inductor/test_fp8.py,TestFP8LoweringXPU.test_rowwise_scaling_tma_template_shape_16,32,32_use_fast_accum_True_xpu

## Error Message

```
torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: LoweringException: NoValidChoicesError: No choices to select. Provided reason: No choices exist for backend. please consider adding ATEN into max_autotune_gemm_backends config (defined in torch/_inductor/config.py) to allow at least one choice.
  target: aten._scaled_mm_v2.default
  args[0]: TensorBox(StorageBox(
    InputBuffer(name='arg2_1', layout=FixedLayout('xpu:0', torch.float8_e4m3fn, size=[1024, 1024], stride=[1024, 1]))
  ))
  args[1]: TensorBox(StorageBox(
    InputBuffer(name='arg1_1', layout=FixedLayout('xpu:0', torch.float8_e4m3fn, size=[1024, 512], stride=[1, 1024]))
  ))
  ...
  args[9]: torch.bfloat16
  kwargs: {'contraction_dim': [], 'use_fast_accum': False}
```

Additionally, a `UserWarning` is emitted for every case using `use_fast_accum=True`:
```
UserWarning: scaled_mm: fast_accum is not supported in XPU for now. It would
silently set use_fast_accum to false. (Triggered internally at
/__w/pytorch/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/ScaledBlas.cpp:218.)
```

## Traceback

```
pytest_command:
pytest test/inductor/test_fp8.py -k "test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template or test_rowwise_scaling_tma_template" -v

Traceback:
  File "test/inductor/test_fp8.py", line 919, in test_tensorwise_scaling_tma_template
    y_compiled, code = run_and_get_code(
  File ".../torch/_inductor/utils.py", line 2734, in run_and_get_code
    result = fn(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../torch/_dynamo/eval_frame.py", line 1278, in compile_wrapper
    raise e.remove_dynamo_frames() from None
  File ".../torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py", line 1192, in _compile_fx_inner
    raise InductorError(e, currentframe()).with_traceback(
  File ".../torch/_inductor/graph.py", line 1567, in call_function
    raise LoweringException(
  File ".../torch/_inductor/lowering.py", line 524, in wrapped
    out = decomp_fn(*args, **kwargs)
  File ".../torch/_inductor/kernel/mm.py", line 1170, in tuned_scaled_mm_v2
    node, _ = autotune_select_algorithm(name, choices, kernel_inputs.nodes(), layout)
  File ".../torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py", line 4063, in __call__
    raise self.create_no_valid_choices(name, "No choices exist for backend.")
torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: LoweringException: NoValidChoicesError: No
choices to select. Provided reason: No choices exist for backend. please
consider adding ATEN into max_autotune_gemm_backends config (defined in
torch/_inductor/config.py) to allow at least one choice.
  target: aten._scaled_mm_v2.default
Found from :
   File "test/inductor/test_fp8.py", line 888, in linear
    y = torch.nn.functional.scaled_mm(
  File ".../torch/nn/functional.py", line 7236, in scaled_mm
    out = torch._scaled_mm_v2(

Same failure pattern (different lowering line numbers: line 1080/1049 for
test_rowwise_scaling_tma_template) for the rowwise-scaling variant.
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`tuned_scaled_mm_v2` in `torch/_inductor/kernel/mm.py` builds a list of
`choices` for `aten._scaled_mm_v2.default` (TMA-based Triton templates and
ATEN fallback) gated by `max_autotune_gemm_backends`. On XPU, the TMA
template path used for tensorwise/rowwise fp8 scaling produces zero valid
choices (either because XPU is not a supported device for the TMA-based
Triton persistent template, or the ATEN choice is not being added/enabled
for XPU when TMA is selected), so `autotune_select_algorithm` raises
`NoValidChoicesError` instead of falling back to an eager/ATEN
`_scaled_mm_v2` implementation. This means fp8 scaled_mm cannot currently be
compiled via Inductor on XPU at all for these configurations, even though
the eager fp8 `scaled_mm` op itself works (as shown by the `UserWarning`
about `use_fast_accum` being silently disabled on XPU, which comes from the
eager `ScaledBlas.cpp` kernel executing normally). The separate
`use_fast_accum` warning is expected/known XPU behavior (fast_accum
unsupported) and is not itself the cause of the failure.

## Related PyTorch Issues

- None found matching `NoValidChoicesError` for `_scaled_mm_v2` on XPU.

## Related Intel/torch-xpu-ops Issues

- None found (searched "scaled_mm_v2 NoValidChoicesError", "tma_template scaled_mm").

## Versions

Branch: daisyden/inductor (repo: daisyden/pytorch)
Commit: 8f036e818c26e60f0a28fb51e89a5010315a27c3
Platform: linux, Python 3.10.20

issues.title: [Bug] Inductor flop counter reports 0 FLOPs on XPU (get_device_tflops has no non-CUDA fallback)
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`TestSchedulerXPU.test_flop_counter_op` fails on XPU because Inductor's flop
counter reports 0 FLOPs for a compiled `mm` op instead of the expected
non-zero value. The test expects `reference flops == counters`, but on XPU
the recorded flop count is always 0 regardless of dtype.

## Affected Tests

Cases:
op_ut,test/inductor/test_inductor_scheduler.py,TestSchedulerXPU.test_flop_counter_op_options0_xpu_float16
op_ut,test/inductor/test_inductor_scheduler.py,TestSchedulerXPU.test_flop_counter_op_options0_xpu_float32

## Error Message

```
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 0 but got 240.
Absolute difference: 240
Relative difference: inf
op = <built-in method mm of type object at 0x750504f86000> reference flops = 240 != counters 0
```

## Traceback

```
pytest_command:
pytest test/inductor/test_inductor_scheduler.py -k test_flop_counter_op -v

Traceback:
  File "test/inductor/test_inductor_scheduler.py", line 642, in test_flop_counter_op
    self.assertEqual(
  File ".../torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 4844, in assertEqual
    raise error_metas.pop()[0].to_error(  # type: ignore[index]
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 0 but got 240.
Absolute difference: 240
Relative difference: inf
op = <built-in method mm of type object at 0x750504f86000> reference flops = 240 != counters 0

----------------------------- Captured stderr call -----------------------------
.../torch/_dynamo/pgo.py:605: UserWarning: dynamo_pgo force disabled by torch.compiler.config.force_disable_caches
  warn_once(
Autotune Choices Stats:
{"num_choices": 5, "num_triton_choices": 5, "best_kernel": "triton_mm_3", ...}
AUTOTUNE mm(4x5, 5x6)
...
W0807 07:22:23.598000 3197941 site-packages/torch/_inductor/utils.py:3002] [0/0] get_device_tflops: no Triton fallback available for non-CUDA devices. Returning 0.0; roofline estimates will use memory bandwidth only.
I0807 07:22:23.599000 3197941 site-packages/torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py:1784] [0/0] [__inductor_metrics] Graph Metrics:
I0807 07:22:23.599000 3197941 site-packages/torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py:1784] [0/0] [__inductor_metrics] {'num_bytes_accessed': 136, 'nodes_num_elem': [(SchedulerNode(name='op0'), 34)], 'node_runtimes': [(SchedulerNode(name='op0'), 0)]}
```

Both `float16` and `float32` variants fail identically (reference flops = 240,
counters = 0).

## Root Cause Analysis

The warning emitted immediately before the graph metrics are logged is the
key clue: `get_device_tflops: no Triton fallback available for non-CUDA
devices. Returning 0.0; roofline estimates will use memory bandwidth only.`
This is logged from `torch/_inductor/utils.py` (`get_device_tflops`), which
only has a CUDA-specific path for querying device TFLOPS/roofline info via
Triton; for any non-CUDA device (including XPU) it returns `0.0` instead of
querying the actual XPU device's compute throughput. The scheduler's flop
counter for compiled kernels derives its counted FLOPs from this roofline
estimation path, so when `get_device_tflops` returns `0.0` for XPU, the
downstream flop count for the `mm` op is also computed/reported as `0`
instead of the expected `240`. This is a device-generic gap in Inductor's
Triton-based device-info utilities: they assume `is_cuda` and have no XPU
(or other non-CUDA GPU backend) equivalent for querying TFLOPS, so the flop
counter (and other roofline-derived metrics) silently under-report on XPU.

## Related PyTorch Issues

- None found matching `get_device_tflops` non-CUDA fallback for flop counter.

## Related Intel/torch-xpu-ops Issues

- None found (searched "flop_counter", "get_device_tflops flop_counter").

## Versions

Branch: daisyden/inductor (repo: daisyden/pytorch)
Commit: 8f036e818c26e60f0a28fb51e89a5010315a27c3
Platform: linux, Python 3.10.20

issues.title: [Bug] Partitioned scatter memory-budget pass misbehaves on XPU (skip/shared-budget logic)
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`TestPartitionedScatterOpt` memory-budget-aware scatter partitioning tests
fail on XPU. The partitioned-scatter Inductor pass is supposed to gate/limit
how many `index_put`/scatter rewrites it performs based on a computed memory
budget (headroom vs. `total_gpu`), but on XPU it (1) applies a partition even
when the test sets the floor so that headroom should be zero ("no headroom,
pass must skip" but a rewrite still happens), and (2) does not share the
per-invocation budget across multiple scatters in the same graph, rewriting
all 3 scatters when only 1 should fit the configured budget.

## Affected Tests

Cases:
op_ut,test/inductor/test_scatter_optimization.py,TestPartitionedScatterOpt.test_memory_aware_partition_count
op_ut,test/inductor/test_scatter_optimization.py,TestPartitionedScatterOpt.test_memory_budget_shared_across_scatters

## Error Message

```
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 0 but got 1.
Absolute difference: 1
Relative difference: inf
floor=total_gpu: no headroom, pass must skip

AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 1 but got 3.
Absolute difference: 2
Relative difference: 2.0
budget fits one expanded buffer but 3 scatters were rewritten: the per-invocation budget is not shared
```

## Test Code Snippet

```python
# test/inductor/test_scatter_optimization.py:545-586 (test_memory_aware_partition_count)
def test_memory_aware_partition_count(self):
    """
    Verify that live tensor memory constrains num_partitions.
    ...
    Sub-test 1: headroom fits P-1 extra output buffers -> P=4 applied.
    Sub-test 2: floor = total_gpu -> no headroom -> pass skips.
    """
    torch.manual_seed(12)
    N = 11_000_000
    output_size = 10_000_000
    persist_n = 100_000_000

    def f(out, idx, vals, persistent):
        scattered = out.index_put([idx], vals, accumulate=True)
        return scattered + persistent.sum()

    out = torch.zeros(output_size, dtype=torch.float32, device=GPU_TYPE)
    idx = torch.randint(0, output_size, (N,), dtype=torch.int64, device=GPU_TYPE)
    vals = torch.randn(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=GPU_TYPE)
    persistent = torch.randn(persist_n, dtype=torch.float32, device=GPU_TYPE)

    with torch.no_grad():
        expected = f(out, idx, vals, persistent)

    _, total_gpu = torch.xpu.mem_get_info() if GPU_TYPE == "xpu" else torch.cuda.mem_get_info()
    ...

# test/inductor/test_scatter_optimization.py:636-676 (test_memory_budget_shared_across_scatters)
def test_memory_budget_shared_across_scatters(self):
    """
    Several scatters in one graph must share the budget, not each claim it.
    ...
    Three 20 MB scatters here share room for one extra buffer, so exactly
    one may be rewritten.
    """
    torch.manual_seed(13)
    S = 5_000_000
    N = 20_000_000

    def f(out0, out1, out2, idx, vals):
        a = out0.index_put([idx], vals, accumulate=True)
        b = out1.index_put([idx], vals, accumulate=True)
        c = out2.index_put([idx], vals, accumulate=True)
        return a, b, c

    outs = [torch.zeros(S, dtype=torch.float32, device=GPU_TYPE) for _ in range(3)]
    idx = torch.randint(0, S, (N,), dtype=torch.int64, device=GPU_TYPE)
    vals = torch.randn(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=GPU_TYPE)
    args = (*outs, idx, vals)
    ...
```

```
    raise error_metas.pop()[0].to_error(  # type: ignore[index]
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 0 but got 1.

Relative difference: inf
floor=total_gpu: no headroom, pass must skip

    raise error_metas.pop()[0].to_error(  # type: ignore[index]
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 1 but got 3.

I0807 07:30:46.008000 3203240 site-packages/torch/_inductor/compile_fx.py:1784] [0/0] [__inductor_metrics] {'num_bytes_accessed': 4200000000, 'nodes_num_elem': [(SchedulerNode(name='op0'), 80000000), (SchedulerNode(name='op4'), 80000000), (SchedulerNode(name='op8'), 80000000), (FusedSchedulerNode(nodes=op1_op5_op9), 540000000), (FusedSchedulerNode(nodes=op2_op3), 90000000), (FusedSchedulerNode(nodes=op6_op7), 90000000), (FusedSchedulerNode(nodes=op10_op11), 90000000)], 'node_runtimes': [(SchedulerNode(name='op0'), 0), (SchedulerNode(name='op1'), 0), (SchedulerNode(name='op2'), 0), (SchedulerNode(name='op3'), 0), (SchedulerNode(name='op4'), 0)]}
```

## Root Cause Analysis

Both tests use `torch.xpu.mem_get_info()` / `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()`
device-agnostically to compute `total_gpu`, then set
`config.partitioned_scatter_non_model_floor_bytes` to derive a specific
headroom for the partitioned-scatter Inductor pass to reason about. The
logged `node_runtimes` in the `[__inductor_metrics] Graph Metrics` output are
all `0` for every scheduler node on XPU (`'node_runtimes': [(SchedulerNode(...), 0), ...]`),
which is consistent with the `get_device_tflops: no Triton fallback
available for non-CUDA devices. Returning 0.0` warning seen right before it
(same underlying gap as the `get_device_tflops` XPU issue previously filed,
intel/torch-xpu-ops#4853). If the partitioned-scatter pass's memory/headroom
accounting or its cost model uses these zeroed-out per-node runtime
estimates (directly, or as part of a combined memory-bandwidth/compute
roofline heuristic) to decide how many partitions/rewrites fit the budget,
then on XPU the pass's decision logic can diverge from the CUDA-validated
expected behavior:
- Test 1: with a floor set so there should be no headroom at all, the pass
  still performs 1 rewrite instead of skipping (expected 0, got 1).
- Test 2: with a budget sized for exactly 1 of 3 candidate scatters, the
  pass rewrites all 3, i.e. it does not appear to be charging/decrementing a
  shared budget across the multiple candidates evaluated in one graph
  (expected 1, got 3).

These could either be (a) a downstream consequence of zeroed runtime
estimates changing which candidates the cost model considers "worth"
rewriting or how per-candidate cost is compared to the shared budget, or (b)
an independent scatter-partitioning budget-tracking bug that happens to
reproduce here on XPU. Further investigation inside
`torch/_inductor/fx_passes` (partitioned scatter/index_put pass) and its use
of `total_gpu` / `partitioned_scatter_non_model_floor_bytes` /
node runtime-based cost estimates is needed to confirm which.

## Related PyTorch Issues

- None found matching partitioned-scatter memory budget behavior on XPU.

## Related Intel/torch-xpu-ops Issues

- intel/torch-xpu-ops#4853 - Inductor flop counter reports 0 FLOPs on XPU
  (get_device_tflops has no non-CUDA fallback) - same zeroed node-runtime
  signature observed in this issue's captured stderr, possibly related root
  cause.

## Versions

Commit: 8f036e818c26e60f0a28fb51e89a5010315a27c3
Platform: linux, Python 3.10.20
</content>

reproduce here on XPU. Further investigation inside

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

40,338 failures (93.4% of all failures in this run) on WSL (Ubuntu 26.04) in Windows 11 with Intel
PTLP XPU (Intel(R) Graphics [0xb080]) with `RuntimeError: No available kernel. Aborting execution.`
raised by `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention`. Every SDPA backend (flash,
memory-efficient, cuDNN, overrideable) is explicitly rejected via `UserWarning` before the final
`RuntimeError`, and this repeats identically for effectively every parametrized test in
`test_transformers_xpu.py`.

**Possible not-a-bug caveat:** the rejection warnings explicitly list the supported architectures as
`intel_gpu_pvc`, `intel_gpu_pvc_vg`, `intel_gpu_bmg_g21`, `intel_gpu_bmg_g31` — if this machine's
integrated GPU (`0xb080`) isn't one of those, this entire category may be **expected/by-design** for
this hardware rather than a regression, and `test_transformers_xpu.py` may need to be skipped
outright on this platform rather than counted as 40k failures. Recommend confirming this against the
GPU's actual supported feature set before treating it as an actionable kernel gap.

### Affected Test Cases

```
Module breakdown (43,212 total failures in this run; this RC = 40,338 of them):
  test_transformers_xpu.py    — 40,333 failures
  functorch/test_vmap_xpu.py  — 4 failures
  higher_order_ops/test_invoke_subgraph_xpu.py — 1 failure
```

Representative single failure:
```
FAILED test_transformers_xpu.py::<TestClass>::test_flash_atteention_large_bf16_nan_values
```

Full per-test list not enumerated in the source report — see `ut_skip.log` for exact test IDs.

### Reproduction

```
# Installing UT requirements
cd ${PYTORCH_ROOT_DIR}
python -m pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt
python -m pip install pytest pytest-timeout pytest-xdist

# UT skip
cd $PYTORCH_ROOT_DIR/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
export PYTEST_ADDOPTS="-v --timeout 600 --timeout_method=thread -n 1"
```

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

### 🐛 Describe the bug

506 failures (1.2%) on WSL (Ubuntu 26.04) in Windows 11 with Intel PTLP XPU (Intel(R) Graphics
[0xb080]) with `OSError: Could not load this library: .../libtorchbind_test.so`. This is a pure
environment/build issue — the custom TorchBind test extension was never compiled/installed into
this environment, so every test that calls `init_torchbind_implementations()` fails identically.

### Affected Test Cases

```
Module breakdown:
  test_fx_xpu.py                     — 210 failures
  export/test_torchbind_xpu.py       — 86 failures
  export/test_serialize_xpu.py       — 78 failures
  export/test_converter_xpu.py       — 46 failures
  export/test_passes_xpu.py          — 27 failures
  higher_order_ops/test_with_effects_xpu.py — 23 failures
  export/test_draft_export_xpu.py    — 22 failures
  export/test_export_xpu.py          — 11 failures
  functorch/test_control_flow_xpu.py — 3 failures
```

Full per-test list not enumerated in the source report — see `ut_skip.log` for exact test IDs.

### Reproduction

```
# Installing UT requirements
cd ${PYTORCH_ROOT_DIR}
python -m pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt
python -m pip install pytest pytest-timeout pytest-xdist

# UT skip
cd $PYTORCH_ROOT_DIR/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
export PYTEST_ADDOPTS="-v --timeout 600 --timeout_method=thread -n 1"
export PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1
export PYTORCH_ENABLE_XPU_FALLBACK=1
time python run_test_with_skip.py | tee $HOME/ut_skip.log
```

### Error Message

<details>
<summary>ut_skip.log</summary>

```
OSError: .../libtorchbind_test.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
File "torch/testing/_internal/torchbind_impls.py", line 182, in load_torchbind_test_lib
```

nodes.bodyText:
It's duplicate of #4105
This is not WSL specific, in fact it's kind of expected.
If we're testing release XPU wheel, there won't be this library present. It's only built when there is BUILD_TEST flag set to ON - which is not, for the release wheel.
The half-fix already partly applied for the mentioned issue #4105, is to skip the test if this library is not found. This is correct approach, given we want to be able to test release wheel and not fail on a lib which has no right to be bundled inside the wheel.
But the other half of the fix would be to actually introduce a script for building this thin bindings lib against the release wheel, so we actually could test the functionality needing this lib also with the release wheel.

Hi @skedzier, it looks like there are several issues and several people working on the same problem with loading libtorchbind_test.so. There is one issue that explicitly describes the problem with lack of needed libraries in torch-xpu-ops CI (#5590) and one that focuses on the loading problem itself (#4436). As the problem is general and not hardware-specific, can we close this issue and track this problem in both issues mentioned above to avoid duplication? Unless you need this one for tracking purposes.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

[0xb080]) with `RuntimeError: XPU device architecture does not support flash attention. Supported
architectures are: intel_gpu_pvc, intel_gpu_pvc_vg, intel_gpu_bmg_g21, intel_gpu_bmg_g31.`, in

architecture-support gap as Issue 1 (RC-001), surfaced here as a directly-raised error rather than
`No available kernel` — likely expected/by-design for this HW if it isn't one of the listed
architectures.

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

32 failures (<0.1%) on WSL (Ubuntu 26.04) in Windows 11 with Intel PTLP XPU (Intel(R) Graphics
[0xb080]) where the `pytest-xdist` worker crashes outright (no Python exception) while running a
test. 12 distinct modules affected, no two crashes share the same test — no signal/exit-code
captured, consistent with the `multi_head_attention_forward` crash pattern seen in the `extended`
suite (see the separate `extended`-suite issue for that specific, more clearly reproducible crash).

### Affected Test Cases

```
32 worker-crash records spread across 12 distinct modules, no two sharing the same test.
```

Full per-test list not enumerated in the source report — see `ut_skip.log` for exact test IDs
(search for `crashed while running`).

### Reproduction

```
# Installing UT requirements
cd ${PYTORCH_ROOT_DIR}
python -m pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt
python -m pip install pytest pytest-timeout pytest-xdist

# UT skip
cd $PYTORCH_ROOT_DIR/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
export PYTEST_ADDOPTS="-v --timeout 600 --timeout_method=thread -n 1"
export PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1
export PYTORCH_ENABLE_XPU_FALLBACK=1
time python run_test_with_skip.py | tee $HOME/ut_skip.log
```

<summary>ut_skip.log</summary>


🐛 Describe the bug
32 failures (<0.1%) on WSL (Ubuntu 26.04) in Windows 11 with Intel PTLP XPU (Intel(R) Graphics
[0xb080]) where the pytest-xdist worker crashes outright (no Python exception) while running a
test. 12 distinct modules affected, no two crashes share the same test — no signal/exit-code
captured, consistent with the multi_head_attention_forward crash pattern seen in the extended
suite (see the separate extended-suite issue for that specific, more clearly reproducible crash).
Affected Test Cases

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

**This issue bundles 61 distinct, unrelated low-frequency root causes (1-29 occurrences each,
199 failures total, 0.5% of all failures) rather than a single bug.** The source analysis report
groups these together as a "long tail" rather than resolving each individually. It is provided here
as a single tracking placeholder — recommend splitting genuinely actionable causes out into their
own issues (using the raw `ut_skip.log`, or a re-run of the root-cause analyzer with a lower
grouping threshold) before treating this as one thing to fix.

Examples called out in the source report:
- `AssertionError: Original OpInfo is broken` (12 occurrences)
- `NotImplementedError: "dot_xpu_mkl" not implemented for 'Char'/'Byte'` (4 + 4 occurrences)
- Optimizer dtype-mismatch errors (6 + 4 occurrences)
- `ZeroDivisionError` (5 occurrences)
- Various `torch.export`/`dynamo` string-diff assertions (7-8 occurrences each)

### Affected Test Cases

```
199 failures spread across 61 distinct root causes; no single module/test breakdown given at this
aggregation level in the source report.
```

issues.title: [Bug] TestDropoutAlignRandomEager.test_dropout_mask_parity_and_rng_offset_cuda: eager-vs-compiled dropout mask mismatch ~50% on XPU (recurrence of #4851)
issues.body:
## Bug Description

`TestDropoutAlignRandomEager.test_dropout_mask_parity_and_rng_offset_cuda`
fails on XPU. The test asserts that `torch.nn.Dropout` run in eager mode and
the same module wrapped with `torch.compile` produce matching dropout masks
(and matching RNG-offset deltas) when seeded identically. On XPU, only
~49.95% of mask elements agree between eager and compiled output, i.e. the
masks are effectively uncorrelated (random ~50% agreement) rather than
identical, for all three tested dtypes (`float32`, `float16`, `bfloat16`).

## Affected Test

```
op_ut,test/inductor/test_dropout_align_random_eager.py,TestDropoutAlignRandomEager.test_dropout_mask_parity_and_rng_offset_cuda
```

Note: the test method is only defined with a `_cuda` suffix in current
upstream `pytorch/pytorch` source (no `_xpu`-suffixed or generic variant
exists); it runs on XPU because `GPU_TYPE`/`HAS_GPU_AND_TRITON` resolve to
XPU in this environment and the class is gated only by
`requires_gpu()`/`IS_LINUX and HAS_GPU_AND_TRITON`, not by an explicit
CUDA-only check.

## Reproduce

```bash
conda activate pytorch_xpu
cd /tmp   # avoid running from inside the pytorch source checkout (conftest.py double-load issue)
python -m pytest -sv "/home/daisyden/upstream/inductor_agnostic/test/inductor/test_dropout_align_random_eager.py::TestDropoutAlignRandomEager::test_dropout_mask_parity_and_rng_offset_cuda"
```

## Observed Failure (this run)

```
FAILED test/inductor/test_dropout_align_random_eager.py::TestDropoutAlignRandomEager::test_dropout_mask_parity_and_rng_offset_cuda

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test/inductor/test_dropout_align_random_eager.py", line 257, in test_dropout_mask_parity_and_rng_offset_cuda
    self.assertLessEqual(
  File ".../unittest/case.py", line 1238, in assertLessEqual
    self.fail(self._formatMessage(msg, standardMsg))
  File ".../unittest/case.py", line 675, in fail
    raise self.failureException(msg)
AssertionError: 0.5005362033843994 not less than or equal to 0.0001
Dropout mask mismatch ratio too high: 0.50053620

1 failed in 15.03s
```

Measured mismatch ratio: **0.5005362** (threshold is `1e-4`), i.e. eager and
compiled masks agree only at chance level (~50%), for the first dtype
(`float32`) tested in the loop; the assertion fails before later dtypes in
the loop are reached.

## Root Cause Analysis

The test seeds eager and compiled runs identically via `_set_seed(BASE_SEED)`
and expects Inductor's Philox-based RNG to reproduce the same
stream/offset as the eager XPU RNG so that dropout masks match bit-for-bit.
Instead, the compiled-vs-eager mask agreement (~50%) indicates the two paths
are drawing effectively independent/uncorrelated random streams rather than
sharing the same seed/offset contract on XPU. This points to a divergence
between the XPU eager RNG stream and the Inductor-generated (Philox) RNG
offset/seed handling used for compiled dropout on XPU — the same failure
mode already described in #4851 for a set of related tests in this same
file (including this exact test method and error message).

## Context

- **intel/torch-xpu-ops#4851** — "[Bug] TestDropoutAlignRandomEager: compiled
  dropout mask ~50% mismatch vs eager on XPU" was filed for the same failure
  signature (same test method, same `AssertionError: ... not less than or
  equal to 0.0001 / Dropout mask mismatch ratio too high: 0.5005...`) across
  4 test methods in this class. **That issue was closed on 2026-08-09 without
  a linked commit or merged PR** (`gh api .../issues/4851/timeline` shows the
  `closed` event has `commit_id: null`), so the closure does not represent a
  verified fix. This new issue is filed because the bug still reproduces
  locally against the current checkout, per the reproduce steps above.
- **pytorch/pytorch#190237** — "TestDropoutAlignRandomEager: 4 tests fail on
  main" (OPEN). Related context on this test class's general flakiness/known
  issues, though it covers different test methods
  (`test_linear_block_compile_parity_forward/backward`,
  `test_dropout_parity_dynamic_shapes`) which are already `@unittest.skip`'d
  in-file citing that issue. Low relevance to the specific RNG-offset root
  cause here but included for completeness since it is the same test class.

## Environment

```
torch: 2.14.0.dev20260726+xpu
Platform: Linux
Python: 3.10.20
GPU: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1550 (device_id=0xBD5)
Driver: 1.6.33578+57 (Level-Zero, oneAPI Unified Runtime)
Checkout: pytorch/pytorch @ deefeb3bd593d7a810baad416abbd9ce180dd98a (branch daisyden/inductor)
```

label-issue: #4882
Root cause: Inductor's eager-aligned random pass is CUDA-gated (torch/_inductor/fx_passes/replace_random.py:217, torch/_inductor/inductor_prims.py:112-114), so compiled XPU dropout draws an unaligned Philox stream while eager XPU is Philox-correct (torch-xpu-ops src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Dropout.cpp:392-399); the test only executes because the upstream @skipIfXpu was locally deleted (test/inductor/test_dropout_align_random_eager.py HEAD:225).



label
reason

Issue carries the bug label and body reports an AssertionError mask mismatch, not a feature ask.


test_module: ut
Reproduce step runs pytest test/inductor/test_dropout_align_random_eager.py; issue already labeled module: ut.


module: inductor
Failure is on the torch.compile path via Inductor's random lowering (torch/_inductor/fx_passes/replace_random.py:217).


P2
1 UT case, AssertionError: 0.5005362 not less than or equal to 0.0001 without crash.


target_component: pytorch
Fix must generalize replace_random.py:217 / inductor_prims.py:112-114 beyond device.type == "cuda".


need_action: NEED_FIX
pytorch product code owns the fix; upstream @skipIfXpu at HEAD:225 is a skip, not a fix.

issues.title: [Bug]: test_cpu_gpu_parity_nn_ConvTranspose1d_xpu_complex32 fails with Tensor-likes are not close!
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`TestModuleXPU::test_cpu_gpu_parity_nn_ConvTranspose1d_xpu_complex32` fails on XPU
with a CPU-vs-XPU numerical mismatch for `complex32` (chalf).

The CPU and XPU outputs of `nn.ConvTranspose1d` diverge beyond the parity
tolerance: 4 of 50 elements mismatch, with a greatest absolute difference of
`0.005523681640625` against an allowed `1e-05`.

### Reproduce


issues.title: [Bug] GPU monitoring overhead on XPU: fork-based approach causes ~46% latency increase
issues.body:
## Summary

When using `multiprocessing.Process` (fork) for GPU monitoring in benchmarks, XPU inference latency increases by ~46% (~21ms vs ~14ms baseline). Using `threading.Thread` instead eliminates the overhead completely.

## Background

This issue was discovered while investigating GPU monitoring overhead in the [HuggingFace_OOB benchmark framework]([地址已移除]) (see [PR #228]([地址已移除]) for the fix).

The benchmark uses a GPUMonitor class that spawns a child process to collect GPU utilization/memory metrics during inference. On XPU, this caused unexpected ~46% latency overhead.

## Reproducer

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce GPU monitoring overhead on XPU: Process vs Thread.

Environment:
  - Machine: G31 (Intel(R) Graphics [0xe223])
  - Model: facebook/pe-a-frame-large (feature-extraction)
  - Compile: torch.compile(model.forward, mode="default")
  - RSS padding: ~2.3GB (torch.randn(600_000_000))
"""

import argparse
import gc
import subprocess
import time
import statistics
import numpy as np
from multiprocessing import Process, Queue, Pipe
import threading

import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor, is_torch_xpu_available


def _sample_pytorch():
    u = int(torch.xpu.utilization())
    m = torch.xpu.device_memory_used() / 1024**3
    return u, m


class ForkPytorchMonitor:
    """multiprocessing.Process + torch.xpu API."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.process = None
        self.q = Queue()

    def start(self):
        def worker(q):
            try:
                while True:
                    q.put(_sample_pytorch())
                    time.sleep(0.05)
            except:
                pass
        self.process = Process(target=worker, args=(self.q,), daemon=True)
        self.process.start()

    def stop_and_collect(self):
        if self.process is None:
            return []
        self.process.terminate()
        self.process.join(timeout=2.0)
        samples = []
        while not self.q.empty():
            try:
                samples.append(self.q.get_nowait())
            except:
                break
        return samples


class ThreadPytorchMonitor:
    """threading.Thread + torch.xpu API (the fix)."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.thread = None
        self.q = Queue()
        self.stop = threading.Event()

    def start(self):
        def worker():
            while not self.stop.is_set():
                try:
                    self.q.put(_sample_pytorch())
                except:
                    pass
                time.sleep(0.05)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=worker, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()

    def stop_and_collect(self):
        if self.thread is None:
            return []
        self.stop.set()
        self.thread.join(timeout=2.0)
        samples = []
        while not self.q.empty():
            try:
                samples.append(self.q.get_nowait())
            except:
                break
        return samples


MONITORS = {
    "fork-pytorch": ForkPytorchMonitor,
    "thread-pytorch": ThreadPytorchMonitor,
}


def flush_memory(flush_compile=False):
    gc.collect()
    if flush_compile:
        torch._dynamo.reset()
        torch._dynamo.reset_code_caches()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=list(MONITORS.keys()), required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=10)
    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=3)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    device = torch.device("xpu")
    print(f"Device: {torch.xpu.get_device_name(0)}")
    print(f"Mode: {args.mode}")

    model_id = "facebook/pe-a-frame-large"
    print(f"Loading {model_id}...")
    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(device).eval()
    model.forward = torch.compile(model.forward, mode="default", fullgraph=False)

    feature_extractor = getattr(processor, "feature_extractor", processor)
    sample_rate = getattr(feature_extractor, "sampling_rate", None) or 16000
    dummy_audio = np.random.randn(sample_rate * 1).astype(np.float32) * 0.01
    inputs = feature_extractor(
        [dummy_audio], sampling_rate=sample_rate, return_tensors="pt", padding=True,
    )

    inputs = {
        k: v.to(device, dtype=torch.bfloat16) if v.is_floating_point() else v.to(device)
        for k, v in inputs.items()
    }

    rss_pad = torch.randn(600_000_000, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    print(f"Allocated ~2.3GB padding to inflate RSS")

    def timed_forward():
        torch.xpu.synchronize()
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        with torch.no_grad():
            _ = model(**inputs)
        torch.xpu.synchronize()
        elapsed = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000
        flush_memory(flush_compile=False)
        return elapsed

    for _ in range(args.warmup):
        timed_forward()

    t_base = [timed_forward() for _ in range(args.iters)]

    MonitorClass = MONITORS[args.mode]
    t_mon = []
    for _ in range(args.iters):
        mon = MonitorClass()
        mon.start()
        lat = timed_forward()
        mon.stop_and_collect()
        t_mon.append(lat)

    def stats(t):
        return statistics.median(t), statistics.mean(t), statistics.stdev(t)

    mb, ab, sb = stats(t_base)
    mm, am, sm = stats(t_mon)

    print()
    print(f"{chr(39)}Mode{chr(39):<40s} {chr(39)}median{chr(39):>10s} {chr(39)}mean{chr(39):>10s} {chr(39)}std{chr(39):>10s} {chr(39)}overhead{chr(39):>10s}")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"{chr(39)}No monitor (baseline){chr(39):<40s} {mb:>9.2f}ms {ab:>9.2f}ms {sb:>9.2f}ms {chr(39)}---{chr(39):>10s}")
    print(f"{args.mode + chr(32) + chr(39) + chr(40) + chr(116) + chr(101) + chr(115) + chr(116) + chr(41) + chr(39):<40s} {mm:>9.2f}ms {am:>9.2f}ms {sm:>9.2f}ms {(mm / mb - 1) * 100:>+9.1f}%")

    del rss_pad
    flush_memory(flush_compile=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## Results (G31, Intel(R) Graphics [0xe223])

| Mode | Median Latency | Overhead |
|------|----------------|----------|
| No monitor (baseline) | 14.26ms | — |
| fork-pytorch (Process + torch.xpu) | 20.80ms | +46% |
| fork-xpu-smi (Process + xpu-smi) | 21.33ms | +49% |
| thread-pytorch (Thread + torch.xpu) | 14.20ms | ≈0% |

## Fix

The fix is applied in [PR #228]([地址已移除]), changing `framework/hardware_metrics.py`:
- `multiprocessing.Process` → `threading.Thread`
- Use `torch.xpu` in-process API instead of subprocess `xpu-smi`

## Environment

- **Machine**: G31 (Intel(R) Graphics [0xe223])
- **Driver**: 26.22.38646.6
- **PyTorch**: 2.10.0+cu131
- **Model**: facebook/pe-a-frame-large (feature-extraction, batch=1, seqlen=1024, compile mode)

## Issue Summary
Performance regression analysis identified multiple models with significant performance degradation. Models with **Ind Ratio < 0.9** or **Eager Ratio < 0.9** are experiencing more than 10% performance drop compared to baseline targets. Analysis reveals that **Eager mode** is severely affected across most models (70+ models), while **Inductor mode** shows relatively better performance (only ~8 models with issues).

## Problematic Model(s)

### Critical Issues (Ratio < 0.75)

## Analysis

### Affected Ratios Summary
- [x] **Ind Ratio < 0.9** - Inductor performance regression (8 models affected)
- [x] **Eager Ratio < 0.9** - Eager mode performance regression (70+ models affected)

## Environment Information

- **PyTorch Version:** 0163eec5ea4
- **OS:**  Ubuntu 24.04

## Expected Behavior

- Both Inductor and Eager modes should maintain performance within 10% (ratio ≥ 0.9) of baseline targets
- Eager mode should not show 15-30% performance degradation across 60%+ of models
- Models should perform consistently across different dtypes and test suites

## Actual Behavior

- **Eager mode**: 73 out of 115 models (64%) show performance regression of >10%
- **Inductor mode**: Only 8 out of 115 models (7%) show performance regression
- **Severity**: Many affected models show 15-30% performance drops in Eager mode
- **Consistency**: Issues observed across multiple dtypes, suites, and model types

## Reproduction Steps

```bash
cd ../
rm -rf ./benchmark
git clone [地址已移除] benchmark
cd benchmark
git checkout ${TORCHBENCH_COMMIT_ID}
python install.py --continue_on_fail <models>

# Example benchmark commands for critical models
python benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py --performance -d xpu -n10 --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency --inference --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --only <models>

python benchmarks/dynamo/timm_models.py --performance -d xpu -n10 --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency --inference --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --only <models>
```

Affected Ratios Summary

Environment Information

PyTorch Version: 0163eec5ea4
OS:  Ubuntu 24.04

Expected Behavior

Both Inductor and Eager modes should maintain performance within 10% (ratio ≥ 0.9) of baseline targets
Eager mode should not show 15-30% performance degradation across 60%+ of models
Models should perform consistently across different dtypes and test suites

Actual Behavior

Eager mode: 73 out of 115 models (64%) show performance regression of >10%
Inductor mode: Only 8 out of 115 models (7%) show performance regression
Severity: Many affected models show 15-30% performance drops in Eager mode
Consistency: Issues observed across multiple dtypes, suites, and model types

Root cause



Case
Issue
Regression reason




Qwen3-0.6B FP16
Ind: 0.7064 / Eager: 0.7060
Caused by Hugging Face Transformers commit 513146c175a (PR #41251). The change in create_masks_for_generate() returns a raw mask instead of a {layer_type: mask} dictionary for single-layer-type models such as Qwen3, which disables reuse of the implicit is_causal fast path and causes a dense 2D attention mask to be materialized, significantly slowing micro_sdpa.


GPT2ForSequenceClassification AMP BF16
0.6511 (Eager)
Caused by IGC commit ca74c9ad3, which disables LICM for loops with invariant switch dispatch. For the mixed BF16/FP32 Add/Mul + LoadWithCast/StoreWithCast kernels, this introduces 1024 B/thread private memory, making the kernels about 2.3–2.5× slower and causing the GPT2 Eager regression.

Case	Issue	Regression reason
Qwen3-0.6B FP16	Ind: 0.7064 / Eager: 0.7060	Caused by Hugging Face Transformers commit 513146c175a (PR #41251). The change in create_masks_for_generate() returns a raw mask instead of a {layer_type: mask} dictionary for single-layer-type models such as Qwen3, which disables reuse of the implicit is_causal fast path and causes a dense 2D attention mask to be materialized, significantly slowing micro_sdpa.
GPT2ForSequenceClassification AMP BF16	0.6511 (Eager)	Caused by IGC commit ca74c9ad3, which disables LICM for loops with invariant switch dispatch. For the mixed BF16/FP32 Add/Mul + LoadWithCast/StoreWithCast kernels, this introduces 1024 B/thread private memory, making the kernels about 2.3–2.5× slower and causing the GPT2 Eager regression.
GPT2ForSequenceClassification AMP FP16	0.7060 (Eager)	Same root cause: IGC commit ca74c9ad3
hf_Albert AMP BF16	0.6952(Eager)	Same root cause: IGC commit ca74c9ad3

timm_vision_transformer BF16	0.7333(Eager)	Same root cause: IGC commit ca74c9ad3
timm_vision_transformer FP16	0.7410(Eager)	Same root cause: IGC commit ca74c9ad3
convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k BF16	0.7121(Eager)	Caused by BF16/FP32 Add/Mul kernel regression, which introduces 1024 B/thread private memory
convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k FP16	0.7021(Eager)	Caused by BF16/FP32 Add/Mul kernel regression, which introduces 1024 B/thread private memory

Fix:
Qwen3-0.6B FP16 regression can be fixed by [Transformers PR #47019], which fixes the mask return-type contract regression and restores the expected attention-mask behavior.
All the other regressions are caused by the BF16/FP16 mixed-precision elementwise kernel issue triggered by IGC commit ca74c9ad3`. The affected Add/Mul + cast kernels introduce excessive private memory usage (up to 1024 B/thread), leading to significant kernel slowdowns. These regressions can be addressed by @weishi-deng’s torch-xpu-ops PR #5005.

issues.title: [release/2.14][B60] Four Inductor E2E models regress to fail_accuracy while 2.13 passed
issues.body:
## Summary

On B60, PyTorch release/2.14 XPU nightly shows four new Inductor E2E `fail_accuracy` results. The same cases passed with PyTorch release/2.13.

## Environment

- Hardware: B60
- Container: `intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18`
- Target PyTorch: `torch==2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu`
- Target torchvision: `torchvision==0.29.0.dev20260806+xpu`
- Target torchaudio: `torchaudio==2.11.0.dev20260806+xpu`
- Target Triton XPU: `triton-xpu==3.8.0+git1e2d42a0`
- Baseline: PyTorch release/2.13 XPU wheel, same tests passed
- Device: XPU
- Backend: Inductor
- CUDAGraphs: disabled
- Models are not included in pytorch CI or HUD

## Affected Cases

| Suite | Dtype | Mode | Model | Batch size | Result | Key failure |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| `timm_models` | `amp_bf16` | training | `fbnetv3_b` | 8 | `fail_accuracy` | `blocks.0.0.bn1.bias.grad` RMSE exceeds tolerance |
| `torchbench` | `float32` | inference | `detectron2_maskrcnn_r_50_fpn` | 4 | `fail_accuracy` | `pred_masks` / `instances` uint8 mismatch |
| `torchbench` | `float32` | inference | `detectron2_maskrcnn` | 4 | `fail_accuracy` | `pred_masks` / `instances` uint8 mismatch |
| `torchbench` | `bfloat16` | training | `timm_efficientnet` | 4 | `fail_accuracy` | `bn1.bias.grad` RMSE exceeds tolerance |

## Reproducer

```bash
docker run -it -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
  --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --privileged \
  --shm-size=8g intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18 bash

curl -LsSf [地址已移除] | sh
source $HOME/.local/bin/env
uv venv myvenv --python 3.10 --clear
source myvenv/bin/activate
uv pip install pip wheel "setuptools<81"

uv pip install \
  torch==2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu \
  torchaudio==2.11.0.dev20260806+xpu \
  torchvision==0.29.0.dev20260806+xpu \
  triton-xpu==3.8.0+git1e2d42a0 \
  --index-url [地址已移除] --pre

pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"
git clone [地址已移除]
cd pytorch
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

uv pip install pip pandas psutil scipy requests
uv pip install -r .ci/docker/ci_commit_pins/huggingface-requirements.txt
uv pip install timm

git clone [地址已移除]
rsync -avz ./torch-xpu-ops/.ci/benchmarks/ ./benchmarks/dynamo/

git clone [地址已移除] tmp-benchmark
cd tmp-benchmark
python install.py --continue_on_fail fbnetv3_b detectron2_maskrcnn_r_50_fpn detectron2_maskrcnn timm_efficientnet
export PYTHONPATH=${PWD}:${PYTHONPATH}
cd ..
```

Representative single-case commands:

```bash
python benchmarks/dynamo/timm_models.py -d xpu --accuracy --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 \
  --training --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 \
  --disable-cudagraphs --only fbnetv3_b

python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --accuracy --float32 \
  --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 \
  --disable-cudagraphs --only detectron2_maskrcnn_r_50_fpn

python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --accuracy --float32 \
  --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 \
  --disable-cudagraphs --only detectron2_maskrcnn

python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --accuracy --bfloat16 \
  --training --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 \
  --disable-cudagraphs --only timm_efficientnet
```

## Observed Results


Representative failure messages:

```text
fbnetv3_b:
RMSE (res-fp64): 0.01330, (ref-fp64): 0.00232 and shape=torch.Size([16]). res.dtype: torch.float32, multiplier: 3.000000, tol: 0.010000

Accuracy failed: uint8 tensor did not match

RMSE (res-fp64): 0.00024, (ref-fp64): 0.00004 and shape=torch.Size([32]). res.dtype: torch.bfloat16, multiplier: 3.000000, tol: 0.001000
Accuracy failed for key name bn1.bias.grad
```

## Expected Behavior

These four cases should pass accuracy on B60 with PyTorch release/2.14, matching the PyTorch release/2.13 baseline result.

## Notes

- Two failures are training gradient accuracy mismatches in CNN models.
- Two failures are Detectron2 inference mask/instance mismatches in `uint8` outputs.
- `detectron2_maskrcnn_r_50_fpn` and `detectron2_maskrcnn` show the same captured graph counts and failure keys, so they may share the same underlying regression.

nodes.bodyText: I have this issue for timm_efficientnet during pre RC test with torch 2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu on BMG B580 Windows. Test passed in PT2.13
fbnetv3_b: pass on B60 with 0805 nightly. Cannot reproduce.

Bisection results for regression (2.13→2.14)
Root cause: pytorch#190206 — "Canonicalize reciprocal(sqrt(x)) to rsqrt(x), Update Batchnorm decomp"

Commit: d39a02cf8b
Introduced between 2026-07-18 and 2026-07-19 nightly wheels

Affected models and verification



Model
Original (0719)
After revert (0719)




timm_efficientnet (training, bf16)
fail
pass


detectron2_maskrcnn_r_50_fpn (inference, fp32)
fail
pass


detectron2_maskrcnn (inference, fp32)
fail
pass



All 3 models share the same root cause.
Fix: revert both changes together
1. Post-grad peephole — disable
File: torch/_inductor/fx_passes/post_grad.py
Line: match.replace_by_example(repl, [x]) (inside reciprocal_sqrt_to_rsqrt)
    # DISABLED for XPU acc: match.replace_by_example(repl, [x])

This replaces reciprocal(sqrt(x)) with rsqrt(x) globally, including training paths, where rsqrt has lower precision on XPU B60.
2. BN decomp inference path — revert
File: torch/_decomp/decompositions.py, line ~2128
-        invstd = torch.rsqrt(running_var + eps)
+        invstd = 1 / torch.sqrt(running_var + eps)
This affects the eager reference, so inductor and eager need to match for accuracy checking.
Both changes must be reverted together — reverting either one alone still fails accuracy.
Reproduced on B60 with torch==2.14.0.dev20260719+xpu (confirmed pass on 0718, fail on 0719).
fbnetv3_b: not reproduced on local PyTorch B60. Only reproduced in the container.  Needs more investigation.
fbnetv3_b: caused by 591d39f. With the cast flag, both failed on B60 with release 2.13 and 2.14 nightly. Without the cast flag, both pass. PR: #5035

issues.title: [release/2.14][B60] E2E performance regressions vs 2.13 on XPU (25 configs)
issues.body:
### Summary

Comparing **release/2.14 (target)** vs **release/2.13 (baseline)** E2E dynamo benchmarks on XPU, **25 model configurations** regress in performance (latency ratio < 0.90 on the inductor or eager path).

Ratio = **baseline (2.13) latency / target (2.14) latency**; **< 1.00 means 2.14 is slower**. Absolute latencies are intentionally omitted — ratios only.

## A. Inductor-path regressions (inductor ratio < 0.90) — 14

| Suite | Model | Dtype / Mode | Inductor ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| torchbench | pyhpc_equation_of_state | amp_bf16 / inference | 0.43 |
| torchbench | pyhpc_equation_of_state | amp_fp16 / inference | 0.43 |
| torchbench | functorch_maml_omniglot | amp_bf16 / training | 0.71 |
| timm_models | cait_m36_384 | amp_fp16 / training | 0.71 |
| timm_models | cait_m36_384 | amp_bf16 / training | 0.72 |
| timm_models | convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k | bfloat16 / inference | 0.79 |
| timm_models | convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k | amp_bf16 / inference | 0.80 |
| timm_models | convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k | float16 / inference | 0.81 |
| torchbench | maml_omniglot | amp_fp16 / inference | 0.81 |
| timm_models | convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k | amp_fp16 / inference | 0.81 |
| huggingface | openai/whisper-tiny | amp_bf16 / inference | 0.84 |
| timm_models | cait_m36_384 | float32 / training | 0.84 |
| torchbench | pyhpc_isoneutral_mixing | float16 / inference | 0.86 |
| torchbench | pyhpc_isoneutral_mixing | bfloat16 / inference | 0.89 |

## B. Eager-path regressions (eager ratio < 0.90, inductor ≈ parity) — 11

| Suite | Model | Dtype / Mode | Eager ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| timm_models | jx_nest_base | float16 / inference | 0.75 |
| timm_models | jx_nest_base | bfloat16 / inference | 0.76 |
| timm_models | jx_nest_base | amp_fp16 / inference | 0.76 |
| timm_models | jx_nest_base | amp_bf16 / inference | 0.77 |
| timm_models | jx_nest_base | float32 / inference | 0.86 |
| huggingface | PLBartForConditionalGeneration | float16 / training | 0.88 |
| huggingface | PLBartForConditionalGeneration | bfloat16 / training | 0.89 |
| huggingface | PLBartForConditionalGeneration | amp_fp16 / training | 0.89 |
| huggingface | RobertaForQuestionAnswering | float16 / training | 0.90 |
| huggingface | PLBartForConditionalGeneration | amp_bf16 / training | 0.90 |
| huggingface | BertForQuestionAnswering | float16 / training | 0.90 |

## Light analysis

- **pyhpc_* (equation_of_state, isoneutral_mixing, torchbench)** — elementwise/pointwise-heavy numerical kernels. `equation_of_state` collapses to ~0.43x inductor across AMP dtypes, a large codegen/fusion regression for pointwise-dominated graphs; `isoneutral_mixing` is milder (~0.86-0.89x). Points to an inductor scheduling/fusion change affecting many small pointwise ops.
- **convnextv2_nano (timm, all 4 inference dtypes)** — uniform ~0.79-0.81x inductor regardless of dtype implies a single kernel/lowering regression (conv or norm path), not a dtype-specific issue.
- **cait_m36_384 (timm, training)** — ~0.71-0.84x inductor; attention-heavy ViT, likely an SDPA/attention or backward-fusion regression.
- **jx_nest_base (timm, all inference dtypes)** — eager-only regression (~0.75-0.86x) with inductor at parity → an eager aten/decomposition op change rather than a compiler issue.
- **PLBart / Bert-QA / Roberta-QA (huggingface, training)** — eager-path training regressions (~0.88-0.90x), inductor unaffected → likely an aten op or autograd change on the eager path.
- **openai/whisper-tiny (amp_bf16 inference)** — ~0.84x inductor, consistent with a previously-observed whisper-tiny inductor perf regressor.
- **maml_omniglot / functorch_maml_omniglot (torchbench)** — both inductor and eager regress (~0.71-0.82x); tiny models where launch/dispatch overhead dominates.

## Environment

- Comparison: release/2.14 vs release/2.13, XPU
- Metric: inductor `abs_latency`; ratio = baseline/target latency, dynamo E2E (huggingface + timm + torchbench)
- Absolute latency data omitted per policy; ratios only.

## Reproducer

Environment (release/2.14 XPU nightly under test; baseline is release/2.13 XPU, same commands):

- Container: `intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18`
- Target PyTorch: release/2.14 XPU nightly (e.g. `torch==2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu`)
- Baseline PyTorch: release/2.13 XPU nightly
- Device: XPU · Backend: Inductor · CUDAGraphs: disabled

```bash
docker run -it -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
  --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --privileged \
  --shm-size=8g intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18 bash

curl -LsSf [地址已移除] | sh
source $HOME/.local/bin/env
uv venv myvenv --python 3.10 --clear
source myvenv/bin/activate
uv pip install pip wheel "setuptools<81"

# install the release/2.14 nightly under test (swap to the release/2.13 wheels for the baseline)
uv pip install \
  torch==2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu \
  torchaudio==2.11.0.dev20260806+xpu \
  torchvision==0.29.0.dev20260806+xpu \
  triton-xpu==3.8.0+git1e2d42a0 \
  --index-url [地址已移除] --pre

pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"
git clone [地址已移除]
cd pytorch
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

uv pip install pip pandas psutil scipy requests
uv pip install -r .ci/docker/ci_commit_pins/huggingface-requirements.txt
uv pip install timm

git clone [地址已移除]
rsync -avz ./torch-xpu-ops/.ci/benchmarks/ ./benchmarks/dynamo/

# torchbench models used below
git clone [地址已移除] tmp-benchmark

  pyhpc_equation_of_state pyhpc_isoneutral_mixing maml_omniglot functorch_maml_omniglot
export PYTHONPATH=${PWD}:${PYTHONPATH}
cd ..
```

```bash
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py   -d xpu --performance --bfloat16                  --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only pyhpc_isoneutral_mixing
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py   -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --training  --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only functorch_maml_omniglot
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py   -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype float16  --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only maml_omniglot
python benchmarks/dynamo/timm_models.py  -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --training  --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only cait_m36_384
python benchmarks/dynamo/timm_models.py  -d xpu --performance --bfloat16                  --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only convnextv2_nano.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k
python benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py  -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only openai/whisper-tiny

# B. Eager-path regressions
python benchmarks/dynamo/timm_models.py  -d xpu --performance --float16                   --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only jx_nest_base
python benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py  -d xpu --performance --float16                   --training  --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only PLBartForConditionalGeneration
```

issues.title: Expose allowTF32OneDNN through the public fp32_precision API so XPU TF32 is controllable from device-agnostic code
issues.body:
> [!NOTE]
> The technical body of this issue was drafted with an AI coding assistant and is
> quoted verbatim below. I have reviewed it, independently reproduced the
> measurements on my own Intel GPU system, and verified the code references
> against the PyTorch tree. Filing it because it blocks device-agnostic TF32
> handling in `torch/testing/_internal/` test helpers: helpers whose entire
> purpose is to *guarantee* full fp32 precision are silently no-ops on XPU today,
> so the guarantee holds only by accident of the default value. Happy to move
> this to pytorch/pytorch if that is the better venue -- see the note at the end
> about where the affected files actually live.

---

<details>
<summary>AI-drafted content (reviewed and verified by me)</summary>

### Summary

XPU TF32 is gated by a single private boolean, `Context::allow_tf32_onednn`, which
has no representation in the public `fp32_precision` API. As a result there is no
device-agnostic way to turn TF32 on or off for XPU. I would like XPU TF32 to be
reachable through the same public surface CUDA and MKLDNN already use.

### Current state

The flag itself:

```cpp
// aten/src/ATen/Context.h:512
bool allow_tf32_onednn = false;

// aten/src/ATen/Context.cpp:256
bool Context::allowTF32OneDNN() const {
  return allow_tf32_onednn;
}
```

It is the sole gate for both XPU matmul and XPU convolution:

```cpp
// aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Matmul.cpp:200
if (m1_dt == dnnl::memory::data_type::f32) {
  bool allow_tf32 = at::globalContext().allowTF32OneDNN();
  if (allow_tf32) {
    pattr.set_fpmath_mode(dnnl::fpmath_mode::tf32);
  } else {
    pattr.set_fpmath_mode(dnnl::fpmath_mode::strict);
  }
}
```

```cpp
// aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Utils.cpp:582
void apply_tf32_if_allowed(dnnl::primitive_attr& pattr) {
  auto& ctx = at::globalContext();
  bool allow_tf32 = ctx.allowTF32OneDNN();
  if (allow_tf32) {
    pattr.set_fpmath_mode(dnnl::fpmath_mode::tf32);
  }
}
```

Meanwhile the structured precision registry has no XPU backend at all:

```cpp
// aten/src/ATen/Context.h:48
enum class TORCH_API Float32Backend { GENERIC, CUDA, MKLDNN };
enum class TORCH_API Float32Op { ALL, CONV, RNN, MATMUL };
```

So `allow_tf32_onednn` sits entirely outside the `fp32_precision` inheritance
chain (`backend/op -> backend/ALL -> GENERIC/ALL`).

### The gap, measured

Measured on `torch 2.13.0.dev20260525+xpu`, `torch.xpu.is_available() == True`,
`torch.xpu.is_tf32_supported() == True`. None of the documented generic knobs
reach the XPU flag:

```
--- generic knob effect on XPU oneDNN tf32 bool ---
  backends.fp32_precision='tf32'  -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  backends.fp32_precision='ieee'  -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  backends.fp32_precision='none'  -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False

--- legacy set_float32_matmul_precision effect on XPU ---
  set_float32_matmul_precision('high'   ) -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  set_float32_matmul_precision('highest') -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  set_float32_matmul_precision('medium' ) -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False

--- per-op mkldnn precision does not drive XPU either ---
  mkldnn.matmul.fp32_precision='tf32' -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
```

The only lever that works is the legacy oneDNN boolean:

```
  initial                                : False
  after backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32=True  : True
  after backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32=False : False
```

Also note `torch.backends.xpu` does not exist:

```
  hasattr(torch.backends, "xpu"): False
```

Reproducer:

```python
import torch
assert torch.xpu.is_available()
assert torch.xpu.is_tf32_supported()

for v in ("tf32", "ieee", "none"):
    torch.backends.fp32_precision = v
    print(v, torch._C._get_onednn_allow_tf32())   # always False

for v in ("high", "highest", "medium"):
    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(v)
    print(v, torch._C._get_onednn_allow_tf32())   # always False

print(hasattr(torch.backends, "xpu"))             # False

torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32 = True           # the only lever that works
print(torch._C._get_onednn_allow_tf32())          # True
```

### Why this matters

**1. Device-agnostic test infrastructure silently does nothing on XPU.**

This is what prompted the request. `torch/testing/_internal/` helpers such as
`tf32_off()` / `with_tf32_off` exist to *guarantee* full fp32 precision for tests
that use matmul or convolution incidentally. On XPU they are no-ops, because
every mechanism they could use is one of the ones measured above. A test wrapped
in `with_tf32_off` on XPU still runs with whatever the ambient TF32 state is. It
happens to pass today only because `allow_tf32_onednn` defaults to `false` -- the
guarantee is accidental, not enforced, and would break silently if the default
ever changed or if a preceding test set the flag.

**2. `allow_tf32` is the API being deprecated.**

Routing XPU through `torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32` means depending on the
surface PyTorch is actively moving away from:

> `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32"`
> (`torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True` is going to be deprecated)
>
> -- docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.md:118

**3. The name is misleading.** Controlling an Intel GPU feature via a knob
spelled `mkldnn` (a CPU backend) is confusing in user code and in test
infrastructure alike, and it conflates two unrelated backends: the CPU MKLDNN
`(MKLDNN, MATMUL)` registry entry and the XPU oneDNN boolean are different state
with the same apparent naming lineage.

**4. No per-op granularity.** One boolean covers both matmul and convolution, so
XPU cannot express the matmul-TF32-on / conv-TF32-off combinations that CUDA and
MKLDNN both support via separate `MATMUL` / `CONV` entries.

### Proposal

Add XPU to the structured precision registry and expose it the same way the other
backends are exposed:

1. Add `XPU` to `Float32Backend`.
2. Register `(XPU, ALL)`, `(XPU, MATMUL)`, `(XPU, CONV)` in the `fp32_precision`
   map, defaulting to `NONE` so they inherit via the existing
   `backend/op -> backend/ALL -> GENERIC/ALL` chain.
3. Back `allowTF32OneDNN()` with `float32Precision(Float32Backend::XPU, op)`,
   treating `TF32` as enabled and `IEEE` as disabled, so the oneDNN call sites in
   `Matmul.cpp` / `Utils.cpp` need minimal change.
4. Expose `torch.backends.xpu.matmul.fp32_precision` and
   `torch.backends.xpu.conv.fp32_precision` in Python, mirroring
   `torch.backends.cuda` / `torch.backends.mkldnn`.
5. Keep `torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32` working as a deprecated alias.

The desired end state is that `torch.backends.fp32_precision = "ieee"` disables
TF32 on XPU exactly as it does on CUDA, so one device-agnostic code path is
correct for both.

### Impact

Positive:

- Device-agnostic TF32 helpers become correct on XPU; test infrastructure in
  `torch/testing/_internal/` can cover XPU without an XPU-specific branch.
- XPU aligns with the non-deprecated `fp32_precision` API.
- Per-op (matmul vs conv) control becomes possible on XPU.
- XPU precision state becomes visible to the `TestCase` fp32-precision leak
  detector, which currently tracks six `fp32_precision` flags and cannot see
  `allow_tf32_onednn`.

Risk / compatibility:

- Behavior change risk is low if `(XPU, *)` defaults preserve the current
  `allow_tf32_onednn = false` default. Worth confirming that `NONE` inheriting
  from an unset `GENERIC/ALL` resolves to TF32-off for XPU, so no existing
  workload silently gains TF32.
- `Float32Precision::BF16` is rejected for CUDA; the XPU policy for `bf16` needs a
  decision.
- Adding a `Float32Backend` enumerator touches a `TORCH_API` enum -- ABI-relevant,
  so it likely wants to land with a PyTorch-side change rather than standalone.

</details>

---

One routing note from me: the affected files (`aten/src/ATen/Context.*`,
`aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/`) all live in the pytorch/pytorch tree rather
than in this repo -- as the README notes, XPU conv and gemm are implemented
directly in PyTorch sources. I am filing here for visibility and routing; glad to
refile upstream if maintainers prefer.

Environment: `torch 2.13.0.dev20260525+xpu`, Intel GPU with
`has_subgroup_matrix_multiply_accumulate == True`.
