has no representation in the public fp32_precision API. As a result there is no
device-agnostic way to turn TF32 on or off for XPU. I would like XPU TF32 to be
reachable through the same public surface CUDA and MKLDNN already use.
Current state
The flag itself:
// aten/src/ATen/Context.h:512
bool allow_tf32_onednn = false;

// aten/src/ATen/Context.cpp:256
bool Context::allowTF32OneDNN() const {
  return allow_tf32_onednn;
}
It is the sole gate for both XPU matmul and XPU convolution:
// aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Matmul.cpp:200
if (m1_dt == dnnl::memory::data_type::f32) {
  bool allow_tf32 = at::globalContext().allowTF32OneDNN();
  if (allow_tf32) {
    pattr.set_fpmath_mode(dnnl::fpmath_mode::tf32);
  } else {
    pattr.set_fpmath_mode(dnnl::fpmath_mode::strict);
  }
}
// aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Utils.cpp:582
void apply_tf32_if_allowed(dnnl::primitive_attr& pattr) {
  auto& ctx = at::globalContext();
  bool allow_tf32 = ctx.allowTF32OneDNN();
  if (allow_tf32) {
    pattr.set_fpmath_mode(dnnl::fpmath_mode::tf32);
  }
}
Meanwhile the structured precision registry has no XPU backend at all:
// aten/src/ATen/Context.h:48
enum class TORCH_API Float32Backend { GENERIC, CUDA, MKLDNN };
enum class TORCH_API Float32Op { ALL, CONV, RNN, MATMUL };
So allow_tf32_onednn sits entirely outside the fp32_precision inheritance
chain (backend/op -> backend/ALL -> GENERIC/ALL).
The gap, measured
Measured on torch 2.13.0.dev20260525+xpu, torch.xpu.is_available() == True,
torch.xpu.is_tf32_supported() == True. None of the documented generic knobs
reach the XPU flag:
--- generic knob effect on XPU oneDNN tf32 bool ---
  backends.fp32_precision='tf32'  -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  backends.fp32_precision='ieee'  -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  backends.fp32_precision='none'  -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False

--- legacy set_float32_matmul_precision effect on XPU ---
  set_float32_matmul_precision('high'   ) -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  set_float32_matmul_precision('highest') -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False
  set_float32_matmul_precision('medium' ) -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False

--- per-op mkldnn precision does not drive XPU either ---
  mkldnn.matmul.fp32_precision='tf32' -> _get_onednn_allow_tf32() = False

The only lever that works is the legacy oneDNN boolean:
  initial                                : False
  after backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32=True  : True
  after backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32=False : False

Also note torch.backends.xpu does not exist:
  hasattr(torch.backends, "xpu"): False

Reproducer:
import torch
assert torch.xpu.is_available()
assert torch.xpu.is_tf32_supported()

for v in ("tf32", "ieee", "none"):
    torch.backends.fp32_precision = v
    print(v, torch._C._get_onednn_allow_tf32())   # always False

for v in ("high", "highest", "medium"):
    torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(v)
    print(v, torch._C._get_onednn_allow_tf32())   # always False

print(hasattr(torch.backends, "xpu"))             # False

torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32 = True           # the only lever that works
print(torch._C._get_onednn_allow_tf32())          # True
Why this matters
1. Device-agnostic test infrastructure silently does nothing on XPU.
This is what prompted the request. torch/testing/_internal/ helpers such as
tf32_off() / with_tf32_off exist to guarantee full fp32 precision for tests
that use matmul or convolution incidentally. On XPU they are no-ops, because
every mechanism they could use is one of the ones measured above. A test wrapped
in with_tf32_off on XPU still runs with whatever the ambient TF32 state is. It
happens to pass today only because allow_tf32_onednn defaults to false -- the
guarantee is accidental, not enforced, and would break silently if the default
ever changed or if a preceding test set the flag.
2. allow_tf32 is the API being deprecated.
Routing XPU through torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32 means depending on the
surface PyTorch is actively moving away from:

torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = "tf32"
(torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True is going to be deprecated)
-- docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.md:118

3. The name is misleading. Controlling an Intel GPU feature via a knob
spelled mkldnn (a CPU backend) is confusing in user code and in test
infrastructure alike, and it conflates two unrelated backends: the CPU MKLDNN
(MKLDNN, MATMUL) registry entry and the XPU oneDNN boolean are different state
with the same apparent naming lineage.
4. No per-op granularity. One boolean covers both matmul and convolution, so
XPU cannot express the matmul-TF32-on / conv-TF32-off combinations that CUDA and
MKLDNN both support via separate MATMUL / CONV entries.
Proposal
Add XPU to the structured precision registry and expose it the same way the other
backends are exposed:

Add XPU to Float32Backend.
Register (XPU, ALL), (XPU, MATMUL), (XPU, CONV) in the fp32_precision
map, defaulting to NONE so they inherit via the existing
backend/op -> backend/ALL -> GENERIC/ALL chain.
Back allowTF32OneDNN() with float32Precision(Float32Backend::XPU, op),
treating TF32 as enabled and IEEE as disabled, so the oneDNN call sites in
Matmul.cpp / Utils.cpp need minimal change.
Expose torch.backends.xpu.matmul.fp32_precision and
torch.backends.xpu.conv.fp32_precision in Python, mirroring
torch.backends.cuda / torch.backends.mkldnn.
Keep torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32 working as a deprecated alias.

The desired end state is that torch.backends.fp32_precision = "ieee" disables
TF32 on XPU exactly as it does on CUDA, so one device-agnostic code path is
correct for both.
Impact
Positive:

Device-agnostic TF32 helpers become correct on XPU; test infrastructure in
torch/testing/_internal/ can cover XPU without an XPU-specific branch.
XPU aligns with the non-deprecated fp32_precision API.
Per-op (matmul vs conv) control becomes possible on XPU.
XPU precision state becomes visible to the TestCase fp32-precision leak
detector, which currently tracks six fp32_precision flags and cannot see
allow_tf32_onednn.

Risk / compatibility:

Behavior change risk is low if (XPU, *) defaults preserve the current
allow_tf32_onednn = false default. Worth confirming that NONE inheriting
from an unset GENERIC/ALL resolves to TF32-off for XPU, so no existing
workload silently gains TF32.
Float32Precision::BF16 is rejected for CUDA; the XPU policy for bf16 needs a
decision.
Adding a Float32Backend enumerator touches a TORCH_API enum -- ABI-relevant,
so it likely wants to land with a PyTorch-side change rather than standalone.



One routing note from me: the affected files (aten/src/ATen/Context.*,
aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/) all live in the pytorch/pytorch tree rather
than in this repo -- as the README notes, XPU conv and gemm are implemented
directly in PyTorch sources. I am filing here for visibility and routing; glad to
refile upstream if maintainers prefer.
Environment: torch 2.13.0.dev20260525+xpu, Intel GPU with
has_subgroup_matrix_multiply_accumulate == True.

issues.title: Flaky: test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False (autotune_artifacts count non-deterministic; flaky on 2.13 & 2.14)
issues.body:
### Description

Two unit-test cases in `test/xpu/dynamo/test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py` fail
**intermittently** (random / flaky). Re-running the same selection produces a mix
of all-pass and 1–2 failures, so they are not deterministic regressions.

**The flakiness reproduces on both `2.13` (baseline) and `2.14` (target)** — it is
not introduced by the 2.14 compiler upgrade; it is a pre-existing flaky test.

Both fail on the same assertion at `test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py:225`:

```python
self.assertEqual(len(cache_info.autotune_artifacts), autotune_expect)
```

`autotune_expect` is `2`, but the number of `cache_info.autotune_artifacts`
loaded is non-deterministic across runs — observed **3, 4 and 5**.

### Affected Test Cases

```
test/xpu/dynamo/test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py::AOTAutogradCacheTests::test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False
test/xpu/dynamo/test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py::AOTAutogradCacheBundledTests::test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False
```

### Observed flakiness

Across 11 back-to-back runs of the 2-case selection (on 2.14):

- `2 passed` — 3 runs
- `1 failed, 1 passed` — 7 runs
- `2 failed` — 1 run

Assertion actual values seen: `got 3` (x1), `got 4` (x6), `got 5` (x2) — always
against `Expected 2`. The same intermittent behavior is seen on 2.13.

### Representative failure

```
_ AOTAutogradCacheBundledTests.test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False _
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../test/xpu/dynamo/test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py", line 225, in test_cache_hot_load
    self.assertEqual(len(cache_info.autotune_artifacts), autotune_expect)
  ...
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 2 but got 5.
Absolute difference: 3
Relative difference: 1.5
```

### Reproducer

```bash
docker run -it -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri \
  --group-add video --privileged -v $(realpath ${HOME}):/home/jenkins \
  --shm-size=8g intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18 bash

# python env
curl -LsSf [地址已移除] | sh
source $HOME/.local/bin/env
uv venv myvenv --python 3.10 --clear
source myvenv/bin/activate
uv pip install pip wheel "setuptools<81"

# torch — pick ONE (both reproduce the flakiness):
# baseline 2.13
uv pip install torch==2.13.0 torchaudio torchvision --index-url [地址已移除]
# target 2.14
# uv pip install torch==2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu torchaudio==2.11.0.dev20260806+xpu \
#   torchvision==0.29.0.dev20260806+xpu triton-xpu==3.8.0+git1e2d42a0 \
#   --index-url [地址已移除] --pre

# pytorch source at the matching commit
pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"
git clone [地址已移除]
cd pytorch
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

# unit-test deps
uv pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt
uv pip install -U typing_extensions
uv pip install pytest pytest-timeout pytest-xdist pytest-rerunfailures

# torch-xpu-ops tests
cd third_party/
rm -rf torch-xpu-ops && git clone [地址已移除]
xpu_ops_commit="$(cat xpu.txt)"
cd torch-xpu-ops
git checkout $xpu_ops_commit
cd test/xpu

# run the two cases; re-run several times to reproduce the intermittent failure
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  python -m pytest -v \
    "test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py::AOTAutogradCacheTests::test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False" \
    "test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.py::AOTAutogradCacheBundledTests::test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False"
done
```

### Environment

- Reproduces on both `2.13` (baseline) and `2.14` (target) compiler stacks
- Python 3.10, pytest 7.3.2
- PyTorch with `third_party/torch-xpu-ops`
- Device: Intel XPU
- Platform: Linux (`intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18`)

### Cases

op_ut,test.xpu.dynamo.test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.AOTAutogradCacheTests,test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False
op_ut,test.xpu.dynamo.test_aot_autograd_cache_xpu.AOTAutogradCacheBundledTests,test_cache_hot_load_device_xpu_bfloat16_dynamic_False

issues.title: test_decomp_xpu.py::TestDecompXPU::test_quick_mv_xpu_uint8 - Tensor-likes are not equal! (mv decomposition overflows uint8 instead of saturating)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test_decomp.py::TestDecompXPU::test_quick_mv_xpu_uint8` fails: the `aten.mv` **decomposition** and the **eager** kernel disagree for `uint8` inputs because the two paths handle integer overflow differently. One path wraps modulo 256, the other saturates at 255.

```
FAILED [0.0061s] test_decomp.py::TestDecompXPU::test_quick_mv_xpu_uint8 - Exception: Tensor-likes are not equal!

Mismatched elements: 3 / 5 (60.0%)
Greatest absolute difference: 253 at index (0,)
Greatest relative difference: 126.5 at index (0,)
mv.default
args = (tensor([[2, 2, 5, 0, 3, 9, 9, 7, 8, 8],
        [0, 4, 0, 3, 7, 4, 1, 2, 6, 1],
        [9, 6, 2, 4, 2, 9, 9, 6, 5, 9],
        [2, 4, 8, 4, 0, 4, 6, 0, 8, 4],
        [5, 8, 7, 2, 5, 7, 5, 8, 5, 5]], device='xpu:0', dtype=torch.uint8), tensor([0, 8, 8, 4, 0, 7, 3, 8, 5, 2], device='xpu:0', dtype=torch.uint8))
kwargs = {}

Caused by sample input at index 0: SampleInput(input=Tensor[size=(5, 10), device="xpu:0", dtype=torch.uint8], args=TensorList[Tensor[size=(10,), device="xpu:0", dtype=torch.uint8]], kwargs={}, broadcasts_input=False, name='')

To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
    PYTORCH_OPINFO_SAMPLE_INPUT_INDEX=0 python test/test_decomp.py TestDecompXPU.test_quick_mv_xpu_uint8
```

### Root cause

The `mv` decomposition in [`torch/_decomp/decompositions.py`]([地址已移除]) rewrites the op as an elementwise multiply followed by a reduction:

```python
@register_decomposition(aten.mv)
@out_wrapper(exact_dtype=True)
@pw_cast_for_opmath
def mv(self, vec):
    ...
    return (self * vec).sum(dim=1)
```

`pw_cast_for_opmath` is defined as:

```python
pw_cast_for_opmath = partial(
    type_casts, type_promotion=utils.ELEMENTWISE_TYPE_PROMOTION_KIND.DEFAULT
)
```

With `ELEMENTWISE_TYPE_PROMOTION_KIND.DEFAULT`, `uint8` inputs get a `uint8` computation dtype — the wrapper only widens **floating point** types to an opmath type, it does **not** widen narrow integers to a wider integer accumulator. So the `.sum(dim=1)` result is truncated back into `uint8` and wraps, whereas the eager `mv` kernel accumulates in a wider type and clamps on store.

Verifying with row 0 of the sample input reproduces the reported numbers exactly:

```
row0 = [2, 2, 5, 0, 3, 9, 9, 7, 8, 8]
vec  = [0, 8, 8, 4, 0, 7, 3, 8, 5, 2]

true dot product     = 258      # overflows uint8 (max 255)
wraparound (mod 256) = 2
saturated            = 255

absolute difference  = 255 - 2  = 253     <-- matches "Greatest absolute difference: 253"
relative difference  = 253 / 2  = 126.5   <-- matches "Greatest relative difference: 126.5"
```

No individual product overflows here (all are < 256); only the accumulated sum (258) exceeds the `uint8` range. That is why exactly the rows whose dot product exceeds 255 mismatch — 3 of 5 rows, consistent with the reported 60%.

This is an **upstream, device-agnostic** decomposition/type-promotion issue rather than an XPU kernel bug. It surfaces on XPU because `uint8` is exercised for `mv` in `test_decomp` here; there is no guard for it upstream:

- `CROSS_REF_EXCLUDE_SET` in [`test/test_decomp.py`]([地址已移除]) contains **no** `mv` entry (it only has `uint8` exclusions for `linspace` and some `interpolate`/`upsample_bilinear` variants).
- `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` → `"test_decomp_xpu.py"` currently lists only slow-test skips, nothing for `mv`.

Possibly related but **not** the same root cause: #2439 (`test_quick_addmv_xpu_float64`, oneDNN float accuracy) and #2474 (`test_decomp` accuracy once dtypes were aligned in `op_db`).

### Suggested resolution

Either of:

1. Skip/exclude integer dtypes for `mv` in `test_decomp` upstream (add an `mv` + integral-dtype entry to `CROSS_REF_EXCLUDE_SET`), and/or
2. Fix the decomposition to accumulate in a wider integer dtype for narrow integer inputs so it matches eager overflow semantics.

As a short-term unblock for XPU CI, `test_quick_mv_xpu_uint8` can be added to the `"test_decomp_xpu.py"` entry in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py`.

### Versions

Extracted from the CI log (full `collect_env.py` output not captured in the run):

```

Python: 3.10 (/opt/conda/envs/py_3.10)
Device: xpu:0
Test suite: test_decomp.py (TestDecompXPU)
```

issues.title: [XPU][CI] Random AOTAutograd cache file conflict when tests run in parallel
issues.body:
## Summary

Parallel XPU unit-test runs can randomly fail in `TestAOTAutogradWithCache` because the AOTAutograd local cache hits a file/directory race under `/tmp/torchinductor_root/aotautograd`.

This looks like a cache-concurrency issue rather than a model/test correctness failure: the failure is in cache lookup/save paths, not in the tested operator result.

## Environment

- Repository: `intel/torch-xpu-ops`
- Test file: `test/xpu/functorch/test_aotdispatch_xpu.py`
- Python: 3.10.20
- Parallel runner: pytest-xdist workers observed as `gw1`, `gw6`
- Device: XPU
- Cache root involved: `/tmp/torchinductor_root/aotautograd`

## Failed Tests Observed

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_aotdispatch_xpu.TestAOTAutogradWithCache,test_input_metadata_mutation_aliases
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_aotdispatch_xpu.TestAOTAutogradWithCache,test_input_mutation_simple
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_aotdispatch_xpu.TestAOTAutogradWithCache,test_view_and_inplace_view


## Error 1: save path loses its temp file before rename

```text
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'/tmp/torchinductor_root/aotautograd/ahbntcmukg7wvan4f3tlvm2a2eziyscbykajslcxsshhlecife32/.396194.140128790849344.tmp'
->
'/tmp/torchinductor_root/aotautograd/ahbntcmukg7wvan4f3tlvm2a2eziyscbykajslcxsshhlecife32/x6hp2ydrhpkbvkkez436t5wezm3wjx4yepc2hjc2jy5vsooiu5q'

W0812 13:32:32.134000 396194 torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/autograd_cache.py:1412]
AOTAutograd cache unable to serialize compiled graph: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: ...
```

Relevant stack:

```text
torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/graph_compile.py:2712 in try_save_cache_entry
  AOTAutogradCache.save(...)
torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/autograd_cache.py:1437 in save
  AOTAutogradCache._write_to_local_cache(key, content)
torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/autograd_cache.py:1355 in _write_to_local_cache
  write_atomic(path, content)
torch/_inductor/codecache.py:591 in write_atomic
  tmp_path.rename(target=path)
```

## Error 2: lookup path sees a missing cache subdir

```text
torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='dynamo_compiler' raised:
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
'/tmp/torchinductor_root/aotautograd/aaprgy4cw7hneencncw5xtu4hpotw5tw7f4w7rkzrzibyzck4vzz'
```

Relevant stack:

```text
torch/_functorch/aot_autograd.py:1219 in aot_module_simplified
  compiled_fn, aot_config = AOTAutogradCache.try_load(...)
torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/autograd_cache.py:1085 in try_load
  AOTAutogradCache._lookup(...)
torch/_functorch/_aot_autograd/autograd_cache.py:1306 in _lookup
  AOTAutogradCache.find_guarded_entry(...)
torch/_inductor/codecache.py:1916 in find_guarded_entry
  for candidate, content, in_local in cls.iterate_over_candidates(...)
torch/_inductor/codecache.py:1852 in iterate_over_candidates
  for path in sorted(os.listdir(subdir)):
```

## Light Root Cause Analysis

The failure is consistent with a race in the local AOTAutograd/Inductor cache during parallel test execution:

1. All xdist workers use the shared local cache root under `/tmp/torchinductor_root/aotautograd`.
2. `AOTAutogradCache._write_to_local_cache()` creates a key-specific subdirectory and writes the serialized entry via `write_atomic(path, content)`.
3. `write_atomic()` creates a temp file named from `os.getpid()` and `threading.get_ident()`:

```python
tmp_path = path.parent / f".{os.getpid()}.{threading.get_ident()}.tmp"
```

4. That temp filename is not content-specific or operation-specific. Multiple cache writes from the same process/thread into the same key directory can target the same temp path.
5. On the lookup side, `iterate_over_candidates()` checks `os.path.exists(subdir)` and then calls `os.listdir(subdir)`. If another worker/process removes or replaces that cache subdir between the exists check and listdir, lookup raises `FileNotFoundError`.
6. These cache errors then escape into the test as `FileNotFoundError` / `BackendCompilerFailed`, even though the cache is an optimization and should ideally be best-effort under concurrent access.

## Expected Behavior

Parallel test runs should not fail because of local cache file races. If a local AOTAutograd cache entry is concurrently written, removed, or unreadable, the cache path should be treated as a miss/bypass and the test should continue by recompiling.

## Possible Fix Direction

- Make `write_atomic()` temp filenames unique per write operation, for example by including a UUID/random suffix or using `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, dir=path.parent)`.
- Treat `FileNotFoundError` from `os.listdir(subdir)` as a cache miss in `iterate_over_candidates()`.
- Consider isolating local cache directories per pytest-xdist worker in CI, or disabling the shared local AOTAutograd cache for tests that intentionally exercise cache behavior in parallel.

## Reproducer

Run the XPU AOTAutograd cache tests with pytest-xdist enabled so multiple workers share the same `/tmp/torchinductor_root` cache root. The observed failing workers were `gw1` and `gw6`.

```bash
python -m pytest -n auto -v test/xpu/functorch/test_aotdispatch_xpu.py -k 'TestAOTAutogradWithCache'
```

```python
                    t.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True) for t in (q, k, v)
                )
                result_eager = fwd_bwd_with_sdpa(*eager_inputs)

                for actual, expected in zip(result_with, result_without):

                for actual, expected in zip(result_with, result_eager):
                    self.assertEqual(actual, expected)
                self.assertEqual(sum(self.count_op(gm_with, op) for op in sdpa_ops), 2)
```

issues.body:
## Summary

In the 2.14 BMG (B60) unit-test run, a number of cases were reported by pytest-xdist as `failed on setup with "worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<nodeid>'"`. Each named `<nodeid>` was **re-run individually** on BMG with a hard 11-minute (660s) cap; the following **20 cases still hang past 10 minutes** (killed at 660s), i.e. they are genuine timeouts that take down the xdist worker and cause collateral setup failures for other cases on the same worker.

## Environment

- `torch 2.14.0.dev+xpu`, BMG (B60), 8 GPUs
- `PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1`

## Reproducer

```bash
cd pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
export PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1
ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0 pytest <nodeid>   # hangs > 10 min
```

## Verified timeout cases (killed at 660s)

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_indexing_xpu.TestIndexingXPU,test_index_add_fast_path_xpu_float64

## Notes

- The hangs are often **dtype-specific**: e.g. `test_binary_operation_mul_SparseBSR_xpu_float64` and `test_fn_gradgrad_stft_xpu_float64` complete quickly, while their `complex128` variants hang. This points at slow/hanging `complex128` (and some `float64`) paths in sparse mul, `index_select`/`to_sparse`, linalg low-rank/`lobpcg`, `stft` grad, and `multi_head_attention` forward.
- The other cases named in the same worker-crash messages were verified as **not** timeouts (they pass, fail fast, or crash for other reasons) and are excluded here.

issues.title: XPU enable_timing events (submit_profiling_tag) serialize concurrent streams
issues.body:
### Summary
`test_side_stream_backward_overlap_xpu` (from `test/test_autograd.py`, class `TestAutogradStreamSynchronizationXPU`) cannot pass on XPU because recording `torch.Event(enable_timing=True)` serializes otherwise-concurrent streams. This test is currently marked as skipp** via `skip_list_common.py` - in [地址已移除] This issue was split out from #3243 (where the original sleep dependency #1986 was resolved and the correctness stream-sync tests were enabled on XPU).

**This issue should be started after [地址已移除] and [地址已移除] are merged.**

### Background
The test measures whether a slow "side" backward overlaps a fast "main" backward by comparing timing events recorded on the two branches:
main_backward_start.elapsed_time(side_backward_end) > 0


On XPU this is always ~`-0.001 ms` (no overlap).

### Root cause
- Independent XPU streams **do** run kernels concurrently (two parallel `_sleep` calls ≈ 1× wall time).
- The autograd engine already assigns the two backward nodes to **distinct** streams (verified; `engine.cpp` / `input_buffer.cpp` are accelerator-generic).
- However, XPU `enable_timing` events use `sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::submit_profiling_tag()` in `c10/xpu/XPUEvent.h`, which behaves as a device-wide serialization point. Recording these events forces the concurrent streams to serialize, so the overlap being measured disappears.

Reproduced directly (two-stream sleep workload):
| Variant | Wall time | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| No events | ~704 ms | concurrent |
| Non-timing events (`torch.Event()`) | ~704 ms | concurrent |
| Timing events (`enable_timing=True`) | ~1405 ms | **serialized** |

### Suggested direction
- Preferred: an oneAPI runtime fix so `submit_profiling_tag` does not serialize concurrent queues.
- Alternative (PyTorch side): rework XPU timing events to use per-event profiling (`ext_oneapi_per_event_profiling`) instead of a barrier-style profiling tag, if supported by the device/driver.

### Definition of Done
- The underlying profiling-tag serialization is resolved (runtime and/or `XPUEvent` timing implementation).
- All required code changes are landed.
- **Correctness is verified by unskipping `test_side_stream_backward_overlap_xpu` (remove it from `skip_list_common.py`) and confirming it passes on XPU.**
- No regression in the other `TestAutogradStreamSynchronizationXPU` tests.

### References
- #3243 (parent / full context)
- #1986 (sleep primitive, completed)
- `c10/xpu/XPUEvent.h` (timing event implementation)

Summary
test_side_stream_backward_overlap_xpu (from test/test_autograd.py, class TestAutogradStreamSynchronizationXPU) cannot pass on XPU because recording torch.Event(enable_timing=True) serializes otherwise-concurrent streams. This test is currently marked as skipp** via skip_list_common.py - in #4955. This issue was split out from #3243 (where the original sleep dependency #1986 was resolved and the correctness stream-sync tests were enabled on XPU).
This issue should be started after pytorch/pytorch#193379 and #4955 are merged.
Background
The test measures whether a slow "side" backward overlaps a fast "main" backward by comparing timing events recorded on the two branches:
main_backward_start.elapsed_time(side_backward_end) > 0
On XPU this is always ~-0.001 ms (no overlap).
Root cause

Independent XPU streams do run kernels concurrently (two parallel _sleep calls ≈ 1× wall time).
The autograd engine already assigns the two backward nodes to distinct streams (verified; engine.cpp / input_buffer.cpp are accelerator-generic).
However, XPU enable_timing events use sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::submit_profiling_tag() in c10/xpu/XPUEvent.h, which behaves as a device-wide serialization point. Recording these events forces the concurrent streams to serialize, so the overlap being measured disappears.

Reproduced directly (two-stream sleep workload):



Variant
Wall time
Behavior




No events
~704 ms
concurrent


Non-timing events (torch.Event())
~704 ms
concurrent


Timing events (enable_timing=True)
~1405 ms
serialized



Suggested direction

Preferred: an oneAPI runtime fix so submit_profiling_tag does not serialize concurrent queues.
Alternative (PyTorch side): rework XPU timing events to use per-event profiling (ext_oneapi_per_event_profiling) instead of a barrier-style profiling tag, if supported by the device/driver.

Definition of Done

The underlying profiling-tag serialization is resolved (runtime and/or XPUEvent timing implementation).
All required code changes are landed.
Correctness is verified by unskipping test_side_stream_backward_overlap_xpu (remove it from skip_list_common.py) and confirming it passes on XPU.
No regression in the other TestAutogradStreamSynchronizationXPU tests.

References

#3243 (parent / full context)
#1986 (sleep primitive, completed)
c10/xpu/XPUEvent.h (timing event implementation)

issues.title: Unexpected implicit dependency: removing local code triggers undeclared identifier in ATen XPU headers
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

In our [PR]([地址已移除]) for [地址已移除] we borrowed parts of the comm/ code from torch-xpu-ops. When we remove a helper that appears locally unused (e.g. syclMaxWorkGroupSize), we start seeing an undeclared identifier error originating from PyTorch internal XPU headers (ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BatchKernel.h).

We’re trying to better understand an integration behavior we observed in our repo code and want to make sure we’re following the intended usage from torch-xpu-ops. From our side, this suggests there may be an implicit dependency through include order or symbol visibility, but we may be misunderstanding the expected contract.

Could you please help clarify:

- Is this behavior expected in the current stack, or does it indicate an unintended coupling?
- Should downstream/integration code ever be in a position to satisfy symbols used by upstream internal headers?
- What is the recommended way to avoid this class of dependency when reusing code patterns from torch-xpu-ops?
- Where is the intended public API surface for torch-xpu-ops (Python and/or C++) documented, and which directories (e.g., comm/) should be treated as internal-only implementation details?
- We’d appreciate any pointers so we can align with the intended architecture and avoid fragile integrations going forward.

### Minimal observed reproducible pattern

0. Install uv or other package manager if needed: [地址已移除]
 
1. Clone repo and checkout the PR branch:
```bash
git clone [地址已移除]
cd torchlib-xpu
git checkout 555e902
```

2. Create uv environment:
```bash
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate
```

2. Remove the local helper declaration/definition of `syclMaxWorkGroupSize` from the borrowed `DeviceProperties.h` code.
```bash
sed -i '/^template <class KernelClass>$/,/^}$/d' packages/fbgemm-xpu/src/fbgemm_xpu/fbgemm_utils/comm/DeviceProperties.h
```

3. Build:
```bash
uv pip install -e packages/fbgemm-xpu \
  --index [地址已移除]
```

```
error: use of undeclared identifier 'syclMaxWorkGroupSize'
213 | wg_size = syclMaxWorkGroupSize();
```

🐛 Describe the bug
In our PR for [地址已移除] we borrowed parts of the comm/ code from torch-xpu-ops. When we remove a helper that appears locally unused (e.g. syclMaxWorkGroupSize), we start seeing an undeclared identifier error originating from PyTorch internal XPU headers (ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BatchKernel.h).
We’re trying to better understand an integration behavior we observed in our repo code and want to make sure we’re following the intended usage from torch-xpu-ops. From our side, this suggests there may be an implicit dependency through include order or symbol visibility, but we may be misunderstanding the expected contract.
Could you please help clarify:

Is this behavior expected in the current stack, or does it indicate an unintended coupling?
Should downstream/integration code ever be in a position to satisfy symbols used by upstream internal headers?
What is the recommended way to avoid this class of dependency when reusing code patterns from torch-xpu-ops?
Where is the intended public API surface for torch-xpu-ops (Python and/or C++) documented, and which directories (e.g., comm/) should be treated as internal-only implementation details?
We’d appreciate any pointers so we can align with the intended architecture and avoid fragile integrations going forward.

Minimal observed reproducible pattern

Clone repo and checkout the PR branch:

cd torchlib-xpu

uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate

Remove the local helper declaration/definition of syclMaxWorkGroupSize from the borrowed DeviceProperties.h code.

Build:

nodes.bodyText:
I was unable to reproduce the AssertionError: False is not true on my local XPU machine where test_cpu_annotation_overlap passes there as-is, with no code changes. After analyzing the source code I decided that this does not prove the test is fine, and I root-caused this as (most probably) parity drift from upstream, because currently this test hardcodes:
activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA],
On XPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA is not a supported activity (supported_activities() returns {CPU, XPU}), so requesting it is a no-op and no XPU device activity is captured. The test uses adjust_profiler_step=True, which aligns ProfilerStep boundaries to the captured device activity. With no device activity captured, the steps aren't adjusted around real device work, so under CI timing a ProfilerStep can partially overlap a
step_helper_func annotation — producing:
AssertionError: False is not true
  self.assertTrue(not self._partial_overlap(step_annotation, overlap_step))

Upstream uses device-appropriate activities (get_profiler_activities(device_type)), and the rest of this XPU file already uses supported_activities():
activities=supported_activities(),

Thanks to that the returned values are {CPU, XPU} on XPU which is correct.
As I said before, this failure does not reproduce locally (passes with and without the change), so this is a correctness/parity fix targeting the most plausible cause. Recommend landing and watching CI.

The linked PR: #4970 is currently merged.
As outlined previously: the failure couldn't be reproduced locally and it seems that it failed randomly on CI, thus we wanted to merge the potential fix and watch if this problem re-appears on the CI. The first part is done, so I'm closing this issue (it wasn't closed automatically) so we can see the CI results.

I saw that on couple of builds in my other MRs this problem re-appeared: BUILD1, BUILD2. That being said I'm re-opening this issue in order to wait for my other PR in profiler test to be merged and then check for the final confirmation.

That being said I'm re-opening this issue in order to wait for my other PR in profiler test to be merged and then check for the final confirmation.

My other PR #4969 is merged. Thus I'm closing this issue to see whether the reported problems are fixed and don't appear in the build.
This issue still exists in the latest nightly tests
We are still observing this issue in latest nightly.

I reproduced this issue on BMG and after analyzing the test logic I think that I've found the root cause.
Long story short: the test asserts ProfilerStep and step_helper_func annotations never partially overlap, but this relies heavliy on adjust_profiler_step=True, which from my understanding is now basically a no-op:
FutureWarning: adjust_profiler_step is deprecated and ignored. It will be removed in a future release.

So right now prof.step() ends the current ProfilerStep#N and starts the next one, ProfilerStep#N+1 (more detailed info can be found in profile.step(), torch/profiler/profiler.py). If an annotation is still open at that moment, it spans both steps. The step adjustment mentioned above used to hide/correct this, but since it's no longer applied then this issue started to show up.
That ultimately means that partial overlap with the adjacent step is now expected, not a bug.
I also confirmed it with a script that keeps an annotation open across prof.step() and checks the exported trace for interval intersection:
ProfilerStep events: 5
step_helper_func events: 5
helper[0] overlaps ProfilerStep indices: [0, 1]

issues.title: [BMG] test_mem_get_info fails because free memory is unchanged after allocation
issues.body:
## Summary

On BMG, `test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py::TestCudaMultiGPU::test_mem_get_info` fails because `mem_get_info()` reports the same free-memory value before and after allocating an 8M-element tensor. The test expects `after_free_bytes < before_free_bytes`.

This was captured from `a.txt`.

## Platform

BMG

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.TestCudaMultiGPU,test_mem_get_info


## Repro

From the XPU test directory:

```bash
for i in {1..10}; do pytest -q test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py::TestCudaMultiGPU::test_mem_get_info; done
```

Single-test repro from the failure output:

```bash
python test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py TestCudaMultiGPU.test_mem_get_info
```

## Failure

```text
F [100%]
FAILURES
TestCudaMultiGPU.test_mem_get_info

File "/workspace/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py", line 1125, in test_mem_get_info
    _test(GPU_TYPE)
File "/workspace/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py", line 1118, in _test
    self.assertLess(after_free_bytes, before_free_bytes)
AssertionError: 25325957120 not less than 25325957120
```

## Expected behavior

After allocating the tensor in `test_mem_get_info`, `after_free_bytes` should be lower than `before_free_bytes`.

## Actual behavior

Both values are identical on BMG:

```text
before_free_bytes = 25325957120
after_free_bytes  = 25325957120
```

## Related

A similar open issue exists for the same assertion shape: #4775. This issue tracks the BMG-specific observation from the local repro above.

### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_control_flow_xpu.TestControlFlowTraced,test_while_loop_autograd_simple
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.higher_order_ops.test_invoke_subgraph_xpu.TestInvokeSubgraphCompile,test_different_strides_in_backward
~~op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.profiler.test_profiler_xpu.TestProfiler,test_profiler_cuda_sync_events~~

~~op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.TestCudaMultiGPU,test_mem_get_info~~

## Detailed Failure Analysis

### 1. functorch/test_control_flow_xpu.py

#### test_while_loop_autograd_simple

**Test Class:** `TestControlFlowTraced`

**Error Type:** `AssertionError`

**Error Message:**
```
AssertionError: 'clas[2133 chars]  sub_1: "i64[]" = torch.ops.aten.sub.Tensor(r[1655 chars]1)\n' != 'clas[2133 chars]  sub: "i64[]" = torch.ops.aten.sub.Tensor(rsu[1645 chars]6)\n'
```

**Details:** The test failed due to a graph output mismatch. The expected output has `sub_1` variable name but the actual output has `sub` variable name. This is likely a variable naming inconsistency in the compiled graph output.

**Reproduction Command:**
```bash
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python test/xpu/functorch/test_control_flow_xpu.py TestControlFlowTraced.test_while_loop_autograd_simple
```

---

### 2. higher_order_ops/test_invoke_subgraph_xpu.py

#### test_different_strides_in_backward

**Test Class:** `TestInvokeSubgraphCompile`

**Error Type:** `AssertionError`

**Error Message:**
```
AssertionError: 'clas[2221 chars]  add_15: "f32[]" = torch.ops.aten.add.Tensor([769 chars]s_0)' != 'clas[2221 chars]  add: "f32[]" = torch.ops.aten.add.Tensor(sum[763 chars]s_0)'
```

**Details:** Similar to the first failure, this is a graph output naming mismatch. The expected output has `add_15` but actual has `add`. This indicates inconsistent variable naming in the compiled graph for backward pass with different strides.

**Reproduction Command:**
```bash
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python test/xpu/higher_order_ops/test_invoke_subgraph_xpu.py TestInvokeSubgraphCompile.test_different_strides_in_backward
```

---

### 3. profiler/test_profiler_xpu.py

#### test_profiler_cuda_sync_events

**Test Class:** `TestProfiler`

**Error Type:** `AssertionError`

**Error Message:**
```
AssertionError: False is not true : Expected to find sync event found = {'PyTorch Profiler (0)', 'thread_sort_index', 'process_labels', 'process_sort_index', 'Record Window End', 'aten::add', 'process_name', 'thread_name', 'Iteration Start: PyTorch Profiler'}
```

**Details:** The test expects to find specific CUDA sync events in the profiler output, but the expected events are not being detected. The profiler is only finding basic events like 'PyTorch Profiler', 'aten::add', etc., but missing the CUDA sync-specific events.

**Reproduction Command:**
```bash
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python test/xpu/profiler/test_profiler_xpu.py TestProfiler.test_profiler_cuda_sync_events
```

---

### 4. profiler/test_profiler_xpu.py

#### test_disable_external_correlation

**Test Class:** `TestProfiler`

**Error Type:** `AssertionError`

**Error Message:**
```
AssertionError: False is not true
```

**Assertion:**
```python
self.assertTrue({"gpu_memcpy", "kernel"}.issubset(seen_event_types))
```

**Details:** When external correlation is disabled, the profiler should still detect `gpu_memcpy` and `kernel` event types. The test failure indicates these event types are not being captured properly.

**Reproduction Command:**
```bash
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python test/xpu/profiler/test_profiler_xpu.py TestProfiler.test_disable_external_correlation
```

---

### 5. test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py

#### test_mem_get_info

**Test Class:** `TestCudaMultiGPU`

**Error Type:** `AssertionError`

**Error Message:**
```
AssertionError: 68702699520 not less than 68702699520
```

**Details:** The test checks that memory is properly freed after allocation and deallocation. The failure indicates that `after_free_bytes` is not less than `before_free_bytes`, suggesting either:
- Memory is not being properly released
- The memory measurement is not accurate
- There might be a timing issue with memory statistics

**Reproduction Command:**
```bash
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py TestCudaMultiGPU.test_mem_get_info
```

PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python test/xpu/functorch/test_control_flow_xpu.py TestControlFlowTraced.test_while_loop_autograd_simple

issues.body:
## Summary

BMG XPU UT reported the following non-FFT failures. These cases are tracked separately from the FFT empty-batch issue.

## Affected cases

Cases:
~~op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_aotdispatch_xpu.TestAOTAutogradWithCache,test_input_mutation_metadata2~~

~~op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_masked_xpu.TestMaskedXPU,test_reference_masked_masked_softmin_xpu_float32~~
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_ops_fwd_gradients_xpu.TestFwdGradientsXPU,test_fn_fwgrad_bwgrad_stft_xpu_float64
~~op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_serialization_xpu.TestSerialization,test_serialization_backwards_compat~~


## Error summary

- `TestAOTAutogradWithCache.test_input_mutation_metadata2`: `FileNotFoundError` while atomically writing the AOTAutograd cache temporary file under `/tmp/torchinductor_root/aotautograd/`.
- `TestExecutionTraceXPU.test_execution_trace_env_enabled_with_pt2_xpu`: Inductor `FileNotFoundError` for a generated cache Python file under `/tmp/torchinductor_root/`.
- `TestProfiler.test_basic_chrome_trace`: assertion failure because the trace event name was not `PyTorch Profiler (0)`.
- `TestCommonPass.test_correctness_CSEPass_MutationMetadata_cpu` and `_xpu`: FX rejected tracing `aten::resize_` because it is mutable.
- `TestCommonPass.test_correctness_CSEPass_MutationTorchTensorCall_cpu`: FX rejected tracing mutable `aten::add_.Tensor`.
- `TestMaskedXPU.test_reference_masked_masked_softmin_xpu_float32`: Level Zero returned `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`.
- `TestFwdGradientsXPU.test_fn_fwgrad_bwgrad_stft_xpu_float64`: pytest worker crashed during the test.
- `TestSerialization.test_serialization_backwards_compat`: `EOFError: Ran out of input` while loading the legacy serialization data.

## Reproduction

Run each case from the XPU test directory using the standard `op_ut` command for the corresponding test file and class.

issues.body:
## XPU alignment triage

The daily XPU alignment workflow posts audit summaries and independently reviewed candidates here.

Every run for which the deterministic gate produces a decision posts one Run Summary, separate from any candidate draft:

- `XPU alignment run complete`: collection and review completed without terminal warnings.
- `XPU alignment run completed with warnings`: one or more units were isolated, while the remaining reviewed results are still valid and the workflow stays green.
- `XPU alignment run completed with partial collection`: fetching stopped before every source completed; source progress and the terminal error are reported, trusted candidates may still be published or queued, and the workflow finishes red.
- `XPU alignment run failed`: a malformed artifact, coverage gap, required producer failure, or other global blocker prevents all candidate publication and the workflow finishes red.

A Run Summary is a snapshot of the completed workflow attempt; each candidate draft comment carries the current filing state.

Only terminal conditions that affect the final outcome are shown in the Run Summary. Recovered retries, transient API failures, and internal tool errors remain in workflow logs and artifacts. A scheduled retry updates the existing Summary for the same run ID; duplicate scheduled Summary markers fail closed. Dry runs may post repeated summaries. If the publisher itself or the GitHub Issues API fails, the Actions result and gate artifact are the fallback because a comment cannot be guaranteed.

Formal scheduled drafts may be approved one at a time with:

```text
@torchxpubot file <unit-id>
```

- Run the command on this issue only.
- Only repository `OWNER` or `MEMBER` accounts may approve filing.
- A formal reviewed draft from either a complete scheduled scan or a structurally valid partial scheduled scan can be filed.
- A scheduled run with exactly one reviewed payload may file it automatically, including when collection is structurally valid but partial.
- Partial runs report source progress, last cursor, rate-limit reset, and terminal errors, notify maintainers, and finish red even when trusted candidates were published or queued.
- `[DRY RUN]` drafts are test output, may repeat, never notify, and cannot be filed.
- Malformed artifacts, incomplete stage coverage, core environment failure, or a failed producer job produce only a failed Run Summary and no formal draft.
- A runner-backed blocker for one unit excludes that unit without invalidating other fully reviewed candidates.
- Historical diagnostic comments remain historical evidence and cannot be filed because they do not carry a formal unit marker.
- The bot copies the reviewed formal draft into a new `[xpu-alignment]` issue with exactly the `ai_generated` label.
- A formal unit can be filed successfully only once; the draft is marked with the created issue number.
- No agent runs between approval and issue creation.
- Before approving, check the scan date, workflow run, reproducer, XPU result, independent reviewer verdict, and any incomplete-collection summary.

alignment scan 2026-08-24, run 32923438489
[DRY RUN] [xpu-alignment] embedding_bag per_sample_weights backward indexes weight/grad with unchecked, int-truncated saved indices on XPU
Summary
aten::_embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_backward on XPU indexes grad and weight with the saved indices / offset2bag values without any bounds check, and truncates both to int. Upstream fixed the equivalent CUDA kernel in the 2026-08-24 window; that fix cannot reach this repository, and its regression tests are CUDA-only.
Upstream source

Commit: pytorch/pytorch@550fa84 -- "Fix CUDA illegal memory access in embedding_bag per_sample_weights backward (#193408)"
PR: pytorch/pytorch#193408 (merged)
Issue: pytorch/pytorch#192445 (closed)
Alignment scan window: [2026-08-24T00:00:00Z, 2026-08-25T00:00:00Z), repository pytorch/pytorch

The upstream change to aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/EmbeddingBag.cu does two things. It stops truncating offset2bag[i] and indices[i] with (int) and keeps both at index_t, and it adds CUDA_KERNEL_ASSERT guards for 0 <= bag_idx < num_bags and 0 <= embedding_idx < num_embeddings before those values are used to address grad and weight. Both regression tests it adds to test/nn/test_embedding.py -- test_embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_rejects_invalid_saved_indices and test_embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_large_index -- are decorated @onlyOn(["cuda"]), so nothing exercises XPU.
Target-path evidence
This op is implemented in this repository, so no upstream change reaches it. Line numbers are from intel/torch-xpu-ops main:

src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/EmbeddingBag.cpp:912 -- _embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_backward_kernel
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/EmbeddingBag.cpp:722 -- _embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_backward_impl (called at :952)
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/EmbeddingBag.h:219 -- EmbeddingBagPerSampleWeightsBackwardKernelFunctor

The functor body is the exact pre-fix CUDA code:
// src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/EmbeddingBag.h:233
const int bag_idx = (int)offset2bag_[sample_idx];
const int embedding_idx = (int)indices_[sample_idx];
if (embedding_idx != padding_idx_) {
  for (int feature_idx = sglid; feature_idx < embedding_features_;
       feature_idx += sgSize) {
    result +=
        grad_[grad_stride0_ * bag_idx + grad_stride1_ * feature_idx] *
        weight_[weight_stride0_ * embedding_idx + weight_stride1_ * feature_idx];
  }
}
Neither num_bags nor num_embeddings is passed into the functor, so no bound is even available to check against. The XPU forward kernel does guard its index -- SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT(weight_index < num_row_) at src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/EmbeddingBag.h:104, upper bound only -- which makes the missing backward guard an internal inconsistency as well as a CUDA divergence.
The (int) casts are a second, independent defect: an int64 index at or above 2^31 wraps and addresses the wrong row even when the index is perfectly valid. That is what upstream's test_embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_large_index covers, also CUDA-only.
Observed XPU behavior
Backward with an out-of-range saved indices value completes silently. weight has 5 rows, every saved index is set to 5 (== num_embeddings), and the per-sample-weights gradient is computed from a weight read one row past the allocation. Upstream's post-fix contract is that such an index is rejected by a device-side assertion.
Reproducer
# repro_embedding_bag_psw_backward.py
import subprocess
import sys

import torch

assert torch.xpu.is_available()
assert torch._C._dispatch_has_kernel_for_dispatch_key(
    "aten::_embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_backward", "XPU"
)

CHILD = '''
import torch

weight = torch.ones((5, 2), device="xpu")
indices = torch.zeros(1024, dtype=torch.int64, device="xpu")
offsets = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int64, device="xpu")
per_sample_weights = torch.ones(1024, device="xpu", requires_grad=True)

output, offset2bag, _, _ = torch._embedding_bag(
    weight, indices, offsets, False, 0, False, per_sample_weights
)

# Alias through DLPack so the saved tensor is mutated without bumping its
# autograd version counter, exactly as the upstream CUDA test does.
torch.from_dlpack(indices).fill_(weight.size(0))  # 5 == num_embeddings

output.sum().backward()
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("CLEAN_EXIT")
'''

proc = subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "-c", CHILD], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=35
)
print("exit:", proc.returncode)
print((proc.stdout + proc.stderr).strip())
# Upstream post-fix contract: a device-side assertion naming an index bound.
# On XPU today: exit 0 and CLEAN_EXIT.
The child runs out of process because the expected upstream outcome is a device-side abort that cannot be caught in process, and it calls torch.xpu.synchronize() before printing so an asynchronous device fault would surface before exit.
Observed output
CASE: indices filled with its upper bound (int64)
  child exit=0
  child output: CLEAN_EXIT
REASON: indices: backward completed with an out-of-range saved index, so the XPU kernel indexed memory with it unguarded
VERDICT: SAME_FAILURE

No ALIAS_FALLBACK line appears, so the DLPack alias -- not .data -- mutated the saved tensor and autograd's version counter was not bumped: the value the kernel read really was the saved one.
Scope of the evidence
Only the indices upper-bound int64 case executed; the harness stops at its first failure. The offset2bag case, the negative-bound cases and the int32 cases in upstream's parametrization were not run. Their status here comes from source inspection: bag_idx is equally unguarded, and no lower bound is checked for either index.
One qualification on the signal. A clean exit demonstrates that the invalid index was used unguarded, not that memory outside the USM allocation was touched -- a two-element overread past a 5x2 fp32 buffer will usually stay inside the same page, so a clean run is expected even though the access is out of bounds. The defect is established by the source above; the run corroborates that no assertion exists.
Suggested fix
Mirror the upstream change:

Thread grad.size(0) (num_bags) and weight.size(0) (num_embeddings) from _embedding_bag_per_sample_weights_backward_impl into the functor.
Read offset2bag_[i] and indices_[i] at index_t instead of casting to int, and keep the addressing arithmetic at that width.
Add SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT bounds checks for both indices before the grad_ / weight_ reads.
Add an XPU test covering {indices, offset2bag} x {negative, upper} x {int32, int64}, since upstream's tests are CUDA-only.

Environment

Python: /opt/conda/bin/python3.13, invoked with -I.
torch install: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch, built from /__w/pytorch/pytorch.
torch.xpu.is_available(): true, asserted by the script before the case ran.
torch version and XPU device name: not recorded by the run that produced this evidence. Stated rather than guessed; please confirm against your own build when reproducing.

Provenance
Produced by the xpu-alignment skill in automation mode, and reviewed independently of the scan that produced the local result. Reproducer alignment-run/scripts/repro_commit-550fa843275302768fc1fe758f308b2dccf543b2.py (sha256 6af1ae19088e7db7c2f8b19ef68c2dfb6771e524b41509a471665725c9431bc6), log alignment-run/runner/logs/commit-550fa843275302768fc1fe758f308b2dccf543b2.log.

alignment scan 2026-08-24, run 32923438489
[DRY RUN] [xpu-alignment] XPU group_norm rejects fp32 affine params over an fp16 input, which the shared ATen mixed-dtype contract supports
Summary
XPU group_norm raises RuntimeError: expected scalar type Half but found Float for a reduced-precision input with fp32 affine parameters -- a combination the shared ATen layer explicitly validates and allocates buffers for, and that CPU computes. Root cause: both XPU dispatch stubs template the entire implementation on X.scalar_type(), so the fp32 buffers the shared layer allocated are accessed as the input type.
Upstream source

PR: pytorch/pytorch#194616 -- "Preserve channels_last in InstanceNorm and fix the channels-last group norm reductions at D == 1" (OPEN, unmerged at review time)
Alignment scan window: [2026-08-24T00:00:00Z, 2026-08-25T00:00:00Z), repository pytorch/pytorch

Among other changes, that PR threads a separate parameter type through the CUDA group norm kernels and allocates dgamma / dbeta from param_scalar_type(X, mixed_type) in shared aten/src/ATen/native/group_norm.cpp. Validating its mixed-dtype contract on XPU surfaced a different, pre-existing failure: XPU does not accept the mixed-dtype call at all.
Why this is a defect and not unsupported input
Shared aten/src/ATen/native/group_norm.cpp supports the combination explicitly:
bool mixed_type = is_mixed_type(X, gamma, beta);
if (mixed_type) {
  check_mixed_data_type(X, gamma, beta);
}
...
auto stat_options = X.options()
                        .memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::Contiguous)
                        .dtype(param_scalar_type(X, mixed_type));
Tensor mean = at::empty({N, group}, stat_options);
Tensor rstd = at::empty({N, group}, stat_options);
For an fp16 X with fp32 gamma / beta, the shared layer validates the combination and allocates mean / rstd as fp32 before calling the backend stub.
This is also the ordinary AMP shape rather than an exotic input: group_norm has no autocast cast policy outside MPS -- KERNEL_MPS(group_norm, fp32) is the only entry in aten/src/ATen/autocast_mode.cpp -- so under torch.autocast("xpu") a GroupNorm fed by a preceding fp16 op receives an fp16 activation together with its own fp32 parameters, unchanged.
Root cause and target-path evidence
Line numbers are from intel/torch-xpu-ops main, src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/GroupNormKernels.cpp:

:1379 -- group_norm_kernel: AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND2(kHalf, kBFloat16, X.scalar_type(), ...)
:2445 -- group_norm_backward_kernel: the same, on X.scalar_type() alone
:1042 -- mean.mutable_data_ptr<T>(), the first throw site (mean is fp32 when mixed, T is bound to Half)
:1055, :1717, :2273 -- gamma.const_data_ptr<T>()
:1777, :2401 -- dgamma.mutable_data_ptr<T>()

Because T is bound to the input's scalar type for the whole implementation, mutable_data_ptr<Half>() on the fp32 mean throws, which is exactly the observed message. There is no separate parameter type anywhere in the file.
The target path is established rather than assumed: the reproducer asserts the XPU dispatch key for both aten::native_group_norm and aten::native_group_norm_backward before any call, and every tensor is allocated on xpu.
Reproducer
# repro_group_norm_mixed_dtype.py
import torch

N, C, H, W, G = 2, 6, 4, 4, 3
HXW, EPS = H * W, 1e-5

assert torch.xpu.is_available()
for op in ("aten::native_group_norm", "aten::native_group_norm_backward"):
    assert torch._C._dispatch_has_kernel_for_dispatch_key(op, "XPU"), op


def run(device):
    torch.manual_seed(7)
    x = torch.randn(N, C, H, W, dtype=torch.float32).to(device, torch.float16)
    torch.manual_seed(8)
    gamma = torch.randn(C, dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
    beta = torch.randn(C, dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
    torch.manual_seed(9)
    grad_y = torch.randn(N, C, H, W, dtype=torch.float32).to(device, torch.float16)
    x.requires_grad_(True)
    gamma.requires_grad_(True)
    beta.requires_grad_(True)

    y, mean, rstd = torch.native_group_norm(x, gamma, beta, N, C, HXW, G, EPS)
    dX, dgamma, dbeta = torch.autograd.grad(y, (x, gamma, beta), grad_y)
    if device == "xpu":

Summary
Upstream source: pytorch/pytorch#195343 (open) - [CUDA] fake_quantize_per_channel_affine gives incorrect result for extreme finite float32 input.
Alignment scan window: [2026-08-30T00:00:00Z, 2026-08-31T00:00:00Z) over pytorch/pytorch.
The upstream report is a CPU/CUDA divergence. XPU reproduces the wrong CUDA value bit for bit, and the defective code is the XPU SYCL functor in this repository, so the fix is owned here.
For a per-channel scale of 1e-7 and quant_min = zero_point = -128, the input -3.4028235e38 must saturate to quant_min and dequantize to (-128 - (-128)) * 1e-7 == 0.0. CPU returns 0.0. XPU returns 2.5499999537714757e-05, which is the full quantization span (127 - (-128)) * 1e-7: the value saturated to the wrong end of the range.
Observed XPU behavior
CPU: [[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]]
XPU: [[2.5499999537714757e-05, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]]
CPU bits: ['0x00000000', '0x00000000', '0x00000000', '0x00000000']
XPU bits: ['0x37d5e8d5', '0x00000000', '0x00000000', '0x00000000']
Exact equal: False
upstream cuda first element: 2.5499999537714757e-05
upstream cuda first element bits: 0x37d5e8d5
per-tensor control exact equal: True

The XPU result is bit-identical (0x37d5e8d5) to the CUDA value in the upstream report. The per-tensor variant of the same operation agrees with CPU bit for bit in the same run, which localizes the defect to the per-channel functor rather than to XPU float semantics in general.

x = torch.tensor(
    [[-3.4028235e38, -1.0e-6], [1.0e6, 3.4028235e38]], dtype=torch.float32
)
scale = torch.tensor([1.0e-7, 1.0e20], dtype=torch.float32)
zero_point = torch.tensor([-128, 127], dtype=torch.int32)

cpu = torch.fake_quantize_per_channel_affine(x, scale, zero_point, 0, -128, 127)
xpu = torch.fake_quantize_per_channel_affine(
    x.xpu(), scale.xpu(), zero_point.xpu(), 0, -128, 127
).cpu()

print("CPU:", cpu.tolist())
print("XPU:", xpu.tolist())
print("equal:", torch.equal(cpu, xpu))

# Control: the per-tensor variant agrees with CPU.
print(
    "per-tensor equal:",
    torch.equal(
        torch.fake_quantize_per_tensor_affine(x, 1.0e-7, -128, -128, 127),
        torch.fake_quantize_per_tensor_affine(x.xpu(), 1.0e-7, -128, -128, 127).cpu(),
    ),
)
Target path and root cause
fake_quantize_per_channel_affine_cachemask dispatches CPU, CUDA, XPU to one shared host function, which calls fake_quant_per_channel_cachemask_stub. The XPU stub is registered in src/ATen/native/quantized/FakeQuantizeCore.cpp and implemented by fake_quant_per_channel_cachemask_kernel in src/ATen/native/quantized/sycl/FakeQuantizeCoreKernels.cpp.
FakeQuantPerChannelCachemaskHelperDFunctor::operator() computes:
const float inv_scale = 1.0f / scale;
const auto qval =
    static_cast<int64_t>(sycl::rint(input_val * inv_scale)) + zero_point;
const auto bounded_qval = sycl::clamp(qval, quant_min_, quant_max_);
return (bounded_qval - zero_point) * scale;
-3.4028235e38 * 1e7 overflows float32 to -inf, rint(-inf) is -inf, and the int64_t cast of -inf is undefined; in practice it yields INT64_MIN. Adding zero_point = -128 then wraps to a large positive value, so sycl::clamp saturates to quant_max = 127 instead of quant_min = -128, and the dequantized result becomes (127 - (-128)) * 1e-7 == 2.55e-05. That arithmetic reproduces the observed value exactly.
The multiply-then-cast happens before any clamp, so the saturation the operator promises never gets a chance to run. The contrasting per-tensor functor in the same file adds zero_point inside the float expression and clamps with fminf/fmaxf on floats, which is why the control case survives.
Review note, not an observed result: FakeQuantPerChannelCachemaskHelperCFunctor, which produces the gradient mask, computes qval with the same expression. A fix should cover both functors consistently so the mask and the value stay in agreement.
Suggested direction: clamp in float before the integer cast (saturate rint(input_val * inv_scale) + zero_point to [quant_min, quant_max] while it is still floating point), which keeps -inf and +inf inputs saturating at the correct end.

[xpu-alignment] layer_norm backward flattens dweight/dbias to [N] in the huge-M two-stage arm, breaking multi-dimensional normalized_shape
Summary
native_layer_norm_backward on XPU returns dweight/dbias flattened to [N] instead of normalized_shape whenever the huge-M two-stage column-reduction arm is taken, so the autograd engine rejects the gradient:
RuntimeError: Function NativeLayerNormBackward0 returned an invalid gradient at index 1 - got [8] but expected shape compatible with [2, 4]

The same F.layer_norm(...).backward() call succeeds on CPU with correctly shaped gradients. The element count is right, only the shape is wrong, so this is a pure shape-plumbing defect in torch-xpu-ops.
Upstream source and scan window

Found while checking XPU parity for pytorch/pytorch commit 64417d6eb27cc17a97e8aa2172ffe60f7843fdc4 (PR 193016), "[CUDA] Fix out-of-bounds/invalid-gradient in layer_norm's huge-M gamma/beta backward": pytorch/pytorch@64417d6
Scan window: 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-02T00:00:00Z (half-open, UTC).

The upstream commit fixes a CUDA-only scratch-sizing bug in the same huge-M gamma/beta backward region (CUDA sized its buffers from dgamma->size(-1) instead of N). torch-xpu-ops carries its own implementation of that region and has an independent defect there, so the upstream fix does not apply to XPU code. The XPU run never reached the upstream out-of-bounds signature because it failed earlier on the shape check.
Root cause
native_layer_norm_backward dispatches to layer_norm_backward_xpu for the XPU key (upstream aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml:3293). That function allocates the weight and bias gradients with empty_like(*gamma) / empty_like(*beta), i.e. shaped like normalized_shape (src/ATen/native/xpu/LayerNorm.cpp:148 and :165), then hands pointers to xpu::layer_norm_backward_kernel.
Inside layer_norm_backward_kernel_impl the two-stage column-reduction arm (src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp:1217) is taken when
use_two_stage_col_reduction && M > xe_core_count * 1024 && tile_n < xe_core_count * 2
where tile_n = N / 32 and use_two_stage_col_reduction additionally requires a float/bfloat16/half dtype. That arm accumulates per-tile partials in
dgamma_blocks = at::empty({num_tile_m, N}, options);   // line 1264
dbeta_blocks  = at::empty({num_tile_m, N}, options);   // line 1270
and then rebinds the caller's tensors rather than writing into them:
*dgamma = dgamma_blocks.sum(0);   // lines 1319 and 1365
*dbeta  = dbeta_blocks.sum(0);    // lines 1321 and 1409
sum(0) produces shape [N], discarding the normalized_shape the caller allocated. When normalized_shape is one-dimensional [N] == normalized_shape, so nothing is visibly wrong; with a multi-dimensional normalized_shape the returned gradient has the wrong shape and autograd's shape check fails.
The simple (below-threshold) arm writes in place through dgamma->data_ptr<weight_t>() (line 1051) and therefore preserves the caller's shape. That is why the defect is M-dependent.
Trigger conditions: multi-dimensional normalized_shape AND M > xe_core_count * 1024 AND N / 32 < xe_core_count * 2 AND float32/bfloat16/float16.
Because the existing above-threshold LayerNorm and RMSNorm regression coverage (added with #4790) uses a one-dimensional normalized_shape, it cannot catch this.

Observed XPU behavior
rrelu_with_noise with training=True and a non-contiguous noise view is accepted on

the returned noise are mutually inconsistent: output != where(self >= 0, self, self * noise).

wrong-result bug; it does not depend on PR 196088 landing.

print("noise contiguous:", noise.is_contiguous())
torch._C._nn.rrelu_with_noise(x, noise, 0.1, 0.3, True, None, out=out)
torch.xpu.synchronize()

print("noise elements still holding the sentinel:",
      int((noise == -1.0).sum().item()), "/", noise.numel())
print("noise min/max:", noise.min().item(), noise.max().item())
expected = torch.where(x >= 0, x, x * noise)
print("max |out - where(x >= 0, x, x * noise)|:",
      (out - expected).abs().max().item())

Summary
On XPU, torch.add(a, b, out=out) with strided a and b and a valid sparse CSR out terminates the process with SIGSEGV and no Python-level exception. Upstream CPU raises a catchable (if unpolished) RuntimeError: ... INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED, so an XPU user gets strictly less than upstream: no diagnosable error at all, and no chance to handle it.
The layout combination itself need not be supported. The defect is that add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu re-dispatches instead of rejecting it, so the call never terminates.

Target-path evidence

aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml at the snapshot dispatches add.out for SparseCsrXPU to add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu, which this repository implements.
The control call (sparse CSR + sparse CSR) ran first and returned torch.sparse_csr on xpu:0 densifying to [[3.0, 0.0], [0.0, 3.0]], so the SparseCsrXPU add path is reachable and functional on this device. No XPU-to-CPU fallback warning was emitted for add (the one fallback warning in the log comes from sparse CSR construction).
The operand layouts and devices were printed immediately before the call, and the reproducer runs under python -u, so the pre-call marker being the last line places the abort inside the target call, not in setup and not after it.

Root cause
src/ATen/native/sparse/xpu/SparseCsrTensorMath.cpp:400:
Tensor& add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu(
    const Tensor& self,
    const SparseCsrTensor& other,
    const Scalar& alpha,
    SparseCsrTensor& out) {
  if (self.layout() == kStrided) {
    at::add_out(out, self, other.to_dense(), alpha);
    return out;
  } else if (other.layout() == kStrided) {
    at::add_out(out, other, self.to_dense(), alpha);
    return out;
  }
Tensor::to_dense() on a strided tensor returns that tensor unchanged, so when both inputs are strided and out is sparse CSR the re-dispatch of at::add_out selects SparseCsrXPU again (the key comes from out) with identical layouts. That recurses without bound and exhausts the native stack, which Python cannot convert into RecursionError; the reproducer catches RecursionError explicitly and it never fired.

The change needed here is the direct analogue of the CUDA patch: introduce using step_t = at::opmath_type<scalar_t> in the half/bfloat16 dispatch of linspace_kernel and logspace_kernel, compute the step (and logspace's base) in step_t, and let LinspaceFunctor/LogspaceFunctor carry it through their existing step_type template parameter. The integral dispatches already use float/double and should not change; opmath_type leaves float, double and complex bit-identical, so only half and bfloat16 outputs move.

Root cause on XPU
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp:370-393, WelfordCombine:
U delta = dataB.mean - dataA.mean;             // line 376
U count = dataA.count + dataB.count;
if (count > decltype(dataB.count){0}) {
  auto coef = sycl::native::recip(count);       // line 380
  auto nA = dataA.count * coef;
  auto nB = dataB.count * coef;
  mean = nA * dataA.mean + nB * dataB.mean;     // line 383
  sigma2 = dataA.sigma2 + dataB.sigma2 + delta * delta * dataA.count * nB;
}
Line 383 combines two partial means as a weighted average rather than as Welford's increment. It is exact only when nA + nB == 1 exactly, which no reciprocal guarantees, correctly rounded or not. The canonical in-tree combine, WelfordOps::combine in aten/src/ATen/native/SharedReduceOps.h, instead uses a.mean + delta * nb_over_n, which cannot move the mean when both partials agree.
The observed failure set points at the formula rather than at sycl::native::recip accuracy: widths 220 and 244 are both in the set upstream measured as failing even with a correctly rounded reciprocal (smallest 164, 188, 220, 244), while the 3 * 2^k widths that dominate the ROCm reports (48, 96, 192, 384, 768) are clean on this device.

layer_norm_kernel_impl (LayerNormKernels.cpp:686-690) selects launch_vectorized_layer_norm_kernel for float / half / bfloat16 when N % 4 == 0, N <= 2^24, and the buffers are 16-byte aligned. Every width in the table is a multiple of 4, so the vectorized kernel ran; its compute_stats calls WelfordCombine at lines 425 (intra-subgroup shuffle) and 450 (inter-subgroup merge).
The N % 4 != 0 fallback, launch_rowwise_moments_kernel, builds its reduction from WelfordOps<...> (LayerNormKernels.cpp:207), i.e. the mean-preserving combine. The divergence is therefore confined to the vectorized arm, matching upstream's account of why non-multiple-of-4 widths are clean.

Suggested direction
Bring WelfordCombine into agreement with WelfordOps::combine, keeping sigma2 as is since it already uses nB and is Chan's M2 term, independent of how the mean is formed:
auto nB = dataB.count * coef;
mean = (dataA.count == U(0)) ? dataB.mean : dataA.mean + delta * nB;
sigma2 = dataA.sigma2 + dataB.sigma2 + delta * delta * dataA.count * nB;
delta is already dataB.mean - dataA.mean at line 376, so the increment is based on dataA. The select covers the idle-lane merge where dataA.count == 0 and the weighted form would otherwise rescale dataB.mean; the mirrored case needs no guard because nB is then exactly zero. On a constant input delta is exactly zero, so the mean cannot move however accurate coef is. This does change bitwise forward output for non-constant input, as the equivalent upstream change does.
WelfordOnlineSum (line 360) also uses sycl::native::recip, but it is not implicated for a constant input: delta is exactly zero from the second element onward, and the first element divides by a count of exactly 1.

Stated so they are not mistaken for oversights:

The reproducer's control, a plain x.mean(dim=-1) on the same tensor, was itself inexact for float32 at widths 220 and 244, so it does not isolate layer_norm for that dtype. For float16 and bfloat16 the control passed, but its result is rounded to the low-precision output dtype while the saved mean is float32, so it is a weak control either way. The CPU-versus-XPU layer_norm oracle is unaffected - CPU returned exactly zero in all six failing rows - and neither is the source divergence above. Whether XPU's generic mean reduction is also inexact at these widths is a separate question this scan does not settle.
Only multiples of 4 were exercised, so the N % 4 != 0 fallback is clean by source reading rather than by measurement.
Backward was not exercised on XPU. Upstream reports that native_layer_norm_backward consumes the saved mean and rstd and contains no Welford reduction, so it should inherit the forward fix, but that was not verified here.

def check_wide_out(op, name, self_v, t1_v, t2_v, value, failures):

    t1_h = torch.tensor(t1_v, dtype=torch.half)
    t2_h = torch.tensor(t2_v, dtype=torch.half)

[xpu-alignment] [26-09-29] torch.unique(dim=...) on XPU fails to deduplicate and sort sub-tensors when the input contains NaN
Summary
torch.unique(x, dim=...) on XPU silently fails to deduplicate: identical sub-tensors come back more than once, the output is not in ascending order, and return_counts reports wrong counts. This happens as soon as the input contains a NaN anywhere. The flattened dim=None path on the same XPU data is correct, so the two paths of the same operator disagree with no error.
The comparator that unique_dim sorts with on XPU, UniqueDimLessFunctor in src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/UniqueKernels.cpp, compares elements with raw < and >. Both are false when either operand is NaN, so the functor is not a strict weak ordering: a row containing NaN neither sorts to a defined position nor groups with its duplicates, and the subsequent compute_unique / compute_inverse passes then count adjacent-equal runs over an unsorted sequence. The flat (dim=None) path in the same file compares with std::isless, which is why only the dim= path is affected.
This is the XPU half of upstream pytorch/pytorch#199057, which reports the same behavior for the CPU std::sort comparator in aten/src/ATen/native/Unique.cpp. Upstream's suggested patch touches only that CPU file, so landing it would not change the XPU kernel.

Root cause in this repository
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/UniqueKernels.cpp, the comparator passed to pstl::sort by unique_dim_template:
template <typename scalar_t>
struct UniqueDimLessFunctor {
  template <typename T>
  bool operator()(T a, T b) const {
    for (int64_t i = 0; i < n_; ++i) {
      scalar_t lhs = c10::load(&input_flat_ptr_[i + a * n_]);
      scalar_t rhs = c10::load(&input_flat_ptr_[i + b * n_]);
      if (lhs < rhs) {
        return true;
      } else if (lhs > rhs) {
        return false;
      }
    }
    return false;
  }
For comparison, the flat path in the same file uses std::isless(a, b), which is well defined for NaN.
The fix is to make the comparator a strict weak ordering by giving NaN a defined position (last, matching at::sort and the dim=None path), as the upstream issue proposes for the CPU comparator. Note that UniqueDimEqualFunctor / UniqueDimNotEqualFunctor in the same file compare with !=, so two NaN sub-tensors are never treated as equal even once sorted; whoever picks this up should decide whether NaN rows are expected to collapse (the dim=None path and numpy.unique both collapse them) and adjust the equality functors to match.

[xpu-alignment] [26-09-30] XPU eager nextafter returns +0.0 instead of -0.0 when stepping up from the smallest negative subnormal
Summary
Eager torch.nextafter on XPU returns +0.0 when x is the smallest negative subnormal (bits 0x80000001 for float32, 0x8000000000000001 for float64) and y is any value greater than x. The IEEE 754 / C nextafter result for that step is -0.0 (bits 0x80000000 / 0x8000000000000000), which is also what the Inductor-compiled Triton kernel returns for the same tensors on the same device. Only the sign of the zero differs, but nextafter is a bit-exact operation and the sign of a zero is observable through signbit, copysign and division.
This is why the device-generic test added by upstream commit 3bfd3c6a9010 fails on XPU: 6 of the 100 non-NaN elements of its input matrix mismatch, in float32 and float64 and in both the contiguous and the transposed layout. All 6 are the single row x = -smallest subnormal together with the 6 columns where y > x. Stepping from that same subnormal away from zero, and every step from +smallest subnormal, match bit-exactly, so the defect is specifically the step that lands on zero.

void isin_kernel(
    const Tensor& elements,
    const Tensor& test_elements,
    bool invert,
    const Tensor& out) {
  std::vector<int64_t> bc_shape(elements.dim(), 1);
  bc_shape.push_back(-1);
  out.copy_(
      invert ? elements.unsqueeze(-1).ne(test_elements.view(bc_shape)).all(-1)

CPU eager returns beta * input - all ones, no NaN - so the mat1 @ mat2 term

aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/Blas.cpp

alpha_ratio = alpha_ / beta_ = 0 becomes a kind_with_linear scale applied
to the already-computed product, followed by kind_with_binary_add of
input and a beta_ scale. The product is therefore computed first and
multiplied by zero second.

onednn::matmul(...) followed by result.mul_(alpha), so float64 is
affected for the same reason.
