issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-20] ctc_loss on XPU indexes with unvalidated target labels: out-of-bounds read in forward, out-of-bounds write in backward
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: pr-197799 -->
## Summary

`torch.nn.functional.ctc_loss` on XPU accepts target label values outside `[0, num_classes)` and uses them directly as indices into device memory. The forward alpha kernel reads at the out-of-range label offset and the backward kernel writes the accumulated gradient at that offset. Both return normally, so an invalid label produces a finite loss and a silent out-of-bounds device write instead of an error.

## Upstream source

- pytorch/pytorch#197799 (open, unmerged) "Fix ctc_loss CPU OOB access on out-of-range target values", fixing pytorch/pytorch#193794. It adds a `check_target_values` helper to `aten/src/ATen/native/LossCTC.cpp`, gated on `targets.device().is_cpu()`, and states in its own notes: "Remaining scope: CUDA, XPU, and MPS kernels are untouched. The CUDA implementation documents the same gap at `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/LossCTC.cu:212-214`; validating there needs a device sync, so it is left for a separate change."
- Alignment scan window: `[2026-09-20T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z)`, `pytorch/pytorch` frozen default-branch head `f3d603baf74daa6ac8fbf15feb37f0edb6ac9ad3`.

## Observed XPU behavior

With `num_classes = 20` and target values `100` and `-5` (batch rows 0 and 1), no exception is raised in either direction:

```text
TARGET: xpu device = Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
torch version: 2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu
TARGET: in-range control loss = 11.84984302520752 device = xpu:0
TARGET: out-of-range targets xpu:0 values 100 -5 num_classes 20
forward returned 11.999288558959961 without raising
backward also returned without raising
```

## Target-path evidence

`_ctc_loss` for XPU dispatches to `ctc_loss_xpu` (`src/ATen/native/xpu/LossCTC.cpp:18`), which calls `at::native::xpu::ctc_loss_kernel` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossCTCKernels.cpp`. Only XPU tensors are used in the reproducer and both the control loss and the bad-target loss are produced on `xpu:0`, so no CPU kernel participates.

The XPU kernel validates `BLANK`, the tensor shapes, `target_lengths[i] >= 0`, and `targets.size(1) >= max_target_length` (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:292-390`), but never the target values themselves. `get_target_prime` carries the ported CUDA comment `- note that no bound-checking is done` (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:42`) and returns `target[offset + stride * (idx / 2)]`, which is then used as an index:

- forward alpha kernel: `log_probs_data_[... + lp_char_stride_ * target_prime]` (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:103-140`)
- backward gradient kernel: `gradient_data_[gr_batch_offset + t * gr_input_stride_ + gr_char_stride_ * current_target_prime]`, an unbounded **write** index (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:800-811`)

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

T, N, C, L = 50, 2, 20, 10
torch.manual_seed(0)
log_probs = torch.randn(T, N, C, device="xpu").log_softmax(2).requires_grad_()
input_lengths = torch.full((N,), T, dtype=torch.long, device="xpu")
target_lengths = torch.full((N,), L, dtype=torch.long, device="xpu")

in_range = torch.randint(1, C, (N, L), dtype=torch.long, device="xpu")
control = F.ctc_loss(log_probs, in_range, input_lengths, target_lengths)
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("in-range control loss =", float(control.detach()), "device =", control.device)

bad = in_range.clone()
bad[0, 0] = C + 80   # 100, out of range for num_classes = 20
bad[1, 0] = -5       # negative label

loss = F.ctc_loss(log_probs, bad, input_lengths, target_lengths)
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("forward returned", float(loss.detach()), "without raising")
loss.backward()
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("backward also returned without raising")
```

Expected: a `RuntimeError` naming the valid target range, as the upstream CPU fix raises (`Expected target values to be in the range [0, C), but got value 100 for batch 0`). Actual: both directions complete and the backward writes at the out-of-range label offset.

## Environment

```text
python:        /opt/conda/bin/python3.13 (3.13.13)
torch:         2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu
torch path:    /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
xpu available: true
xpu device:    Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership rationale

The XPU `ctc_loss` forward and backward kernels, including all of their input validation, live in this repository (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossCTCKernels.cpp`); the upstream CPU allocator's new check is explicitly gated to CPU tensors, so no upstream change reaches the XPU path. A search of `pytorch/pytorch` found no issue or PR that owns target-value validation for the XPU kernel, and no existing `intel/torch-xpu-ops` tracker covers it (issue #1637 was a separate `test_ctc_loss_error_xpu` floating-point exception, closed as completed).

### Tradeoff for maintainers

CUDA has the identical gap and documents it deliberately (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/LossCTC.cu:211-214`, present at the frozen head: "we do not check that the labels are in the valid range. As we use them for indexing in the kernels, you'll see memory errors when you pass corrupt labels"). Upstream deferred the accelerator side of #197799 because host-side validation of device targets requires a device sync per call. So this is a memory-safety gap XPU shares with CUDA rather than an XPU-vs-CUDA divergence, and the fix approach is a maintainer decision: host-side validation with a sync, an in-kernel bounds assert, or waiting for the upstream accelerator decision. Filed so the gap is tracked with a runner-backed reproducer either way.

Summary
torch.nn.functional.ctc_loss on XPU accepts target label values outside [0, num_classes) and uses them directly as indices into device memory. The forward alpha kernel reads at the out-of-range label offset and the backward kernel writes the accumulated gradient at that offset. Both return normally, so an invalid label produces a finite loss and a silent out-of-bounds device write instead of an error.
Upstream source

pytorch/pytorch#197799 (open, unmerged) "Fix ctc_loss CPU OOB access on out-of-range target values", fixing pytorch/pytorch#193794. It adds a check_target_values helper to aten/src/ATen/native/LossCTC.cpp, gated on targets.device().is_cpu(), and states in its own notes: "Remaining scope: CUDA, XPU, and MPS kernels are untouched. The CUDA implementation documents the same gap at aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/LossCTC.cu:212-214; validating there needs a device sync, so it is left for a separate change."

TARGET: xpu device = Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
torch version: 2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu
TARGET: in-range control loss = 11.84984302520752 device = xpu:0

forward returned 11.999288558959961 without raising
backward also returned without raising

issues.title: Enable Inductor collective autotuning on XPU (device-agnostic _run_collective_benchmark)
issues.body:
## Summary
Inductor's collective autotuning path is currently CUDA-only. On an XPU build, the collective autotuning tests (e.g. `test/inductor/test_collective_autotuning.py`) pass while actually autotuning nothing — every choice is skipped and the autotuner silently falls back to the default implementation.

## Root Cause
`SelectAlgorithm._run_collective_benchmark` uses `torch.cuda.synchronize()` and `torch.cuda.Event` unconditionally:
- `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:5291`
- `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:5296`
- `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:5298-5299`

On an XPU-only build these raise `AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled`, so every choice fails and the autotuner falls back.

## Reproduction
Running the collective autotuning tests on 8x PVC (`xccl` available, `get_default_backend_for_device("xpu:0") == "xccl"`):

```
Collective benchmark exception for choice test::equiv_ar_autotuned_sum_allreduce_0. Skipping this choice.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py", line 5348, in benchmark_collective_choice
    cls._run_collective_benchmark(
  File "torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py", line 5291, in _run_collective_benchmark
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
  File "torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 596, in _lazy_init
    raise AssertionError("Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled")
AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled

Autotune Choices Stats:
{"num_choices": 3, "num_triton_choices": 0, "best_kernel": "...sum_allreduce_0", "best_time": Infinity}
At least one choice failed or timed out during collective benchmarking. Falling back to default implementation.
```

## Proposed Fix
Make `_run_collective_benchmark` device-agnostic (use the appropriate accelerator's `synchronize()` / `Event`, e.g. via `torch.accelerator` or the device-appropriate module) so collective autotuning works on XPU.

Ref: [地址已移除]

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-21] adaptive_max_pool3d_backward on XPU reads a non-contiguous indices tensor as if it were contiguous: silently wrong gradients under torch.compile with channels_last_3d inputs
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-197888 -->
## Summary

`adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp` makes `gradOutput` contiguous but reads `indices` through its raw data pointer. When `indices` arrives with `channels_last_3d` strides the kernel scatters the gradient to the wrong positions, with no error. Inductor lays the saved indices out in the input's memory format, so `F.adaptive_max_pool3d` under `torch.compile` on a `channels_last_3d` XPU input trains with silently wrong gradients through every adaptive max pool.

This is the XPU half of upstream `pytorch/pytorch#197888`, which reports the same class of defect for the CPU kernels of `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward`, `fractional_max_pool2d_backward` and `fractional_max_pool3d_backward`. Only `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward` reproduces on XPU; the two XPU `fractional_max_pool*_backward` kernels use `PackedTensorAccessor64`, honour the real strides, and are correct.

## Upstream source and scan window

- Upstream issue: [地址已移除] (OPEN, no fix PR as of this scan)
- Scan window: `[2026-09-21T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-22T00:00:00Z)` on `pytorch/pytorch`
- Frozen `pytorch/pytorch` default-branch head: `6b5c7ad181277ba21aa48b1dc03786ab95f68ad4`
- Upstream oracle: the correct gradient is the one obtained when the same index values are read with their real strides (equivalently, from a contiguous copy of `indices`). Upstream reports that on CUDA the compiled gradient matches eager, so upstream's stated fix scope is the CPU kernels.

## Root cause in this repository

`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp`, `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel`:

```cpp
void adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel(
    const Tensor& gradOutput,
    const Tensor& input,
    const Tensor& indices,
    const Tensor& gradInput) {
  const Tensor gradOutput_ = gradOutput.contiguous();   // indices is not normalized
  ...
          const int64_t* indices_data = indices.const_data_ptr<int64_t>();
```

`gradOutput` is normalized, `indices` is not, and both templates then index `indices_data` with contiguous arithmetic. The XPU kernel is reached through `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_out_xpu` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cpp`.

The upstream CUDA kernel (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cu` at the frozen head) carries the same raw-pointer pattern, but upstream reports its compiled path does not hit it; the XPU compiled path does.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

A = torch.ops.aten

# 1. Kernel level: identical index values, contiguous vs channels_last_3d strides.
torch.manual_seed(0)
x3 = torch.randperm(240).float().reshape(1, 4, 4, 3, 5).to("xpu")
v, i = F.adaptive_max_pool3d(x3, (2, 3, 5), return_indices=True)
go = torch.arange(1.0, v.numel() + 1, device="xpu").reshape(v.shape)
i_nc = i.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last_3d)  # same values, different strides
print("indices strides", tuple(i_nc.stride()))
print(
    "same gradient as with contiguous indices:",
    torch.equal(
        A.adaptive_max_pool3d_backward(go, x3, i),
        A.adaptive_max_pool3d_backward(go, x3, i_nc),
    ),
)

# 2. User level: eager vs aot_eager vs inductor on a channels_last_3d input.
torch.manual_seed(0)
f = lambda t: F.adaptive_max_pool3d(t, (2, 3, 5))
x = torch.randperm(1 * 4 * 4 * 6 * 5).float().reshape(1, 4, 4, 6, 5).to("xpu")
for name, xin in (
    ("contiguous", x),
    ("channels_last_3d", x.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last_3d)),
):
    grads = []
    for backend in (None, "aot_eager", "inductor"):
        torch._dynamo.reset()
        t = xin.detach().clone(memory_format=torch.preserve_format).requires_grad_()
        out = (f if backend is None else torch.compile(f, backend=backend))(t)
        w = torch.arange(1.0, out.numel() + 1, device="xpu").reshape(out.shape)
        (out * w).sum().backward()
        grads.append(t.grad.clone())
    print(
        f"{name:17s} aot_eager==eager: {torch.equal(grads[0], grads[1])}"
        f"   inductor==eager: {torch.equal(grads[0], grads[2])}"
        f"   max diff {(grads[0] - grads[2]).abs().max().item():.0f}"
    )
```

## Observed XPU behavior

```
KERNEL: adaptive_max_pool3d_backward indices_stride=(120, 1, 60, 20, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=False
KERNEL: adaptive_max_pool2d_backward indices_stride=(60, 1, 20, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
KERNEL: max_pool3d_with_indices_backward indices_stride=(96, 1, 32, 16, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
KERNEL: fractional_max_pool2d_backward indices_stride=(36, 1, 12, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
KERNEL: fractional_max_pool3d_backward indices_stride=(32, 1, 16, 8, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
COMPILE: contiguous aot_eager==eager=True inductor==eager=True max_diff=0.0
COMPILE: channels_last_3d aot_eager==eager=True inductor==eager=False max_diff=118.0
```

## Target-path evidence

All five pooling backward ops were invoked with `xpu` tensors and asserted to have produced `xpu` outputs, so the divergence comes from the XPU SYCL kernels rather than from a host fallback. At user level, `aot_eager==eager=True` while `inductor==eager=False` on the same `channels_last_3d` XPU input, and `t.grad.device.type` was asserted to be `xpu`; that isolates the wrong gradient to the XPU backward kernel reached through inductor's memory-format choice, not to the tracing layer.

## Environment

```
torch            2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu
torch path       /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
python           3.13.13 (/opt/conda/bin/python3.13)
xpu available    True
xpu device       Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership rationale

The wrong code is `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel` in this repository, reached through `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_out_xpu`; the fix is to normalize `indices` next to the existing `gradOutput.contiguous()` (or to index it through its real strides). Upstream `pytorch/pytorch#197888` reports CUDA's compiled gradient as correct and scopes its suggested fix to the CPU kernels, so landing it would not change the XPU kernel. No `pytorch/pytorch` issue or PR was found that explicitly owns the XPU part, and no existing `intel/torch-xpu-ops` tracker covers it.

Scope note for whoever picks this up: only `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward` needs the change on XPU. `adaptive_max_pool2d_backward`, `max_pool3d_with_indices_backward` and both `fractional_max_pool*_backward` kernels already handle non-contiguous `indices` correctly, so the two `fractional_max_pool*` thirds of the upstream oracle do not apply here.

Filed by the XPU alignment automation; the finding was produced by a scan and independently reviewed before filing.

adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel
(src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp:500) normalizes only
one of the three tensors its kernels address with contiguous index arithmetic.
Line 505 takes gradOutput.contiguous(), but indices is passed straight
through as a raw pointer (lines 553 and 577) and both kernel templates then walk
it as if it were contiguous:
indices_ + o_plane * osizeH_ * osizeW_ + oh * osizeW_ + ow (lines 285 and
360). With channels_last_3d indices those offsets land on unrelated
elements, so atomicAdd/+= scatters each gradOutput element to whatever
input position the misread index happens to name -- wrong gradients, no error.
The same applies to the destination: lines 550/574 take
gradInput.mutable_data_ptr() and lines 283/358 offset it as
gradInput_ + d * isizeT_ * isizeH_ * isizeW_, so a non-contiguous gradInput
is written through contiguous arithmetic too.
Both instances are silent and both are reachable from Python on the current
nightly (2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu): the indices one through
torch.compile, which saves indices in the input's memory format, and the
gradInput one through the adaptive_max_pool3d_backward.grad_input out=

set_output_raw_strided(0, input.sizes(), {}, input.options())
(aten/src/ATen/native/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cpp:81), and an empty strides
argument does not restride a caller-supplied out.
The XPU kernel is a direct port of the CUDA one, which carries the same
raw-indices pattern
(aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cu:403,449,472), so upstream
pytorch/pytorch#197888 -- which scopes its fix to the CPU kernels because it
observes CUDA's compiled gradient as correct -- would not change the XPU path.
The sibling 2D kernel in this repository already carries the fix pattern:
adaptive_max_pool2d_backward_kernel normalizes grad_output and indices and
stages a contiguous grad_input with a copy-back
(src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling2dKernels.cpp:341-345,391-393),
and #3941 established that idiom for the non-contiguous-output case in the
same family. Fix strategy: apply that same normalization inside
adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel.

Target repo: torch-xpu-ops
Domain: xpu-kernel

Automated by fix-root-cause.



Implementation
One file changed: src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp.
adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel now normalizes indices the same way it
already normalized gradOutput, and stages a contiguous gradInput with a
copy-back when the caller's gradInput is not contiguous. Both dispatch lambdas
(atomic and non-atomic) take their pointers from the normalized tensors. This is
the idiom adaptive_max_pool2d_backward_kernel already uses in this repository.
 void adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel(
     const Tensor& input,
     const Tensor& indices,
     const Tensor& gradInput) {
+  // Both kernel templates address gradOutput, indices and gradInput with
+  // contiguous index arithmetic, so all three have to be normalized here.
   const Tensor gradOutput_ = gradOutput.contiguous();
+  const Tensor indices_ = indices.contiguous();
+  const Tensor gradInput_ = gradInput.is_contiguous()
+      ? gradInput
+      : at::empty(gradInput.sizes(), gradInput.options());

-  gradInput.zero_();
+  gradInput_.zero_();
@@ (both AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND2 lambdas)
-          scalar_t* gradInput_data = gradInput.mutable_data_ptr<scalar_t>();
+          scalar_t* gradInput_data = gradInput_.mutable_data_ptr<scalar_t>();
           const scalar_t* gradOutput_data =
               gradOutput_.const_data_ptr<scalar_t>();
-          const int64_t* indices_data = indices.const_data_ptr<int64_t>();
+          const int64_t* indices_data = indices_.const_data_ptr<int64_t>();
@@ (end of function)
   }
+
+  if (!gradInput.is_contiguous()) {
+    gradInput.copy_(gradInput_);
+  }
 }

does for its input -- was rejected: the forward kernel encodes argmax as a

issues.title: [skip-added] test_regional_fallback_by_default_invoke_subgraph_xpu on XPU (dill 0.3.7 by-value pickling)
issues.body:
Auto-added by `fix-implement` (`allow_skip=true`) while handling the DISABLED test tracked by `pytorch/pytorch#195876`.

**Test:** `test/inductor/test_compile_subprocess.py::GPUTests::test_regional_fallback_by_default_invoke_subgraph_xpu`

**Original failure:** `torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: TypeError: cannot pickle '_thread._local' object`

**Root cause (device independent).** `test_compile_subprocess.py` re-runs `CommonTemplate` with `fx_compile_mode = SUBPROCESS`, so each graph goes through `GraphPickler` (`torch/fx/_graph_pickler.py`), which uses `dill` instead of the stdlib pickler when `dill` is importable. dill's `_locate_function` resolves a dotted module name by importing the parent package and doing `getattr(parent, last_component)`; for `torch._higher_order_ops.invoke_subgraph` that returns the `InvokeSubgraphHOP` instance re-exported by `torch/_higher_order_ops/__init__.py`, not the submodule. Every function and class defined in `invoke_subgraph.py` therefore looks unresolvable, dill pickles them by value, and walking their `__globals__` reaches a `_thread._local`.

This test is the only `CommonTemplate` case that calls `get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options()`, which hangs `functools.partial` compiler callables off `NestedCompileRegionOptions`, so it is the only one that trips the path.

**Reason for skip.** The same test is already declared `TestFailure(("cpu", "cuda"), is_skip=True)` in that file for exactly this reason; `xpu` was left out of the tuple, which is why XPU CI was the only configuration still running it. The patch just adds `"xpu"` to the existing tuple.

**Real fix is upstream and needs a maintainer decision.** The test passes unmodified under `dill==0.4.1` (newer dill honours `byref` for functions, not only classes); pytorch CI pins `dill==0.3.7` in `.ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt`. Either bumping that pin (rebuilds every CI image, and also changes the other four `is_skip` entries in the same dict) or teaching `GraphPickler` to force by-reference function saving (changes fx-graph serialization for every backend) would be a real fix. No XPU-side work is involved.

**Base analyzed:** pytorch@8224fee7

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

```
import torch

DEVICE = "xpu"   # "cpu" -> OK, "xpu" -> ValueError
B, H, S, D = 2, 2, 7, 16
HID = H * D


class Attention(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.q_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)
        self.k_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)
        self.v_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x, mask):
        q = self.q_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        k = self.k_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        v = self.v_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        attn = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=mask)
        attn = attn.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        return attn.reshape(B, S, -1)


model = Attention().eval().to(DEVICE)
inputs = {
    "x": torch.randn(B, S, HID, device=DEVICE),
    "mask": torch.zeros(B, 1, S, S, device=DEVICE).expand(B, H, S, S),
}
ep = torch.export.export(model, (), dict(inputs), strict=False)
torch.onnx.export(ep, args=(), kwargs=dict(inputs), dynamo=True, optimize=False)
```

import torch

DEVICE = "xpu"   # "cpu" -> OK, "xpu" -> ValueError
B, H, S, D = 2, 2, 7, 16
HID = H * D


class Attention(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.q_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)
        self.k_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)
        self.v_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x, mask):
        q = self.q_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        k = self.k_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        v = self.v_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        attn = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=mask)
        attn = attn.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        return attn.reshape(B, S, -1)


model = Attention().eval().to(DEVICE)
inputs = {

nodes.bodyText: @LuFinch

On XPU, SDPA backend selection depends on GradMode, and different backends produce different output memory layouts.

requires_grad=False -> _fused_sdp_choice = 4 (overrideable aka oneDNN) -> alloc_with_matching_layout(query, ...) (Attention.cpp:336)	(224, 16, 32, 1) — follows query's layout
requires_grad=True  -> _fused_sdp_choice = 0 (math) -> allocates its own buffer	(224, 112, 16, 1) — plain contiguous

The ONNX exporter evaluates the meta of the same SDPA node three times, and the grad context flips twice:



#
Stage
Grad
Backend
SDPA output stride




1
torch.export.export (pre-dispatch)
on
math
(224, 112, 16, 1)


2
run_decompositions() (re-traced below autograd)
off
overrideable
(224, 16, 32, 1)


3
InsertTypePromotion fake-tensor re-propagation
on
math
(224, 112, 16, 1)



Hence, the rootcause is that ONNX sometime run with grad mode and sometime run with no-grad mode.  PT XPU doesn't enable overrideable backward yet so that grad mode will choose math backend. Different backends have different layout and then throw error.
pytorch/pytorch#162454 will enable SDPA overrideable backend and this issue will be fixed.

issues.title: test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu fails: constant-buffer allocation not reflected by XPU memory query
issues.body:
## Description
`test_update_user_managed_buffer` fails on XPU for both
`AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu` and `AOTInductorTestDualWrapper`. The test
allocates an owned constant buffer via `runner.update_constant_buffer(...)` and
asserts that memory usage increased (`mem_after > mem_before`). On XPU the two
measured values are identical, so the assertion fails.

## Failing tests
- `test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu`
- `test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestDualWrapper::test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu`

## Error
```
File "test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py", line 8622, in test_update_user_managed_buffer
    self.assertGreater(mem_after, mem_before)
AssertionError: -68702699520 not greater than -68702699520
```

## Analysis
The memory probe differs by device (test_aot_inductor.py:8601-8605):
```python
def constant_buffer_memory_used():
    if self.device == "cuda":
        return torch.cuda.memory_allocated(self.device)
    free_memory, _ = getattr(torch, GPU_TYPE).mem_get_info(self.device)
    return -free_memory
```
On XPU, `mem_get_info` free memory is unchanged across the constant-buffer
allocation (`update_constant_buffer(new_weights, True, False, False)`), so
`mem_after == mem_before`. Note the CUDA path also sets
`aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator=True` (line 8590-8591), which is not
applied for XPU. The XPU memory query is likely too coarse to observe the
allocation, or the allocation path is not tracked by `mem_get_info`.

## Repro
```
python test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu.test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu
```

## Environment
- pytorch: fc5530887482e83d171231ad1f7c1dd6498da99e
- torch-xpu-ops: 562950cc554685d4e7461d6277d71306d1e468eb
- Platform: Linux

@daisyden  I couldn't reproduce this on a bare-metal Max 1550 (same driver, 1.6.33578). I ran the full test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py the way CI does (run_ut.sh PYTEST_ADDOPTS, one tile per worker via ZE_AFFINITY_MASK, numactl pinning), without any test changes. Both test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu variants passed. I logged torch.xpu.mem_get_info() after every test, and it never reported free == total.
-68702699520 is exactly the total memory of one tile. On PVC-817255, mem_get_info returns free == total both before and after the 64 MB allocation, which means no real free-memory data comes back. The same numbers appear in every failing run I found (30987352138, 31362886717, 35871429007), so I suspect the CI environment rather than AOTI.

issues.title: [upstream_ut] XPU backward kernels missing input-validation error checks (replication_pad2d, grid_sample)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Running upstream `test/test_nn.py` on XPU, two "error-checking" cases fail because
the XPU backward kernels do not raise the validation error that CPU/CUDA raise.
Both PASS on CPU.

**test_Pad_backward_channel_mismatch_xpu** (test/test_nn.py:8791)
```
with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "grad_output channel unexpected"):
AssertionError: RuntimeError not raised
```
The XPU `replication_pad2d_backward` kernel lacks the channel-dim bounds check that
CPU/CUDA got from pytorch/pytorch#189463; it silently returns a wrong-shaped result.
Related: #4565.

**test_grid_sample_backward_error_checking_xpu** (test/test_nn.py:7132)
```
with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "expected grad_output to have sizes"):
AssertionError: ValueError not raised
```
The XPU `grid_sampler` backward does not validate grad_output sizes.

Note: neither case is caught by torch-xpu-ops CI because the vendored
`test/xpu/test_nn_xpu.py` is a stale copy that does not contain these cases.

### Versions
main

issues.title: [XPU] Segfault in ReflectionPad with empty complex64 input
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Running upstream `test/test_nn.py` on XPU, `test_ReflectionPad_empty_xpu_complex64`
crashes the process with a GPU segfault (worker crash), while the same test passes
on CPU/CUDA.

```
pytest -v test/test_nn.py -k "test_ReflectionPad_empty_xpu_complex64"
```

```
Segmentation fault from GPU at 0x0, ctx_id: 1 (CCS) type: 0 (NotPresent), level: 3 (PML4), access: 0 (Read), banned: 1, aborting.
worker 'gw0' crashed while running 'test/test_nn.py::TestNNDeviceTypeXPU::test_ReflectionPad_empty_xpu_complex64'
```

The test exercises `ReflectionPad1d/2d/3d` on empty tensors (leading dim 0) with
`dtype=torch.complex64`. The XPU reflection_pad kernel appears to perform an
out-of-bounds GPU read for the empty complex64 case.

Note: this case is not caught by torch-xpu-ops CI because the vendored
`test/xpu/test_nn_xpu.py` is a stale copy of upstream `test/test_nn.py`.

### Versions

main (branch inductor_agnostic), PyTorch built with torch-xpu-ops.

issues.title: FlopCounterMode reports 0 FLOPs for SDPA on XPU (`_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable` has no flop formula)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Bug Description

`torch.utils.flop_counter.FlopCounterMode` reports **0 FLOPs** for every `scaled_dot_product_attention` call on XPU. The same call on CPU is counted correctly. This affects any XPU user of the flop counter, not just tests.

This blocks enabling `test_flop_counter.py::TestFlopCounterDeviceXPU::test_sdpa_gqa_xpu` on XPU (see pytorch/pytorch#197249), which asserts `gqa_flops > 0` and fails with `AssertionError: False is not true`.

## Affected Tests

```
op_ut,test/test_flop_counter.py,TestFlopCounterDeviceXPU.test_sdpa_gqa_xpu
```
Note: Test will be enabled in [地址已移除]

## Reproducer

```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.flop_counter import FlopCounterMode

q = torch.randn(2, 32, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)
k = torch.randn(2, 8, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)
v = torch.randn(2, 8, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)

with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as mode:
    F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True, enable_gqa=True)
print(sum(v for _, v in mode.flop_counts["Global"].items()))
```

## Error Message

```
XPU SDPA flops : 0
CPU SDPA flops : 268435456
```

Expected the XPU count to be non-zero

## Root Cause Analysis

XPU SDPA dispatches to `aten::_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable` (confirmed with a `TorchDispatchMode` trace). That op is **not registered** in `torch/utils/flop_counter.py`:

```python
>>> torch.ops.aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable in flop_registry
False
```

`register_flop_formula` for `sdpa_flop` covers only the CUDA/CPU variants (`_scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention`, `_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention`, `_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention_for_cpu`, `_scaled_dot_product_cudnn_attention`), and `sdpa_backward_flop` likewise omits the overrideable backward op. Unregistered ops contribute 0, so the total is 0.

## Suggested Fix

Add the overrideable ops to the existing formulas in `torch/utils/flop_counter.py` — the math is backend-independent, so no new formula is needed:

- `aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable` → `sdpa_flop`
- `aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable_backward` → `sdpa_backward_flop`

Both overloads exist in this build. The fix is upstream in pytorch/pytorch.

## Related Intel/torch-xpu-ops Issues

- #4853 — `Inductor flop counter reports 0 FLOPs on XPU (get_device_tflops has no non-CUDA fallback)`. **Different layer**: #4853 is Inductor's peak-TFLOPS/roofline path; this issue is the dispatch-level `flop_registry`. Fixing one does not fix the other.
- #5444, #5124 — roofline runtime estimates returning 0 on XPU (same layer as #4853)

### Versions

torch 2.15.0a0+gita95d76a
commit 08bdc2a8e0d
Platform: linux, Python 3.12.3
Device: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1550 (PVC)

q = torch.randn(2, 32, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)
k = torch.randn(2, 8, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)
v = torch.randn(2, 8, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)

with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as mode:
    F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True, enable_gqa=True)
print(sum(v for _, v in mode.flop_counts["Global"].items()))
Error Message
XPU SDPA flops : 0
CPU SDPA flops : 268435456

Expected the XPU count to be non-zero
Root Cause Analysis
XPU SDPA dispatches to aten::_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable (confirmed with a TorchDispatchMode trace). That op is not registered in torch/utils/flop_counter.py:
>>> torch.ops.aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable in flop_registry
False
register_flop_formula for sdpa_flop covers only the CUDA/CPU variants (_scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention, _scaled_dot_product_flash_attention, _scaled_dot_product_flash_attention_for_cpu, _scaled_dot_product_cudnn_attention), and sdpa_backward_flop likewise omits the overrideable backward op. Unregistered ops contribute 0, so the total is 0.
Suggested Fix
Add the overrideable ops to the existing formulas in torch/utils/flop_counter.py — the math is backend-independent, so no new formula is needed:

aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable → sdpa_flop
aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable_backward → sdpa_backward_flop

Both overloads exist in this build. The fix is upstream in pytorch/pytorch.
Related Intel/torch-xpu-ops Issues

#4853 — Inductor flop counter reports 0 FLOPs on XPU (get_device_tflops has no non-CUDA fallback). Different layer: #4853 is Inductor's peak-TFLOPS/roofline path; this issue is the dispatch-level flop_registry. Fixing one does not fix the other.
#5444, #5124 — roofline runtime estimates returning 0 on XPU (same layer as #4853)

Versions
torch 2.15.0a0+gita95d76a
commit 08bdc2a8e0d
Platform: linux, Python 3.12.3
Device: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1550 (PVC)

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-24] XPU linspace/logspace compute the half and bfloat16 step in the output dtype, so results diverge from CPU
issues.body:
## Upstream source - Origin: `pytorch/pytorch@1614f7f277b640ca057b20aa452178eb1f31e898` (PR #198415), "[BE] Compute linspace/logspace step in the opmath type for half and bfloat16", committed `2026-09-24T03:52:29Z`. It changes `aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/RangeFactoriesKernel.cpp` and `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/RangeFactories.cu` only. - Scan window: `[2026-09-24T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-25T00:00:00Z)` on `pytorch/pytorch`, frozen default-branch head `cae30b13eb94e8a7faa09cd832f9cc84f9935e44`. The commit is an ancestor of that head (`compare` reports `behind_by: 0`), so the CPU/CUDA fix has landed. Upstream summary of the defect: for half and bfloat16 the step was rounded to the output dtype before being multiplied by the index, so the rounding compounds across the range. Upstream switched the step (and, for `logspace`, the base and hence the `pow`) to `at::opmath_type`, which promotes exactly half and bfloat16 and leaves float, double and complex bit-identical. ## Observed XPU behavior Running `linspace`/`logspace` in half and bfloat16 on XPU and comparing against the CPU result and against a float64 reference rounded to the output dtype: ```text TARGET-PATH-PROOF float16 logspace: out=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float16 numel=38 OBSERVED float16 logspace: vs float64-rounded reference xpu 26/38 cpu 0/38 | xpu vs cpu 26 | max|err| xpu 1.6958520834906494 cpu 0.19585208349064942 TARGET-PATH-PROOF bfloat16 logspace: out=xpu:0 dtype=torch.bfloat16 numel=38 OBSERVED bfloat16 logspace: vs float64-rounded reference xpu 21/38 cpu 0/38 | xpu vs cpu 21 | max|err| xpu 7.6047930354503706 cpu 1.6958520834906494 OBSERVED commit example linspace(0, 10, 38) half element 3: xpu 0.810546875 cpu 0.810546875 correctly-rounded 0.811035156 unwidened-step 0.810546875 ``` Two distinct observations: 1. **`logspace` is already wrong relative to CPU in the tested build.** CPU `logspace` computed its step and `pow` in double before this commit, so it is exact against the float64 reference (`0/38`). XPU disagrees with CPU on 26 of 38 half elements and 21 of 38 bfloat16 elements, and its maximum absolute error is an order of magnitude larger (`1.696` vs `0.196` in half; `7.605` vs `1.696` in bfloat16). This divergence does not depend on the upstream commit at all. 2. **`linspace` produces the unwidened-step value.** For the commit's own worked example, `linspace(0, 10, 38)` in half, element 3, XPU returns `0.810546875`, which is the unwidened-step value rather than the correctly rounded `0.811035156`. CPU in the tested build returns the same wrong value because the build predates the commit; at the frozen upstream head CPU returns the correctly rounded value, so XPU will diverge from CPU once the fix reaches an XPU build. `linspace(-3, 7, 129)` and bfloat16 `linspace(0, 10, 38)` were bit-identical to CPU, as expected: those ranges have steps that are exactly representable in the output dtype. Raw evidence: `runner/logs/commit-1614f7f277b640ca057b20aa452178eb1f31e898.log` (sha256 `f21a7d72489ec2ca21500fde3db72ec763eaf89bdf2210e161b386b7e3077a80`) from `scripts/repro_commit-1614f7f2.py` (sha256 `c224fe97212035e50f55f077e1be82b95b7e1f88488af37fccc1bb7d40ba9674`), returncode 0, 3.736 s, no timeout. ## Target-path evidence Every compared XPU tensor is reported on `xpu:0` with the expected dtype and `numel`, and the CPU and float64 references are computed separately on CPU, so the comparison is not XPU against itself. The XPU implementation is this repository's own kernel. In `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/RangeFactoriesKernel.cpp`, the non-integral dispatch of both kernels still declares the step in `scalar_t`: ```cpp // linspace_kernel, AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_AND_COMPLEX_TYPES_AND2(kHalf, kBFloat16, ...) scalar_t step = (scalar_end - scalar_start) / static_cast(steps - 1); // logspace_kernel, same dispatch scalar_t scalar_base = static_cast(base); scalar_t step = (scalar_end - scalar_start) / static_cast(steps - 1); ``` This is the pre-commit CUDA code, line for line. `LogspaceFunctor` does cast to `at::opmath_type` for the `sycl::pow` call, but its exponent `scalar_start_ + step_ * ind` is already accumulated in `scalar_t` before that cast, which is why `logspace` is the worse of the two. For contrast, `arange_kernel` and `range_kernel` in the same file already widen via `at::acc_type_device`, so the gap is specific to `linspace_kernel` and `logspace_kernel`. ## Why this is XPU-owned The upstream commit touches only the CPU and CUDA kernels. XPU has its own SYCL kernels in this repository, so nothing upstream can fix them. The change needed here is the direct analogue of the CUDA patch: introduce `using step_t = at::opmath_type` in the half/bfloat16 dispatch of `linspace_kernel` and `logspace_kernel`, compute the step (and `logspace`'s base) in `step_t`, and let `LinspaceFunctor`/`LogspaceFunctor` carry it through their existing `step_type` template parameter. The integral dispatches already use `float`/`double` and should not change; `opmath_type` leaves float, double and complex bit-identical, so only half and bfloat16 outputs move. Searched for prior art and found none: `intel/torch-xpu-ops` has no open or closed issue or PR covering the `linspace`/`logspace` step type (the merged #4331 "Align range factories with shared PyTorch helpers" did not change it, and the current `main` source above is unwidened), and `pytorch/pytorch` has no issue or PR claiming the XPU side of #198415. ## Reproducer
repro_linspace_logspace_step.py (exact bytes run, sha256 c224fe97212035e50f55f077e1be82b95b7e1f88488af37fccc1bb7d40ba9674) ```python import torch DTYPES = (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) print(f"ENV torch={torch.__version__} xpu_available={torch.xpu.is_available()}") print(f"ENV device={torch.xpu.get_device_name(0)}") CASES = ( ("linspace", lambda dt, dev: torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=dt, device=dev), lambda dev: torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)), ("linspace(-3,7,129)", lambda dt, dev: torch.linspace(-3, 7, 129, dtype=dt, device=dev), lambda dev: torch.linspace(-3, 7, 129, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)), ("logspace", lambda dt, dev: torch.logspace(0, 3, 38, dtype=dt, device=dev), lambda dev: torch.logspace(0, 3, 38, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)), ) for dtype in DTYPES: dname = str(dtype).replace("torch.", "") for label, make, make_ref in CASES: xpu = make(dtype, "xpu") cpu = make(dtype, "cpu") ref = make_ref("cpu") want = ref.to(dtype) xpu_c = xpu.cpu() print( f"{dname} {label}: out={xpu.device} " f"vs float64-rounded reference xpu {int((xpu_c != want).sum())}/{want.numel()} " f"cpu {int((cpu != want).sum())}/{want.numel()} | " f"xpu vs cpu {int((xpu_c != cpu).sum())} | " f"max|err| xpu {(xpu_c.double() - ref).abs().max().item()!r} " f"cpu {(cpu.double() - ref).abs().max().item()!r}" ) x = torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=torch.float16, device="xpu") cpu_x = torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=torch.float16) print( f"commit example linspace(0, 10, 38) half element 3: xpu {float(x[3])!r} " f"cpu {float(cpu_x[3])!r} correctly-rounded 0.811035156 unwidened-step 0.810546875" ) ``` The script as run also gates on `torch.xpu.is_available()` and prints a single machine-readable `RESULT:` line; the logic above is the part that produces the evidence.
## Environment ```text python 3.13.13 (/opt/conda/bin/python3.13) torch 2.15.0.dev20260923+xpu (/opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py) xpu available, Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics ``` The tested build is dated `2026-09-23` and therefore predates the `2026-09-24` upstream commit. That affects only the `linspace` comparison, where CPU in this build still shows the old unwidened value; the `logspace` divergence from CPU is fully observable in this build, and the XPU source above is unwidened at current `main` either way. ## Verification After the fix, half `logspace(0, 3, 38)` and bfloat16 `logspace(0, 3, 38)` on XPU should match CPU bit for bit, and half `linspace(0, 10, 38)[3]` on XPU should be `0.811035156`. `torch.float32`, `torch.float64` and complex outputs must stay bit-identical.

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-25] XPU layer_norm returns non-zero on a constant input: vectorized WelfordCombine averages partial means instead of using Welford's increment
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-198581 -->
## Summary

`F.layer_norm` on an exactly constant input returns a non-zero result on XPU. A constant input has exactly zero variance, so every output element must be exactly zero, and CPU eager does return exactly zero on the same values.

Observed on `Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`, torch `2.15.0.dev20260925+xpu`, with `eps=1e-5` on `torch.ones(4, width)`:

| dtype | width | XPU max abs | saved mean exactly 1 | CPU max abs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| float32 | 220 | 5.654593e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| float32 | 244 | 3.769729e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| float16 | 220 | 5.656481e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| float16 | 244 | 3.767014e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| bfloat16 | 220 | 5.650520e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| bfloat16 | 244 | 3.767014e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |

21 of the 27 (dtype, width) pairs tested were exactly zero; widths 48, 96, 164, 188, 192, 384 and 768 were clean on this device. The saved mean is the culprit: `rstd` behaviour is not implicated, and with `eps=1e-5` the factor `rsqrt(1e-5) = 316.23` amplifies a one-ulp mean error into the values above.

## Upstream source

- `pytorch/pytorch#198581` (OPEN, labels `module: correctness (silent)` and `module: norms and normalization`) reports the same defect for `cuWelfordCombine` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/layer_norm_kernel.cu`, measured on gfx950 and gfx942.
- `pytorch/pytorch#198587` proposed the CUDA-side fix but is CLOSED and UNMERGED (no merge timestamp, no merge commit). It was closed by its own author on 2026-09-26T01:42:13Z alongside an unsigned-CLA notice, with green CI and no maintainer review, so the close is not an upstream rejection of the premise.
- That PR touches only `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/layer_norm_kernel.cu` and `test/test_nn.py`, and its own text states that XPU inherits the new bitwise-exactness expectation which the patch neither changes nor verifies. No issue or PR in `pytorch/pytorch` owns the XPU half of the work, and no `intel/torch-xpu-ops` tracker covers it.
- Alignment scan window: `[2026-09-25T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-26T00:00:00Z)`.

## Root cause on XPU

`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp:370-393`, `WelfordCombine`:

```cpp
U delta = dataB.mean - dataA.mean;             // line 376
U count = dataA.count + dataB.count;
if (count > decltype(dataB.count){0}) {
  auto coef = sycl::native::recip(count);       // line 380
  auto nA = dataA.count * coef;
  auto nB = dataB.count * coef;
  mean = nA * dataA.mean + nB * dataB.mean;     // line 383
  sigma2 = dataA.sigma2 + dataB.sigma2 + delta * delta * dataA.count * nB;
}
```

Line 383 combines two partial means as a weighted average rather than as Welford's increment. It is exact only when `nA + nB == 1` exactly, which no reciprocal guarantees, correctly rounded or not. The canonical in-tree combine, `WelfordOps::combine` in `aten/src/ATen/native/SharedReduceOps.h`, instead uses `a.mean + delta * nb_over_n`, which cannot move the mean when both partials agree.

The observed failure set points at the formula rather than at `sycl::native::recip` accuracy: widths 220 and 244 are both in the set upstream measured as failing even with a correctly rounded reciprocal (smallest 164, 188, 220, 244), while the `3 * 2^k` widths that dominate the ROCm reports (48, 96, 192, 384, 768) are clean on this device.

## Target-path evidence

- `layer_norm_kernel_impl` (`LayerNormKernels.cpp:686-690`) selects `launch_vectorized_layer_norm_kernel` for float / half / bfloat16 when `N % 4 == 0`, `N <= 2^24`, and the buffers are 16-byte aligned. Every width in the table is a multiple of 4, so the vectorized kernel ran; its `compute_stats` calls `WelfordCombine` at lines 425 (intra-subgroup shuffle) and 450 (inter-subgroup merge).
- The `N % 4 != 0` fallback, `launch_rowwise_moments_kernel`, builds its reduction from `WelfordOps<...>` (`LayerNormKernels.cpp:207`), i.e. the mean-preserving combine. The divergence is therefore confined to the vectorized arm, matching upstream's account of why non-multiple-of-4 widths are clean.
- The reproducer asserts that the output device type is xpu and reads the saved mean through `torch.native_layer_norm`, whose mean is `T_ACC` (float32) for all three input dtypes. It is inexact in all six failing rows.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
    for width in (220, 244, 384):
        x = torch.ones(4, width, dtype=dtype, device='xpu')
        out = F.layer_norm(x, (width,), eps=1e-5)
        _, mean, _ = torch.native_layer_norm(x, (width,), None, None, 1e-5)
        cpu = F.layer_norm(x.cpu(), (width,), eps=1e-5)
        print(
            dtype,
            width,
            'xpu_max_abs=%.6e' % out.abs().max().item(),
            'saved_mean_exact=%s' % bool((mean == 1).all().item()),
            'cpu_max_abs=%.6e' % cpu.abs().max().item(),
        )
```

Expected at every width: `xpu_max_abs=0.000000e+00` and `saved_mean_exact=True`. Observed: widths 220 and 244 are non-zero with an inexact saved mean in all three dtypes, while CPU is exactly zero; width 384 is a control that passes on this device.

## Suggested direction

Bring `WelfordCombine` into agreement with `WelfordOps::combine`, keeping `sigma2` as is since it already uses `nB` and is Chan's `M2` term, independent of how the mean is formed:

```cpp
auto nB = dataB.count * coef;
mean = (dataA.count == U(0)) ? dataB.mean : dataA.mean + delta * nB;
sigma2 = dataA.sigma2 + dataB.sigma2 + delta * delta * dataA.count * nB;
```

`delta` is already `dataB.mean - dataA.mean` at line 376, so the increment is based on `dataA`. The select covers the idle-lane merge where `dataA.count == 0` and the weighted form would otherwise rescale `dataB.mean`; the mirrored case needs no guard because `nB` is then exactly zero. On a constant input `delta` is exactly zero, so the mean cannot move however accurate `coef` is. This does change bitwise forward output for non-constant input, as the equivalent upstream change does.

`WelfordOnlineSum` (line 360) also uses `sycl::native::recip`, but it is not implicated for a constant input: `delta` is exactly zero from the second element onward, and the first element divides by a count of exactly 1.

## Evidence limitations

Stated so they are not mistaken for oversights:

- The reproducer's control, a plain `x.mean(dim=-1)` on the same tensor, was itself inexact for float32 at widths 220 and 244, so it does not isolate `layer_norm` for that dtype. For float16 and bfloat16 the control passed, but its result is rounded to the low-precision output dtype while the saved mean is float32, so it is a weak control either way. The CPU-versus-XPU `layer_norm` oracle is unaffected - CPU returned exactly zero in all six failing rows - and neither is the source divergence above. Whether XPU's generic mean reduction is also inexact at these widths is a separate question this scan does not settle.
- Only multiples of 4 were exercised, so the `N % 4 != 0` fallback is clean by source reading rather than by measurement.
- Backward was not exercised on XPU. Upstream reports that `native_layer_norm_backward` consumes the saved `mean` and `rstd` and contains no Welford reduction, so it should inherit the forward fix, but that was not verified here.

## Environment

```
python : /opt/conda/bin/python3.13 (3.13.13)
torch  : 2.15.0.dev20260925+xpu (/opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py)
device : Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership

The affected kernel is `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp` in this repository, so the change belongs to `intel/torch-xpu-ops`. It does not depend on `pytorch/pytorch#198587` landing: the weighted-average combine is present in the XPU source independently of that PR, and the defect reproduces in the tested build.

---

Filed by the xpu-alignment automation scan for the window `[2026-09-25T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-26T00:00:00Z)`.

The N % 4 != 0 fallback, launch_rowwise_moments_kernel, builds its reduction from WelfordOps<...> (LayerNormKernels.cpp:207), i.e. the mean-preserving combine. The divergence is therefore confined to the vectorized arm, matching upstream's account of why non-multiple-of-4 widths are clean.
The reproducer asserts that the output device type is xpu and reads the saved mean through torch.native_layer_norm, whose mean is T_ACC (float32) for all three input dtypes. It is inexact in all six failing rows.

Reproducer
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
    for width in (220, 244, 384):
        x = torch.ones(4, width, dtype=dtype, device='xpu')
        out = F.layer_norm(x, (width,), eps=1e-5)
        _, mean, _ = torch.native_layer_norm(x, (width,), None, None, 1e-5)
        cpu = F.layer_norm(x.cpu(), (width,), eps=1e-5)
        print(
            dtype,
            width,
            'xpu_max_abs=%.6e' % out.abs().max().item(),
            'saved_mean_exact=%s' % bool((mean == 1).all().item()),
            'cpu_max_abs=%.6e' % cpu.abs().max().item(),
        )
Expected at every width: xpu_max_abs=0.000000e+00 and saved_mean_exact=True. Observed: widths 220 and 244 are non-zero with an inexact saved mean in all three dtypes, while CPU is exactly zero; width 384 is a control that passes on this device.
Suggested direction
Bring WelfordCombine into agreement with WelfordOps::combine, keeping sigma2 as is since it already uses nB and is Chan's M2 term, independent of how the mean is formed:
auto nB = dataB.count * coef;
mean = (dataA.count == U(0)) ? dataB.mean : dataA.mean + delta * nB;
sigma2 = dataA.sigma2 + dataB.sigma2 + delta * delta * dataA.count * nB;
delta is already dataB.mean - dataA.mean at line 376, so the increment is based on dataA. The select covers the idle-lane merge where dataA.count == 0 and the weighted form would otherwise rescale dataB.mean; the mirrored case needs no guard because nB is then exactly zero. On a constant input delta is exactly zero, so the mean cannot move however accurate coef is. This does change bitwise forward output for non-constant input, as the equivalent upstream change does.
WelfordOnlineSum (line 360) also uses sycl::native::recip, but it is not implicated for a constant input: delta is exactly zero from the second element onward, and the first element divides by a count of exactly 1.
Evidence limitations
Stated so they are not mistaken for oversights:

The reproducer's control, a plain x.mean(dim=-1) on the same tensor, was itself inexact for float32 at widths 220 and 244, so it does not isolate layer_norm for that dtype. For float16 and bfloat16 the control passed, but its result is rounded to the low-precision output dtype while the saved mean is float32, so it is a weak control either way. The CPU-versus-XPU layer_norm oracle is unaffected - CPU returned exactly zero in all six failing rows - and neither is the source divergence above. Whether XPU's generic mean reduction is also inexact at these widths is a separate question this scan does not settle.
Only multiples of 4 were exercised, so the N % 4 != 0 fallback is clean by source reading rather than by measurement.
Backward was not exercised on XPU. Upstream reports that native_layer_norm_backward consumes the saved mean and rstd and contains no Welford reduction, so it should inherit the forward fix, but that was not verified here.

Environment
python : /opt/conda/bin/python3.13 (3.13.13)
torch  : 2.15.0.dev20260925+xpu (/opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py)
device : Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics

Ownership
The affected kernel is src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp in this repository, so the change belongs to intel/torch-xpu-ops. It does not depend on pytorch/pytorch#198587 landing: the weighted-average combine is present in the XPU source independently of that PR, and the defect reproduces in the tested build.

Filed by the xpu-alignment automation scan for the window [2026-09-25T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-26T00:00:00Z).

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-27] XPU addcmul/addcdiv dispatch on the out= dtype, so a wider out= widens the computation and diverges from CPU and CUDA
issues.body:
## Upstream source - Origin: `pytorch/pytorch@ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e` (PR #196924), `[MPS] Migrate addc[mul|div] to Metal`, a default-branch commit inside the scan window. ghstack chain #196924 -> #198743 -> #198753 (the last landed as `4b0647ed`). - Scan window: `[2026-09-27T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-28T00:00:00Z)` on `pytorch/pytorch`, frozen default-branch head `2e9b4aff8d49b22bbebf288ccbf63983c51e45f0`. The commit is reachable from that head. - Upstream defect, quoted from the commit message: the Metal `_cast_` ternary kernels `were instantiated for the output dtype, so an out= wider than the common dtype widened the computation as well. They now compute at the iterator's common dtype and cast on store, like CPU.` The commit notes this is the same cast error that was already fixed for `lerp` and `clamp`. CPU and CUDA were already correct; the commit fixed MPS. XPU has its own ternary kernels in this repository and still has the defect. ## Observed XPU behavior `torch.addcmul` and `torch.addcdiv` with `float16` inputs and a `float32` `out=`, on inputs whose intermediate overflows in half but not in float32: ```text TARGET: addcmul.out inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 CHECK addcmul-wide-out: cpu=['inf', '17.0'] xpu=['240001.0', '17.0'] CHECK addcmul-wide-out: FAIL (xpu widened the computation) TARGET: addcdiv.out inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 CHECK addcdiv-wide-out: cpu=['inf', '2.75'] xpu=['120001.0', '2.75'] CHECK addcdiv-wide-out: FAIL (xpu widened the computation) TARGET: addcmul value=0 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float32 CHECK addcmul-value-zero: cpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] xpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] CHECK addcmul-value-zero: PASS TARGET: addcdiv value=0 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float32 CHECK addcdiv-value-zero: cpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] xpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] CHECK addcdiv-value-zero: PASS RESULT: CONFIRMED failed=addcmul-wide-out,addcdiv-wide-out ``` `1 + 60000 * 4` and `1 + 60000 / 0.5` overflow `float16`, so the reference result is `inf`: the TensorIterator common dtype for this call is `float16`, because `compute_common_dtype` skips output operands, and the established semantics are to compute at the common dtype and cast on store. CPU returns `inf`; XPU returns the `float32` values `240001.0` and `120001.0`. XPU therefore returns a silently different number than CPU and CUDA for the same supported call, in both directions of the family (`addcmul.out` and `addcdiv.out`). The second oracle carried by the same chain (#198753: with `value=0`, NaN/Inf in `tensor1` must still propagate) passed on XPU for both ops, so this report is scoped to the `out=` dtype only. Raw evidence: `runner/logs/commit-ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e.log` (sha256 `0a4c4502cb14520ce4971caed4c85553a628767c4f56fbf1ba5a7ac29b7cdbac`) produced from `scripts/repro_commit-ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e.py` (sha256 `5d40eb5cec83fa4831d5b4c14ec412dbac29c917b6a3186b191c3e3ed7ee34b0`); returncode 0, 3.736 s, no timeout. ## Target-path evidence Every compared XPU tensor is reported on `xpu:0` with its dtype, and the CPU reference is built separately on CPU from the same initialized values, so the comparison is not XPU against itself. The printed `inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32` pair is exactly the mixed-dtype `aten::addcmul.out` / `aten::addcdiv.out` call that reaches `at::native::xpu::addcmul_kernel` / `addcdiv_kernel`. `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/PointwiseOpsKernels.cpp` computes the common dtype but then dispatches the real branches on the output dtype: ```cpp void addcmul_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) { // ... auto dtype = iter.common_dtype(); if (iter.is_cpu_scalar(3)) { if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { // dtype: correct AT_DISPATCH_COMPLEX_TYPES(dtype, "addcmul_xpu", ... } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2( at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16, iter.dtype(), // output dtype "addcmul_xpu", ... } } else if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { // dtype: correct // ... } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND_COMPLEX_AND2( at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16, iter.dtype(), // output dtype "addcmul_xpu", ... } } void addcdiv_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) { auto dtype = iter.common_dtype(); if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { /* dtype: correct */ } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2( at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16, iter.dtype(), // output dtype "addcdiv_xpu", ... } } ``` `iter.dtype()` is `iter.dtype(0)`, the output operand's current dtype. In `aten/src/ATen/TensorIterator.cpp` at the frozen head, `compute_types` only replaces a mismatched output with a common-dtype temporary when `common_device == kCPU`; on a device iterator the output operand keeps `float32`. So on this call `iter.dtype()` is `float32` while `iter.common_dtype()` is `float16`: `scalar_t` and therefore `at::acc_type_device` are instantiated at `float32`, the functor argument types no longer match the half inputs, and `gpu_kernel_impl` takes its dynamic-casting path (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Loops.h:559`) which converts each half input up on load. The arithmetic runs in `float32` instead of at the iterator's common dtype, which is exactly the observed output. CUDA at the same frozen head dispatches both kernels on the common dtype: ```cpp // aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/PointwiseOpsKernel.cu void addcdiv_cuda_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) { auto dtype = iter.common_dtype(); if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { /* ... */ } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2(kHalf, kBFloat16, dtype, "addcdiv_cuda", [&]() { ``` `addcmul_cuda_kernel` is the same, including its CPU-scalar `tensor2` branch. ## Why this is XPU-owned The kernels are in this repository. The upstream commit changed only the MPS Metal kernels, and CPU and CUDA already dispatch on the common dtype, so nothing upstream can correct the XPU dispatch. The fix is to pass the already-computed `dtype` (that is, `iter.common_dtype()`) instead of `iter.dtype()` in the three non-complex `AT_DISPATCH` calls above: both branches of `addcmul_kernel` and the non-complex branch of `addcdiv_kernel`. The complex branches already use `dtype`. Note that no OpInfo sample can cover this, because a `SampleInput` cannot express an `out=` dtype that differs from the inputs (observed upstream in #198795), so a targeted test is needed rather than a new sample. Prior art was searched and none covers this work. In `intel/torch-xpu-ops`: #3275 changed `addcmul` to `sycl::fma` for FMA parity, #3608 fixed the CPU-scalar `tensor2` error, and #5523 is the same class of defect (computing in the output dtype) but in `linspace_kernel`/`logspace_kernel`; no open or closed issue or PR covers the addc{mul,div} `out=` dtype. In `pytorch/pytorch` there is no issue or PR claiming an XPU side of #196924. ## Reproducer

return [repr(v) for v in t.tolist()] def eq_with_nan(a, b): return bool(((a == b) | (a.isnan() & b.isnan())).all()) def check_wide_out(op, name, self_v, t1_v, t2_v, value, failures): self_h = issues.bodyText:
Upstream source

Origin: pytorch/pytorch@ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e (PR #196924), [MPS] Migrate addc[mul|div] to Metal, a default-branch commit inside the scan window. ghstack chain #196924 -> #198743 -> #198753 (the last landed as 4b0647ed).
Scan window: [2026-09-27T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-28T00:00:00Z) on pytorch/pytorch, frozen default-branch head 2e9b4aff8d49b22bbebf288ccbf63983c51e45f0. The commit is reachable from that head.
Upstream defect, quoted from the commit message: the Metal _cast_ ternary kernels were instantiated for the output dtype, so an out= wider than the common dtype widened the computation as well. They now compute at the iterator's common dtype and cast on store, like CPU. The commit notes this is the same cast error that was already fixed for lerp and clamp.

CPU and CUDA were already correct; the commit fixed MPS. XPU has its own ternary kernels in this repository and still has the defect.
Observed XPU behavior
torch.addcmul and torch.addcdiv with float16 inputs and a float32 out=, on inputs whose intermediate overflows in half but not in float32:
TARGET: addcmul.out inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0
CHECK addcmul-wide-out: cpu=['inf', '17.0'] xpu=['240001.0', '17.0']
CHECK addcmul-wide-out: FAIL (xpu widened the computation)
TARGET: addcdiv.out inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0
CHECK addcdiv-wide-out: cpu=['inf', '2.75'] xpu=['120001.0', '2.75']
CHECK addcdiv-wide-out: FAIL (xpu widened the computation)
TARGET: addcmul value=0 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float32
CHECK addcmul-value-zero: cpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] xpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan']
CHECK addcmul-value-zero: PASS
TARGET: addcdiv value=0 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float32
CHECK addcdiv-value-zero: cpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] xpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan']
CHECK addcdiv-value-zero: PASS
RESULT: CONFIRMED failed=addcmul-wide-out,addcdiv-wide-out

1 + 60000 * 4 and 1 + 60000 / 0.5 overflow float16, so the reference result is inf: the TensorIterator common dtype for this call is float16, because compute_common_dtype skips output operands, and the established semantics are to compute at the common dtype and cast on store. CPU returns inf; XPU returns the float32 values 240001.0 and 120001.0. XPU therefore returns a silently different number than CPU and CUDA for the same supported call, in both directions of the family (addcmul.out and addcdiv.out).
The second oracle carried by the same chain (#198753: with value=0, NaN/Inf in tensor1 must still propagate) passed on XPU for both ops, so this report is scoped to the out= dtype only.
Raw evidence: runner/logs/commit-ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e.log (sha256 0a4c4502cb14520ce4971caed4c85553a628767c4f56fbf1ba5a7ac29b7cdbac) produced from scripts/repro_commit-ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e.py (sha256 5d40eb5cec83fa4831d5b4c14ec412dbac29c917b6a3186b191c3e3ed7ee34b0); returncode 0, 3.736 s, no timeout.
Target-path evidence
Every compared XPU tensor is reported on xpu:0 with its dtype, and the CPU reference is built separately on CPU from the same initialized values, so the comparison is not XPU against itself. The printed inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32 pair is exactly the mixed-dtype aten::addcmul.out / aten::addcdiv.out call that reaches at::native::xpu::addcmul_kernel / addcdiv_kernel.
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/PointwiseOpsKernels.cpp computes the common dtype but then dispatches the real branches on the output dtype:
void addcmul_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) {
  // ...
  auto dtype = iter.common_dtype();
  if (iter.is_cpu_scalar(3)) {
    if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) {            // dtype: correct
      AT_DISPATCH_COMPLEX_TYPES(dtype, "addcmul_xpu", ...
    } else {
      AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2(
          at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16,
          iter.dtype(),                        // output dtype
          "addcmul_xpu", ...
    }
  } else if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) {       // dtype: correct
    // ...
  } else {
    AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND_COMPLEX_AND2(
        at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16,
        iter.dtype(),                          // output dtype
        "addcmul_xpu", ...
  }
}

void addcdiv_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) {
  auto dtype = iter.common_dtype();
  if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { /* dtype: correct */ }
  else {
    AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2(
        at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16,
        iter.dtype(),                          // output dtype
        "addcdiv_xpu", ...
  }
}
iter.dtype() is iter.dtype(0), the output operand's current dtype. In aten/src/ATen/TensorIterator.cpp at the frozen head, compute_types only replaces a mismatched output with a common-dtype temporary when common_device == kCPU; on a device iterator the output operand keeps float32. So on this call iter.dtype() is float32 while iter.common_dtype() is float16: scalar_t and therefore at::acc_type_device<scalar_t, kXPU> are instantiated at float32, the functor argument types no longer match the half inputs, and gpu_kernel_impl takes its dynamic-casting path (src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Loops.h:559) which converts each half input up on load. The arithmetic runs in float32 instead of at the iterator's common dtype, which is exactly the observed output.
CUDA at the same frozen head dispatches both kernels on the common dtype:
// aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/PointwiseOpsKernel.cu
void addcdiv_cuda_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) {
  auto dtype = iter.common_dtype();
  if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { /* ... */ } else {
    AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2(kHalf, kBFloat16, dtype, "addcdiv_cuda", [&]() {
addcmul_cuda_kernel is the same, including its CPU-scalar tensor2 branch.
Why this is XPU-owned
The kernels are in this repository. The upstream commit changed only the MPS Metal kernels, and CPU and CUDA already dispatch on the common dtype, so nothing upstream can correct the XPU dispatch.
The fix is to pass the already-computed dtype (that is, iter.common_dtype()) instead of iter.dtype() in the three non-complex AT_DISPATCH calls above: both branches of addcmul_kernel and the non-complex branch of addcdiv_kernel. The complex branches already use dtype. Note that no OpInfo sample can cover this, because a SampleInput cannot express an out= dtype that differs from the inputs (observed upstream in #198795), so a targeted test is needed rather than a new sample.
Prior art was searched and none covers this work. In intel/torch-xpu-ops: #3275 changed addcmul to sycl::fma for FMA parity, #3608 fixed the CPU-scalar tensor2 error, and #5523 is the same class of defect (computing in the output dtype) but in linspace_kernel/logspace_kernel; no open or closed issue or PR covers the addc{mul,div} out= dtype. In pytorch/pytorch there is no issue or PR claiming an XPU side of #196924.
Reproducer

import traceback

import torch


def fmt(t):
    return [repr(v) for v in t.tolist()]


def eq_with_nan(a, b):
    return bool(((a == b) | (a.isnan() & b.isnan())).all())


def check_wide_out(op, name, self_v, t1_v, t2_v, value, failures):
    self_h = torch.tensor(self_v, dtype=torch.half)
    t1_h = torch.tensor(t1_v, dtype=torch.half)
    t2_h = torch.tensor(t2_v, dtype=torch.half)

    cpu_out = torch.empty(len(self_v), dtype=torch.float32)
    op(self_h, t1_h, t2_h, value=value, out=cpu_out)

    xs = self_h.to("xpu")
    x1 = t1_h.to("xpu")
    x2 = t2_h.to("xpu")
    xpu_out = torch.empty(len(self_v), dtype=torch.float32, device="xpu")
    op(xs, x1, x2, value=value, out=xpu_out)
    torch.xpu.synchronize()
    got = xpu_out.cpu()

    print(
        "TARGET: %s.out inputs=%s out=%s in_device=%s out_device=%s"
        % (name, xs.dtype, xpu_out.dtype, xs.device, xpu_out.device)
    )
    print("CHECK %s-wide-out: cpu=%s xpu=%s" % (name, fmt(cpu_out), fmt(got)))
    if eq_with_nan(got, cpu_out):
        print("CHECK %s-wide-out: PASS" % name)
    else:
        print("CHECK %s-wide-out: FAIL (xpu widened the computation)" % name)
        failures.append("%s-wide-out" % name)


def check_value_zero(op, name, failures):
    self_c = torch.tensor([1.0, 1.0, 1.0], dtype=torch.float32)
    t1_c = torch.tensor([float("nan"), float("inf"), float("-inf")], dtype=torch.float32)
    t2_c = torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.float32)

    exp = op(self_c, t1_c, t2_c, value=0)

    xs = self_c.to("xpu")
    x1 = t1_c.to("xpu")
    x2 = t2_c.to("xpu")
    got_x = op(xs, x1, x2, value=0)
    torch.xpu.synchronize()
    got = got_x.cpu()

    print(
        "TARGET: %s value=0 in_device=%s out_device=%s dtype=%s"
        % (name, xs.device, got_x.device, got_x.dtype)
    )
    print("CHECK %s-value-zero: cpu=%s xpu=%s" % (name, fmt(exp), fmt(got)))
    if eq_with_nan(got, exp):
        print("CHECK %s-value-zero: PASS" % name)
    else:
        print("CHECK %s-value-zero: FAIL (non-finite tensor1 not propagated)" % name)
        failures.append("%s-value-zero" % name)


def main():
    print("INFO: torch", torch.__version__)
    if not torch.xpu.is_available():
        print("RESULT: BLOCKED_ENV torch.xpu.is_available() is False")
        return
    print("INFO: xpu device", torch.xpu.get_device_name(0))

    failures = []
    # half intermediates below overflow in half but not in float32:
    #   addcmul: 1 * 60000 * 4 -> inf in half, 240000 in float32
    #   addcdiv: 1 * 60000 / 0.5 -> inf in half, 120000 in float32
    check_wide_out(
        torch.addcmul, "addcmul", [1.0, 2.0], [60000.0, 3.0], [4.0, 5.0], 1.0, failures
    )
    check_wide_out(
        torch.addcdiv, "addcdiv", [1.0, 2.0], [60000.0, 3.0], [0.5, 4.0], 1.0, failures
    )
    check_value_zero(torch.addcmul, "addcmul", failures)
    check_value_zero(torch.addcdiv, "addcdiv", failures)

    if failures:
        print("RESULT: CONFIRMED failed=%s" % ",".join(failures))
    else:
        print("RESULT: NOT_REPRODUCED all oracles held on xpu")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception:
        traceback.print_exc()
        print("RESULT: BLOCKED_SCRIPT_ERROR unexpected exception outside the oracle")

xpu      available, Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics

issues.title: [XPU] test_reference_numerics_extremal_acos_xpu_complex64 fails with nan mismatch
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`test_reference_numerics_extremal_acos_xpu_complex64` in `test/test_unary_ufuncs.py`
fails consistently on XPU with a `nan` mismatch against the reference.

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!

Mismatched elements: 18 / 81 (22.2%)
Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0,) (up to 0.01 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: nan at index (0,) (up to 1.3e-06 allowed)
```

This is a `nan`-handling discrepancy for complex `acos` at extremal input values.

### To Reproduce

```
python test/test_unary_ufuncs.py TestUnaryUfuncsXPU.test_reference_numerics_extremal_acos_xpu_complex64
```

### Environment

- Test job: `linux-noble-xpu-n-py3.10 / test (default, 10, 12, linux.idc.xpu)`
- Seen while enabling `TestUnaryUfuncs` on XPU in pytorch/pytorch PR #197782

### Additional context

Related `test_reference_numerics_extremal` failures for other transcendental complex
ops (`atanh`, `sin`, `tan`, `tanhshrink`, `sqrt`) are already skipped in the XPU skip
lists, but `acos` is not currently tracked. May be related to RFC #3266 (migrating XPU
kernel math functions from `std::`/`::` to `sycl::`/`sycl::native::`).

nodes.bodyText:
Root cause found: it's a compiler bug in SYCL libdevice, not a NaN-handling problem in our kernel. Filed as CMPLRLLVM-78570.
The two failing inputs are inf+infj and inf-infj, each repeated 9 times, which gives the 18/81. XPU returns 0x3f490fda for the real part of acos(inf+infj) instead of 0x3f490fdb (pi/4), which is 1 ulp low. The imaginary part is ±inf on both sides, so |actual - expected| is inf - inf = nan, and a 1 ulp error becomes a mismatch. That's the "nan at index (0,)" in the message.
import torch
t = torch.tensor([complex(float("inf"), float("inf"))], dtype=torch.complex64)
print(torch.acos(t.xpu()).item(), torch.acos(t).item())
# (0.7853981256484985-infj) (0.7853981852531433-infj)
Our kernel calls std::acos(c10::complex<float>), which ends up in libdevice's __devicelib_cacosf. That function computes pi as atan2(+0.0f, -0.0f) in float, and on Intel GPUs this returns pi rounded down (0x40490fda). libc++, which libdevice ported this code from, does that atan2 in double and so gets a correctly rounded pi. Every pi-derived special value inherits the error; for example, acos(0j).real is also 1 ulp low. complex128 is exact.
The same root cause covers more than acos:

test_reference_numerics_extremal complex64 fails on XPU this way for acos, asin, acosh, asinh and their _refs variants. The acosh/asin/asinh ones are currently tracked under #5552.
atan and atanh are also 1 ulp off, but they pass because both components of the result are finite.
Switching to sycl:: math (RFC #3266) won't help, because the sycl_ext_oneapi_complex header computes pi the same way.

Plan: no torch-xpu-ops code change. We keep the XPU skip from pytorch/pytorch#197782 and remove it once PyTorch's XPU build moves to a compiler with the fix. libdevice is compiled into libtorch_xpu.so, so a driver update alone won't fix it.
Reproduced on Max 1550 with oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1.1 and IGC 2.11.43.

issues.title: grid_sample: implement mode='bicubic' with 5-D input on XPU
issues.body:
## Summary

`torch.nn.functional.grid_sample` gained support for `mode='bicubic'` with
5-D input on CPU and CUDA in `pytorch/pytorch#194787` (upstream commit
`20fb7bd04e`). XPU does not implement it: `grid_sampler_3d_kernel` and
`grid_sampler_3d_backward_kernel` in
`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/GridSampler.cpp` call the mode-taking overload
`check_grid_sampler_3d(input, grid, interpolation_mode)`
(`aten/src/ATen/native/GridSamplerUtils.h:88`), which raises

```
NotImplementedError: grid_sampler(): bicubic interpolation with 5D input
                     is not implemented for xpu
```

Upstream kept that overload solely for torch-xpu-ops, with a TODO to drop
it once XPU implements the mode
(`aten/src/ATen/native/GridSamplerUtils.h:83-86`).

## Why this is filed

The same upstream PR made `sample_inputs_grid_sample` yield `bicubic` for
5-D input on every backend, so every OpInfo-driven suite now hits the
unimplemented mode on XPU. Upstream marked the affected tests
`unittest.expectedFailure` for `device_type="xpu"` in the
`nn.functional.grid_sample` OpInfo `skips` tuple
(`torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py`), each with a
`TODO: drop these when mps / xpu implement 5-D bicubic`.

One suite was missed: `test/test_overrides.py`
`TestTorchFunctionRedispatchOpsDeviceXPU::test_redispatch_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_*`,
which was consequently auto-disabled upstream as
`pytorch/pytorch#197521`, `pytorch/pytorch#197522`,
`pytorch/pytorch#197523` and `pytorch/pytorch#197524`. That gap is being
closed by adding the matching `xfail` entry; this issue tracks the real
work.

## What is needed

Port the CUDA implementation from `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/GridSampler.cu`
and `GridSampler.cuh` to SYCL in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/GridSampler.cpp`:

- `resolve_cubic_taps` / `compute_coordinates_sized` /
  `grid_sampler_unnormalize*_sized` helpers (`GridSampler.cuh:321-408`)
- a dedicated 5-D bicubic forward kernel (CUDA keeps it separate from
  `grid_sampler_3d_kernel` for register pressure reasons)
- the matching 5-D bicubic backward kernel
- switch both XPU 5-D entry points from
  `check_grid_sampler_3d(input, grid, interpolation_mode)` to the
  rank-only `check_grid_sampler_3d(input, grid)`

The double backward lives in device-agnostic
`torch/csrc/autograd/FunctionsManual.cpp` and already handles bicubic, so
it needs no XPU work.

## Coordination note

The upstream `expectedFailure` entries are strict: once XPU implements the
mode they turn into "unexpected success" failures. A torch-xpu-ops PR
implementing this must land together with a `pytorch/pytorch` PR that
removes those entries and the `test/test_overrides.py` one.

issues.body:
`@torchxpubot fix` runs an autonomous agent on an XPU host for up to five hours,
so it answers to a named list rather than to every intel org member. The
standing list is `SEED` in `.github/scripts/bot_fix_access.js`.

To ask for access, comment here with what you mean to work on. An approver
replies on this issue:

```
@torchxpubot allow @your-login
```

That takes effect on your next `@torchxpubot fix` -- no PR, no workflow edit.
Revoking works the same way with `@torchxpubot deny @your-login`, and the last
comment naming a login wins, so this issue's history is the record of who has
access and why.

Approvers: `chuanqi129` `EikanWang` `gujinghui` `riverliuintel` `tye1`

Grants are read from this issue and nowhere else.
